/Saturday April 23rd, 2011 /

Vicky hated when her mom was right.

Unfortunately, she was both a fairly successful lawyer and experienced
parahuman, so she was often right about things that were relevant to
Vicky’s interests.  It was even more frustrating when she was wrong,
because more than twenty years of experience as a cape wasn’t the same
as actual experts who studied parahumans.  The plural of anecdote wasn’t
data, after all.

Her mom had yelled a lot the first time Vicky tried that one.

Still, single data point or no, Vicky was still rattled by the fact that
the Butcher really did have an unhealthy fixation on her sister.  Except
it wasn’t just fixation, it was… friendship?   Was it even possible to
be friends with the Butcher? 

The answer, apparently, was yes.  Now that Vicky had cooled down from
the argument with her sister and the Teeth — they had to be separate in
her head — she could admit that Amy really had made friends among the
gang.  Vicky considered herself an expert in spotting people faking
friendship for benefits, and it was clear to her that there was real
camaraderie between those girls.

Admitting that was not pleasant for Vicky, as it confirmed something for
her that she had long suspected: Amy was unhappy with her life.  Their
mother was… difficult, her healing duties were long, and —now that Vicky
was really thinking about it— Amy didn’t have much in the way of friends
beyond Vicky herself.  But why had Amy made friends with supervillains?

Vicky considered that as she flew through the fading twilight, no real
destination in mind.  Flying was probably her favorite power and pastime
both, and she would often retreat into the sky to clear her head.  She
had considered landing to call her mom or aunt several times, only to
realize that she had no idea how to start a conversation about her
sister sororitizing with the enemy.

Worse, Vicky didn’t know what to make of those enemies, either.  Lisa
revealing herself to be a Thinker seemed to support the PRT’s assessment
that she wasn’t very good at being a cape, but maybe that was just what
she wanted Vicky to think.  Or not.  It seemed too absurd that Lisa
would unmask herself to save another cape’s family, Butcher or no, but
now that Vicky had seen them all just lounging together and eating popcorn…

Yeah, she had to do something.

Dropping down onto an abandoned building in the middle of the Docks,
Vicky pulled out her cell phone and punched in a number she was not in
the habit of calling.  It had barely rung once when a clipped voice
answered, “Armsmaster speaking.  How can I help you, Miss Dallon?”

“Sorry to call you out of the blue, I know you’re busy and all, but I,
uh, need some help.”

There was a faint sound of machinery on the other end.  “I assume you do
not mean immediately, having called my non-emergency line.”

“No, I’m fine.  But I just got back from dropping my sister off at a
sleepover with four other girls, and I’m pretty sure that they’re all
supervillains.”

Armsmaster was silent for a long minute.  “And how do you know this?”

“Uh, one of them was Wea—”

“Stop,” Armsmaster commanded, and Vicky’s mouth clicked shut at the
sheer authority in his voice.  “Do you currently fear for your sister’s
life or well-being?  Yes or no only, please.”

It hurt Vicky to be honest.  “No.”

“Do you know the names or faces of the civilian identities of Teeth capes?”

“Yes.”

Armsmaster sighed loudly.  “Did Weaver reveal herself to you?”

“By accident.”  Vicky was still amazed that the supervillain had just
owned it instead of even trying to deflect, but that matched the
Butcher’s usual audacity.  “Can you do anything to help my sister?”

If not for the faint mechanical noises on the other side of the line,
Vicky might have hung up in the silence that followed her response. 
“Miss Dallon, while I appreciate that you brought this issue to my
attention, I want to establish a few facts.  First, Weaver has made her
opinion on the Unwritten Rules exceedingly clear.”

“About damn time,” Vicky muttered, which earned a huff of what was
hopefully amusement from the other hero.

“Second, Weaver has demonstrated exceptional restraint in both powers
and actions since inheriting —”

“You can’t be serious!”

Armsmaster made a displeased sound about being cut off.  “I am privy to
a rather large collection of disturbing facts that you are not, Miss
Dallon.  While I do share your concern for your sister —”

“She’s dating Tattletale!” Vicky blurted out.

“Be that as it may,” he ground out, “I believe that attempting to remove
your sister from this sleepover would likely result in far more
casualties than if we simply speak with her tomorrow.  Weaver is highly
unlikely to initiate hostilities as a civilian.”

Vicky’s voice turned arctic.  “So we’re just going to leave Amy with
supervillains.”

“Miss Dallon, please understand that —”  Vicky flipped the phone shut,
then launched herself into the air.  Rationally, she knew that
Armsmaster wasn’t a coward and that the last thing she wanted to do was
fight Weaver, but that didn’t help ease the memory of Amy’s laughter as
she bantered with the Teeth.

It also didn’t help that Vicky had now met Taylor, the somewhat
unassuming teenager behind the terrifying mask.  Sure, the girl had been
a bit weird, but the Butcher wasn’t supposed to be shy.  Or quiet, and
definitely not cuddled up on a couch with her girlfriend while watching
old comedies.  Butcher should definitely not seem genuinely worried
about Amy!

The fact that Taylor was so normal just compounded with Vicky’s own
fears and Armsmaster’s unwillingness to help, winding up Vicky’s anger
like a spring.  The tension was going to release one way or another;
Vicky had enough presence of mind to know that going back to Taylor’s
house was a Bad Idea.

But… Amy!

Vicky pulled herself up short after turning and darting back towards the
Butcher’s… lair away from lair?  She could feel the strange disconnect
in her brain between the villainous murder machine and the shy girl
laughing alongside Amy, simultaneously reminding Vicky that her sister
was still surrounded by a whole room of supervillains and that she
couldn’t do anything about it.

So, after a somewhat cathartic scream into an uncaring sky, Vicky set a
course for the Palanquin.

Getting mildly drunk was probably not the wisest course of action right
now, but Vicky would settle for the one that made it marginally less
likely that she would do something stupid.  She could go, drink a little
bit, talk to the interesting people who frequented the Palanquin, and
while she could hardly forget her sister’s plight, Vicky had to trust
that Amy knew what she was doing… right?

Amy was the best hero Vicky knew.  There had to be a reason she was
hanging out with the Teeth, and it wasn’t like Armsmaster was going to
sit there and do nothing while Amy became entangled with villains.  If
he thought she was going to be okay for tonight, Vicky could probably
trust him.

Vicky just wished that it didn’t feel like running away.

 

------------------------------------------------------------------------

 

“But that’s not true!” Vicky said, gesturing wildly with her glass of…
whiskey?  Something expensive that the bartender assured her was on
someone else’s tab, despite the fact that Vicky had talked to a half
dozen people tonight and none of them were bringing her any drinks.  Not
that she would have taken them, of course — the only person she trusted
other than herself here was the bartender.  

In every other place she’d tried drinking she’d be leery of them as
well, but the Palanquin was different.  It was an open secret that
Faultline was behind the scenes here on some level, but their group
straddled a sufficiently subtle level of villainy that it just wasn’t
worth storming a place full of civilians to take them down.  Something
happening to public darling Glory Girl on their watch would change that
in an instant.

It was easy enough for her alcohol-addled attention span to ignore the
parallels between here and that arena the Teeth had taken over.

“Miss Dallon, please be —”

“How can you be so sure?” the cute but oddly serious platinum-blonde-
haired girl sitting next to Vicky at the bar said, lips pulling up in a
barely visible smile.

“I am took — have taken classes on it,” Vicky said.  “Sorry.  I’m taking
classes at the university.  The idea that parahumans whose powers
permanently change their app—apart— damn it, appearance are more likely
to be sociopaths was conclusively debunked!”

The man on the blonde’s other side snickered at Vicky’s inability to
words correctly, so Vicky shot him a glare that would have set him on
fire had her powers been a bit different.  Though, why were her powers
so different from her parents?  Something about second-generation powers
tickled Vicky’s mind, given how her shield was more like her cousins,
but she dismissed it as a useless drunken thought.

“And those professors — they were capes too, naturally.”  The blonde
girl might have sounded sincere if not for the twist of distaste on her
lips.  “Otherwise, it would be impossible for them to have ever really
experienced the terror of facing the parahumans they so easily write
about in their cowardly papers.”

“Um, I don’t think so?” Vicky replied, ignoring the way the man two
seats down set down his drink hurriedly and scampered away.  “But even
if they were, it’s not like they would want to fight the people they’re
researching.”

Blonde girl snorted, true amusement on her face for the first time that
night.  “Capes fight.  That’s what they do.”

Vicky opened her mouth to retort, but the logical (if liquor-soaked)
part of her brain reminded her that the other girl was right.  “Not all
of them.  Wait,” she said, cutting off the other girl.  “I’ve seen the
numbers.  But you should meet my sister — I’m not even sure she /can /
fight.”

Her drinking partner tilted her head before blinking several times in
quick succession.  “Ah, that would be Panacea, yes?  She is certainly
a /para /gon of heroism.”

“Damn right she is,” Vicky agreed, setting her drink down
enthusiastically.  She barely noticed as the bartender rushed over with
a rag to clean up the shattered glass.  “Makes the rest of us look bad.”

The other girl scoffed, rolling her eyes dramatically.  “As if the
Protectorate needs her assistance in that… endeavor.  One can only
wonder how they have managed to be so thoroughly shamed by the least
coordinated, least reputed gang of idiots on this coast.  Repeatedly.” 
Vicky opened her mouth to comment, but was distracted by her lack of
drink, the blonde girl just waved dismissively.  “Yes, yes, Butcher XV
may have somehow wrangled her gang of morons, but their conduct reeks of
incompetence.”

Right, the Teeth — Vicky had blissfully forgotten about her sister after
a drink or… three?  Enough that she wasn’t thinking about the fact that
Amy was hanging out with those same morons /right now /, probably doing
normal girl sleepover things?  Or did Teeth sleepovers involve shit like
going to Dunkin Donuts and robbing the place?

Even worse, from Vicky’s point of view, was that Amy was dating a
supervillain!  Vicky hadn’t even realized that her sister was gay before
Amy went off and snuggled up to the axe-crazy murder cannibals and their
unacceptably quiet leader and —

A single tear rolled down Vicky’s cheek, and it would have plopped into
her drink if she had one.  She glanced at the bartender, who was
glowering at her.  “Hey, Emily, hook a girl up, would you?”

“Miss Dallon —”

“Just give me a damn whiskey!  My sister is —”

A brief pressure on her other hand interrupted that thought, and Vicky
turned to find blondie giving her an oddly intense stare.  “Something
tells me you should not air your dirty laundry to the whole bar.”

“I still want that drink,” Vicky complained.  “Amy… We kinda had a
fight?  I think it counts as a fight.  I’m just worried about her and…” 
She trailed off, making a helpless gesture at the other girl.

The other girl threw her drink back in a single elegant, practiced
motion, setting the glass down with an odd sense of finality.  “Well, if
you want a sympathetic ear, why don’t we move to somewhere a bit
quieter, and less public?”

Several competing thoughts all tried to run through Vicky’s addled
brain, causing a pileup at the door and only letting one through.  A
shoulder to cry on about Amy’s situation sounded lovely right now; the
bartender’s relieved face, the cuteness of the blonde girl, Vicky’s open
tab, and any potential ramifications of telling other people that her
sister was becoming a villain were all jammed in the ‘to think about
later’ pile.

“Will there be more alcohol in it for me?” Vicky blurted. 

“Within reason,” the girl agreed with a dazzling smile, hauling Vicky to
her feet.  “I’m rather fond of my new apartment, and the walls do not
need any extraneous holes from a drunk wrecking ball.” 

Oh god, she had seen the video.  She’d been banned from drinking at high
school parties by all of her friends and family after that mess.  Well,
if she wanted to play that game, she could play games right back! 

“Lead the way then, oh blonde mistress.” 

They were both laughing as she led Vicky off by the hand.  Getting drunk
had been the best idea ever and Dean’s insistence that she never drink
again could suck it!

/Sunday April 24th, 2011 /

The sun was evil, whoever opened those shades was… double evil.

Vicky might have come up with a better insult had her head not felt like
she had been using it to pound nails all right; she had spent most of
the time since waking up trying futilely to escape the light screaming
in through the window without moving too much.  Last night must have
been a hell of a time if she was this hungover, but rather than try to
strain her throbbing brain remembering, Vicky was content to let her
mind wander.

Well, not actually content, but the next best thing.

She must have been trying to avoid thinking about something, if she was
this drunk.  Seeking solace at the bottom of a bottle wasn’t a healthy
coping mechanism, but being a hero — seeing the worst of humanity on a
semi regular basis, at least until the Empire collapsed — meant that
even she wanted a drink occasionally.

Hmm, the Empire… right, dismantled by the Teeth.

Vicky was reminded momentarily of her slimeball ex-boyfriend and his
Empire-apologist family, only to wince when she tried to grimace. 
Breaking up with him had been easier than expected, so that /probably /
wasn’t the reason she was drinking…

Neither was the fact that the Teeth got to take the Empire out instead
of Vicky.  Now, being jealous of the Butcher — that was certainly
hangover-worthy, but there were an infinite number of deserving assholes
to punch that even Amy —

Vicky lurched upright, nearly falling over with dizziness and nausea as
the events of last night finally caught up to her.  Amy had insisted on
going to the sleepover, and Vicky had agreed, despite her better
judgment.  Then her chance to grill the smug supervillain had gone right
out the window when it turned out that the shy girl on the couch was /
the fucking Butcher! /

That reminder twisted Vicky’s stomach.

She fought down the nausea, trying to piece together the rest of the
night.  After abandoning Amy to the Butcher’s clutches, Vicky had made a
beeline for the Palanquin — they didn’t care if she was underage.  She
barely remembered some guy hitting on her, then some blonde girl
interposing herself between them and starting a conversation on
parahuman psychology of all things.  They had talked a bunch, then she
led her off to a private room, words were said, and the rest…

Vicky blushed as she remembered the haziest portions of the night in
bits and flashes of lips and teeth.  Great, she’d had a fling with some
random girl she’d met at a bar.  One more thing she could check off the
bucket list.  Now she just had to figure out where the hell she was, and
where she had left the last dregs of her dignity.

Oh, and what to do about the fact that her sister was a villain now.

Also, keep away from any media attention before one of the cape rags ran
an article about her (mis)adventures last night.  Mom was good about
keeping them out of the spotlight with cease and desist orders and
veiled threats of lawsuits if they ran stories on her minor children,
but that didn’t do shit about PHO, and no doubt someone had posted
pictures or — Scion forbid — video. 

Vicky felt a shiver run down her body at the thought of that.  She had
been rather… animated as the night went on, and her dance partner had
gone with the flow.  She needed to find her phone…and her pants,
apparently.  A blush spread as she realized what state she was in and
she hurried to grab the only clothing she recognized as her own. 

As she did, her eyes finally adjusted and she took in the rest of the room.

Did she hook up with the world’s weirdest hoarder?  No, that wasn’t
quite right — the piles of weird junk were actually arranged in a way
that might generously be called ‘artfully,’ if an interior designer and
a civil engineer had a kid with violent tendencies.  Seriously, why were
there so many bits of concrete and asphalt on display alongside twisted
bits of metal?

“Oh good, you’re awake.”

Vicky looked up at the teasing voice to find a young, blonde-haired
woman only a year or two older than herself gazing imperiously from the
doorway.  Her expression was somewhere between haughty indifference and
cat-caught-a-falcon smug, which might have worked better had the girl
not obviously just woken up.  Still, Vicky could admire the effort that
went into such a complicated hairdo, flyaway strands or no.

“Something like that,” Vicky muttered.  “Um, no offense, but —”

A flicker of annoyance passed over the other girl’s face, but it was
quickly hidden.  “You forgot my name already?”

“I don’t usually drink that much!”

“Indeed.  I am known as the great Ashley Stillons.  You can refer to me
as, er, Ashley.”

Vicky nodded slowly, mostly due to her head still feeling like a box of
firecrackers.  “Hi Ashley, I’m Vicky.”  The other girl’s smile deepened
at that; there was zero chance she didn’t know who Vicky was, though
vague memories of last night indicated that Ashley had not made a big
deal out of drinking with Glory Girl. 

Ashley reached down, took her hand but rather than shake it, she pulled
it up to her lips and placed a gentle kiss on her knuckles.  “A pleasure
to be properly introduced, Miss Dallon.” 

Vicky couldn’t hide the heat blooming on her face as she looked away,
though it did at least confirm she had been recognized.  “I didn’t think
you would still be interested after we both sobered up…” 

There was that melodic laugh again that sent flutters through Vicky’s
stomach.  “Oh come now, I didn’t let myself get that drunk.” 

“Great, so it was just me making a fool of myself,” Vicky muttered. 

“And what an adorable fool you make.” 

Vicky wasn’t sure how to take that, so in the express interest of
avoiding further embarrassment, she chose to take it as a compliment and
move on.

“I have prepared coffee,” Ashley declared, sweeping dramatically through
the door and presumably towards the kitchen.  “I find it essential after
nights like the last.”

Vicky double-checked that she was decent before prying herself off the
couch and half-walking, half-floating after her host.  “Speaking of last
night… what did we actually do?”

“We drank, discussed topics ranging from your academic studies to your
sister’s girlfriend, and kissed, not necessarily in that order,” Ashley
replied, striding into the kitchen.  “No further, however — you held
your liquor remarkably well, but I am not one to take advantage of an
en-date in that fashion.”

Vicky really didn’t want to think about whether or not last night’s
shitshow was a date, so she instead focused on the steaming mugs of
coffee sitting on the kitchen table.  Everything in the kitchen seemed
almost brand-new except for those two mugs, which were gouged in strange
ways.  Still, they held coffee, and Vicky could wait to understand
Ashley’s taste in art after her brain was working.

Ashley joined her shortly after that, and they drank their coffee in
silence for a few minutes.  Coffee or no, Vicky was definitely not awake
or sober enough to deal with the self-satisfied smirk that kept curling
around Ashley’s own mug of morning ambrosia.  So, she gave the white-
haired girl a tired smile of her own and tried to focus on not thinking
about Amy.

Vicky rubbed at her temple.  Goddamnit, Amy.

“Are you alright?” Ashley murmured.  “Need something for your head?”

“It won’t help.”

Ashley set down her mug and arched a nearly-white eyebrow at Vicky, then
she smirked, fingers teasing at the hem of her shirt.  “How about
something to distract you?”

“Probably won’t help either,” Vicky groaned, attempting to banish the
image of Tattletale sitting on her sister’s lap from her mind.  

Ashley pouted and instead crossed her arms.  “I see.  In that case, it
is nearly noon.  What do you say we partake of the coming press conference?”

Vicky blinked in confusion, but unless something happened last night,
she didn’t recall anything of the sort going on.  While she deliberated,
Ashley swept back out of the kitchen, and when Vicky caught up, she was
already perched on the couch that Vicky had crashed on last night,
watching Deputy Director Renick hand off the microphone to —

Holy shit, that was Legend!

“This is certainly a show of force,” Ashley declared, though her
dismissive tone was at odds with the way that she clamped her hands
together on her lap.  Vicky certainly agreed with that assessment —
Legend was flanked by Armsmaster, Myrddin, and Chevalier, and all of
their various underlings were mingled about the rest of the stage.

A flicker of hope ran through Vicky’s chest.  “Do you think that they’re
here to fight the Teeth?”

Ashley snorted.  “Why would they do that?  I think you would agree that
Butcher XV is terrifying enough, yes?”

“Because we can’t just let the Teeth have the city!” Vicky retorted. 
“And Weaver is good, but against some of the strongest heroes in the
Protectorate?”

“Perhaps.”  Ashley gestured to the television, turning up the volume on
Legend’s speech.

/“… of bad news.  Director Emily Piggot is going into retirement, citing
ongoing health issues from her service at Ellisburg.” /

Vicky’s jaw dropped.  “No way.  Piggot’s tougher than nails.  Why would
she leave now, just when the PRT needs her?”

“Needs her for what?” Ashley asked with a smirk and a raised eyebrow. 
“To keep antagonizing the Teeth?”

“What do you mean, ‘keep antagonizing?’  The PRT has barely done
anything about the Teeth since Weaver took over!”  Vicky knew that this
wasn’t exactly fair, because even she herself had found the threat of
Weaver showing up to be a significant deterrent.  And with the Empire
gone, Vicky’s patrols had been much less exciting.

“To be fair, that’s the same amount they did concerning the Empire,”
Ashley pointed out. 

“They aren’t even trying,” Vicky whispered.  “The Teeth corrupt my
sister, and the Protectorate just… rolls with it!”

“Politics,” Ashley said with a shrug.  “I suspect that this incident
with your sister is not the only indiscretion the Teeth are holding over
the Protectorate.  That being said, the heroes need to be seen taking
some sort of action that won’t, say, see the city devolve like Boston.” 

“Still doesn’t make it right, not after all Amy’s done for them…” Vicky
muttered. 

“Well, I suppose you are sober enough for this discussion now.” Vicky
finally looked up at the girl and her sudden shift in tone, her platinum
blonde hair glistening in the afternoon (shit) light in a way that made
it look white.  “Did Amy ever once give you any indication that she was
being coerced?” 

Vicky was appalled by the question.  “Why would she want to hang out
with the Teeth?  They’re murderers!” 

Ashley, however, didn’t even acknowledge her statement.  “And you made
it pretty obvious she’s dating Tattletale.”  

“That isn’t an excuse!”

“No, but it does suggest that things are more complicated than they
seem.  Your sister is her own person, not some… damsel for you to rescue.”

The other girl chuckled at that for some reason, and Vicky rolled her
eyes to hide her blush.  Then she turned her attention to the press
conference rather than argue about family and cape politics with a girl
she… well, had shared a delightful night with, now that her head was
clearing up.  Somewhere between learning that Amy was gay and that Dean
was a douchenozzle, Vicky had started to appreciate girls a bit more and —

/“Is it true Miss Militia shot Panacea?” /

“WHAT?” Vicky yelped, the reporter’s shouted question yanking her back
the present.

/“There was an intelligence breakdown during a routine operation that…” /

Legend’s obvious dodge did nothing to assuage Vicky’s fears, and she
realized with a start that she had not checked her phone for messages
since waking up.  Her frantic searching of the couch was brought to an
abrupt halt when Ashley held out her misplaced device; she stumbled
twice putting in her password before being bombarded by friends asking
about Amy and family demanding to know where Vicky was.  All of that
however was ignored as she loaded PHO, and at the top of the Brockton
boards was the damning proof.

Holy shit.

At least the post confirmed that Ames was alright, though the rational
part of Vicky’s brain pointed out that the PRT wasn’t saying anything
about the operation.  That didn’t stop her from knowing where Amy was
last night, letting her fill in the obvious gap.  The PRT had attacked
Weaver’s sleepover — and wasn’t that an idea Vicky never thought she
could take seriously.  A sleepover that included her sister.  Amy had
been shot by another hero!

“I need to go,” Vicky blurted, frantically gathering the rest of her
things and forcing herself not to panic.  Her mind was awhirl with so
many conflicting thoughts that keeping any of them straight was
hopeless.  Amy was becoming a villain.  The PRT was ignoring the Teeth. 
New Wave had been made fools of by the Empire.  The Protectorate had
shot her sister.

A final check of her pockets revealed that her phone had gone missing
again, but an unfamiliar ringtone revealed that Ashley had taken the
device and called herself.

“There, now you have my number,” the bizarre girl said, proffering
Vicky’s phone.  “Feel free to text or call me whenever.  I’m in town to
meet family that I thought was lost for good.” Ashley said, then her
face turned a bit somber.  “Do try to not judge your sister too harshly,
for family can be a fleeting thing.  Be the family she clearly needs.” 

Vicky felt her throat go dry at the absolutely pleading look on Ashley’s
face.  “I…  I’ll talk to her.  Promise.” 

Ashley smiled, it was radiant as the sun as she brushed Vicky’s chin
with her fingers.  “Good girl.” 

There was no hiding the shiver that ran down her spine at those words. 
Nor the surprise when Ashley placed her phone back in her hand, then
swiftly walked over to a window and threw it open. 

“Best be off, though I’m sure we’ll meet again,” Ashley said, waving as
Vicky decided to take her up on the offered exit and set off for home as
quickly as she could.

 

------------------------------------------------------------------------

 

Once again, Vicky found herself flying away from a girl’s house far more
confused than when she arrived.

Fortunately, this time it wasn’t because of supervillains. 
Unfortunately, Vicky had no other ideas how to deal with Ashley.  She’d
been the very picture of a gentleman… or whatever the equivalent was for
a girl?  Ugh, this was all so confusing and all the lesbians she knew
were in the fucking Teeth, which was half her problem!  She had no idea
what to do about the fact that she wasn’t opposed to the idea of
pursuing something with Ashley, but she had nobody she could ask!  

Well, there was nothing stopping her from asking the Teeth in question,
but Vicky wasn’t so desperate that she would go to villains for help. 
She sure as hell didn’t want to talk about it with her mom, because as
awkward as the ‘talk’ was when she started dating Dean, she could only
imagine the conversation that would come from hooking up with a random
girl at the bar.   

She could reach out to Amy, but that would just be awkwardness
personified after she just flew off in a huff.  If Tattletale also
happened to be present, Vicky might just end up punching the smug bitch
for the inevitable mockery and Vicky didn’t trust herself enough to not
lose it at the moment. 

Knowing her luck, Dad was having a bad day.  Aunt Sarah would be too
worried about the PR bomb to have any time.  Uncle Neil was an /
incorrigible gossip / and would grill her about Ashley before making
sure his knitting group knew every sordid detail.  She hadn’t heard any
hint of her cousins experimenting with their dating pool, even with
Crystal off in college; she absolutely would have heard because Uncle
Neil wouldn’t be able to keep his mouth shut.  Seriously, it wasn’t like
she could just roll up on Legend and ask ‘how do I gay, even?’  

Her PR and merch sales were good, but not /that /good.

So, she was going home where she could hopefully unwind and not deal
with half the shit currently spiraling out of control in her life.  She
didn’t want to think about Amy being with a villain, and she sure as
hell didn’t want to think about Dean being a secret Nazi.  No wonder he
had been so weird about Amy at times, he must have seen her emotions
spike whenever she saw a cute girl. 

And… there was her house.  Why did flying have to be so damn fast? 
Maybe she could just overshoot it ‘accidently’ and take a lazy loop
across the bay before doubling back home…  No, that was just delaying
things and she still hadn’t answered her mom’s texts and calls.  There
was an ass chewing of biblical proportions coming and delaying it would
only fan the apocalyptic flames. 

Vicky didn’t even have her feet on the ground when the first screams
reached her ears.  Amy must have beat her home.  Well, best to get the
awkward disaster out of the way so she could go skulk in her room and
burn Dean’s bigoted face out of all their pictures. 

“You will /NOT / call yourself that under my roof!” Mom yelled as soon
as Vicky quietly opened the door.

Ah, home sweet home. 

“Why not?  Amelia is my goddamn name!” Amy yelled right back.

“You will not spit on my generosity by bringing /him / into this house!”

Amy scoffed.  “Yeah, my father was evil, big fucking deal.  At least he
kept the Nazis in check and wouldn’t have tolerated sex traffickers
setting up in the Bay!” 

“Who told you?” Their mother’s voice was almost deathly silent, and
Vicky could imagine her ‘lawyer stare.’  “Regardless, I will not let
this distract us from the issue at hand.  I find it very suspicious that
you were injured visiting your so-called ‘friends,’ especially when you
refuse to help me learn more about them.  Heroes do not shoot unprovoked
at other heroes, which suggests that your ‘friends’ are not the sort of
people I — or the authorities — want you associating with.”

Yeah, Amy was in Weaver’s house all right, but confirming that to their
mother would probably send her into a berserk rage.  Maybe Vicky could
sneak past all the drama and sequester herself away and ride the storm out. 

“The authorities were there!” Amy yelled.  “Remember the part of the
story where I got shot?” 

“Oh, I remember,” their mother said derisively.  “But the PRT’s story is
just as suspicious as your so-called ‘friends,’ and I have no doubt that
they’re hiding something.  For whose benefit, I don’t know, but I may
just have to ask Legend the real reason behind his visit.  A member of
the Triumvirate doesn’t just drop in on Brockton because a PRT Director
overstepped her bounds.” 

Yeah, discretion was absolutely the better part of valor today.  Thank
god Vicky’s flight was soundless.  The problem was that Amy had a line
of sight on the stairway up to their rooms, but as Vicky considered just
darting past, Ashley’s request floated back into her mind.  Maybe Vicky
could help her sister in another way.  Rather than try to sneak around,
she set her feet on the ground and stepped around the corner. 

Amy saw her immediately.  “Vicky!”

Holy hell was Ames pissed.  Vicky had just stepped into a much more
hostile situation than she had anticipated, but she had succeeded in
derailing the conversation at least.

“Victoria.”  Her mom’s stern voice rang out, sending a cold chill down
her spine.

Scratch that.  Was it too late to just fly off and find someplace to
hide?  Ashley had been nice, maybe she could…  No, she couldn’t run away
now, not when Amy needed her.  Keep the focus on herself, admit to
something illegal but largely harmless and maybe Mom would blow up at
her instead and forget all about Ames.

Vicky very pointedly did not think about calling Weaver and telling her
that one of her capes was in trouble.  For Vicky’s peace of mind, that
could not possibly work.

“Hi Mom, sorry I was out last night.” 

“You also failed to answer your phone,” her mom said with her lawyer voice. 

Shit, that was worse than bad.  Okay, Vicky just needed to smooth things
over enough to avoid a full on meltdown.  She’d even accept being
grounded if it got her out of a lecture or three.  Maybe the truth would
be so outrageous that she skipped straight to the part where she didn’t
spend hours getting lectured by the lawyer that was thoroughly raking
the PRT over the coals with the Canary case.

“Would you believe me if I said I got drunk and hooked up with a hot
blonde?” 

The hardened lawyer blinked at her casual admission of guilt. 

“I am aware, Victoria.  Your escapades were the talk of PHO until Amy
had her… indiscretion, which you missed because of said escapades.  What
do you have to say for yourself?” 

“Underage drinking is bad?” Vicky tried with a smile and grimace. 

It didn’t work if her mother’s growing indignation was any indication.

“Try again.” 

Vicky winced, yeah, she wasn’t weaseling her way out of this one.  Not
without betraying Amy at least, and there was no way she was going to do
that.  Amy was watching her while trying not to be obvious about it, and
she could see the tension in her form, though she wouldn’t be running
away while on crutches. 

Well, may as well come out with it then. 

“I guess the stuff with Dean hit me harder than I thought… and I made a
series of poor judgments that culminated in what may or may not be a
rather surprising discovery about myself.  It was irresponsible and rash
of me and I understand if you want to ground me for not being there when
my sister needed me.” 

The normally stoic lawyer blinked in surprise at her response and Vicky
bit down a smirk because damn, if that wasn’t such a mature response she
would eat her skirt.  Thinking about that, maybe she could use the
costume upgrade?  She’d been rocking the same look since she triggered
three years prior and it was a bit childish.

Thoughts for later.

“It might have been partially my fault too.” Amy added, giving Vicky a
look she couldn’t decipher.  “Vicky dropped me off at Taylor’s and
everything with Dean came up again.  Lisa and I obviously have a…
personal interest in the Empire being gone.  Words were said that I
think we’re all not proud of.” 

An olive branch that didn’t betray anything…  Okay, Vicky could work
with that. 

“I’m willing to put it behind us if you are,” Vicky said with as much
sincerity as she could manage.  It must have been enough, because Amy
responded with a tired smile and nodded.  “Now, how the hell did you get
shot?” 

Sorry Ames, but Vicky needed to know what cover story to run with before
she put her foot too far down her throat.  Obviously it involved the
Teeth, but she couldn’t just out her sister like that and risk
destroying any trust she had left.  No, this required subtlety and tact. 

Two things that had never come easily to her… which was why she would be
using that to her advantage by being as untactful as possible about the
right things to keep their mother’s attention off the wrong things!  It
was a brilliant plan and Vicky was quite proud of it. 

Her mother let out an exasperated sigh, pinching the bridge of her nose.
“Officially, the same people that called in the fake kidnapping tried it
again when your sister was visiting her friends last night.” 

“Which culminated in Miss Militia shooting me through a wall while I was
eating breakfast,” Amy added.  “She honestly thought that one of the
girls there was a Teeth cape, for some godforsaken reason, and I guess
someone got spooked.  They certainly sent enough heroes to fight a small
battle.” 

“Taylor did mention her dad was targeted by Hookwolf.  I’m sure that
didn’t help,” Vicky added cautiously.

Amy had already name-dropped Taylor so that much should have been safe. 
Their mom was very talented when it came to digging up information on
people, but not perfect.  She had missed the Stanfields’ connections
after all. 

“Hell no.  I was trying to finish my meal when the yelling started, and
before I could even stand — /bam /— a new hole in my leg.”  She gestured
at the bandaged section of her thigh under the skirt that Lisa must have
insisted she wear.  Amy was very much a ‘pants’ girl.  “Thankfully the
heroes realized their mistake immediately and patched me up.” 

“I just wish you hadn’t put it all over PHO,” their mom said.  “We have
public relations too, and your brash statements will have consequences
both short and long term, especially with the PRT.” 

“Not my fault they shot me,” Amy snapped.  “Even if they had been right
about everything, why the fuck would Militia try to shoot anyone, cape
or no, with lethal ammunition?  I’m pretty sure she tried that shit
against the Butcher, which is probably half the reason they’re getting
rid of her trigger-happy ass!  Are they /trying / to get a nuclear-
capable Butcher?”

Now that Vicky was thinking about it, Militia had been awfully uncareful
around Weaver.  Amy’s theory could have some weight to it, and she
couldn’t help but wonder if Director Piggot had ordered Militia to steal
the mantle and walk into the Birdcage.  Vicky had heard the Wards
complain about their boss enough to have a picture of what kind of woman
Piggot could be. 

“What do you mean ‘if’ they had been right?” Carol demanded, ice
creeping into her voice.  “Are you saying that the PRT was not mistaken
about their target?” 

Shit, that was exactly the wrong question to ask and knowing Ames, she
might get pissed enough with the run around to actually be honest about
it.  That was a disaster Vicky needed to avert immediately. 

So, she snorted.

At her Mom’s raised eyebrow she pressed on.  “Mom, I get it — there’s
been a lot of stupidity lately, but do you honestly think I would have
left Ames’ with the Teeth?  Who do you take me for?” 

“Victoria, the things I’ve been hearing from my friends in the PRT —” 

“Are rumors and speculation,” Vicky hastily said.  “We both know how
quickly those can spiral out of control.  Lisa was friends with Taylor,
whose dad happened to be the Hookwolf video guy and even I can admit
that kinda looks bad, but Taylor is an awkward nerd at best.” 

Just don’t mention that her girlfriend is named Chrissie and doesn’t
seem to give two shits about hiding her identity as Vex.  Weaver’s
identity was likely classified at the Director level, but Vex’s might
not be.  Nevermind her mom’s own deductive reasonings. 

“If you want, I can invite Taylor over for dinner,” Amy cut in, causing
Vicky’s attention to snap back to her sister. 

That was a dangerous offer, because while Taylor could pull off the
whole ‘harmless nerd’ routine, she was the goddamn Butcher and could
fall into that persona out of nowhere.  That would tip off Carol faster
than anything ever could, especially given that her mom had fought the
Butcher the last time the Teeth had been in town.  Hell, Ames showing up
in whatever costume she wore with them would be less of a bombshell than
Weaver at their dinner table. 

Rather than continue on that subject…  “Ames, why aren’t you in bed
resting?  Oh, and why isn’t Lisa here?” 

Amy’s eyes narrowed a bit.  “Lisa’s running an errand, she’ll be back
soon.”  Her attention shifted back to their mom with a harsh glare.  “As
for why I’m not in bed resting…”

Ah, the Amelia thing.  “Mom, I think this rousing game of twenty
questions can wait.  Ames needs her rest.” 

Vicky knew her mom wanted to retort, to say something and continue to
interrogate Amy.  Unfortunately for her, however, she could never resist
it when Vicky turned up the pleading eyes and pouting lip that hadn’t
failed her since she was six. 

An unreadable expression crossed her mother’s face.  “Very well, but
this conversation isn’t over.” 

“Thanks mom,” Vicky said quickly and was airborne, picking her sister up
with an indignant squawk and taking her up the stairs in one smooth
flight even as she heard her mother yelling about flying in the house. 

Anything that might distract things from Amy — Vicky needed to get to
the bottom of things with a clear and open mind, to let Amy tell her
side of the story without all the yelling and posturing.  She picked
Ames’ room to talk, dropping them both to the carpet carefully before
floating back to give Amy some space.

Any doubt that Vicky made the right choice by sticking up for her sister
when she came home was eliminated when she finally got a good look at
the ordinarily-exhausted healer.  Oh sure, the perpetual bags under
Amy’s eyes were only diminished and she wasn’t any less frazzled in
appearance, but there was a distinct lack of gloom and doom that Vicky
didn’t need her stupid ex-boyfriend to see.  “So, you want to go by
Amelia now?”

“It helps me remember my dad; what few memories I have of him are…
pleasant.  I don’t want to lose them.” 

“Tell me about him?” Vicky asked, taking a seat on the bed and patting
the spot next  to her for Am—elia to sit down.

Amelia smiled, taking the offered spot but leaning into her huge pile of
pillows instead of onto Vicky’s shoulder.  “I can’t remember his face
very well, but I remember him reading to me before bed, sitting with me
for tea parties and…” Her smile faltered.  “Him telling me to hide in
the closet until it was safe to come out.” 

That must have been when the Brigade came for him.  Vicky quickly ran
through her parents’ history, wondering if they had taken down any
notable villains about a decade ago.  There were some no-name criminals
that even Vicky couldn’t remember, but then there were also those like
Marquis and —

Oh fuck!

Vicky didn’t need the sinking feeling in her gut to know that she was
correct, even without the obvious-in-hindsight similarities in their
powers.  No wonder their mom wasn’t taking it well, she still hated
Marquis and if she was directing that same hate onto Amelia… 

Their family had sent Amelia’s father to the Birdcage, but how was
Amelia present when they attacked?  Was he bringing her to his lair or
something?  The details of how they had captured Marquis were never
published, and Mom never talked about it in detail… 

“Ames…  Where was that closet?” 

“His private study in our home,” she said softly.  “That’s why nobody
made a big deal over Fleur.  They didn’t have a leg to stand on, and
they were afraid of the Empire trying to make good on Allfather’s pact
to kill any daughter of the Marquis.” 

Christ, was her entire life a lie?  Between the revelations about the
Stanfields, the Teeth just chilling with her sister over Blazing Saddles
like the teenagers they were, and now her own family…  Were there any
good people left in the city?  She couldn’t even count herself among
that number after having the dumpster incident thrown back in her face
like that. 

“Tell me about Lisa?” Vicky flailed instead, hopefully one of her darts
would stick on something less traumatic for her sister.  “You seemed
pretty close at the sleepover and as your sister, I feel like I need to
hear all the juicy details.” 

Amelia groaned, but there was a smile back on her face.  “She’s been
amazing.  I met her at Taylor’s… clubhouse when I went there to tell
them off.  Things, uh, didn’t go quite to plan.  We all ended up
talking, which I obviously fucking needed, but Lisa went the extra mile
and gave me a hug.  I ended up crying myself to sleep in her arms.” 

Well, that was kind of sweet, but at least Lisa seemed to care about
her.  The last thing Vicky would tolerate was a Thinker manipulating her
sister.  “Well, if she ever breaks your heart, let me know so I can do
my sisterly duty and break her everything-else.” 

“Vicky!” Amelia exclaimed, smacking her shoulder.  “No smiting my
girlfriend in righteous indignation.  Even if Taylor wasn’t so
enthusiastic about protecting her friends, Lisa was the one who is
helping me with the healing goo.  So if you want me back on my feet soon…”

“Well, so long as you’re happy, they have nothing to fear!” Vicky said
confidently, pointedly ignoring the implication that Amelia was bio-
tinkering in her spare time.  The Star Wars nerd in her wanted to ask
about tanks of blue healing gel, but…  “I’m still not entirely okay with
everything, but I want what’s best for you…and they seem good for you,
weird as that is.” 

“Tell me about it,” Amelia grumbled quietly.  “If someone had told me a
month ago that sharing a blunt with the goddamn Butcher would be the
turning point of my life getting better, I would have had them admitted
to a psych ward immediately.” 

Vicky couldn’t help but snort.  “Weaver does seem to be a different kind
of Butcher.” 

“She’s just as dumbfounded by her life improving as well,” Amelia said. 
“Isn’t that sad?  Taylor has been shit on by basically everyone, and
it’s only the Teeth who would give her the time of day.  Makes you
wonder what she could have accomplished if the world didn’t hate her.” 

The weird thing was, Ames wasn’t wrong.  The ABB was gone, the Empire
was ashes, and whatever Coil had been was no more.  The Teeth were all
that was left and their leader was a cuddlebug lesbian who liked old
comedies.  Things could be so much worse. 

“Enough of that though,” Amelia said, propping herself up with a
devilish grin.  “Tell me about this girl you met.” 

Vicky groaned, flopping back on the bed.  “Ask me again after we’ve had
a proper date.” 

Amelia’s grin only grew.  “So there /will /be a second date then?” 

Vicky’s face grew hot enough that she had to look away, but there was a
smile tugging at her lips. 

“Yeah, I think there will be.” 

“Nice.” Amelia said, then she fished something out of her coat pocket. 
“Lisa forbade me from taking too many pain meds, so weed it is.  Wanna
get high with me?” 

Vicky stared for a moment at the offered blunt, knowing full well that
it would probably be the best weed she had ever smoked if it came from
Amelia’s personal stash that the Teeth were begging her for…  Plus, it
was a way for her to bond with the sister she would do anything for —
including lie through her teeth to their mother.. 

“Fuck it, I’m in.” Vicky pried open the window next to the bed as Amelia
lit the blunt, took a hit, and passed it with practiced ease.  Drugs or
no, Teeth or no… seeing Amelia happy mattered more to Vicky than
anything else at the moment. 

“Does this girl have a name at least?”

Vicky braced herself to cough, only to discover that her sister really
did amazing work.  There was no harsh smoke and what was there barely
smelled at all.  “Ashley.” 

Ames smirked as Vicky returned the blunt.  “Ashley, huh?  Funny given
we’re both sucking ash right now.” 

Vicky couldn’t help but chuckle, especially with how this amazing wonder
weed was making her feel.  “Yeah, she introduced herself as Ashley
Stillons, went all grandiose with the introduction too.” 

Amelia burst into a fit of hacking coughs, forcing the blunt into
Vicky’s hand and using the other to stabilize herself.  “Still—/cough /
… Stillons?  Are y— /cough /—fuck, you sure?”

“Yeah, why?” 

Vicky watched as Amelia’s situation deteriorated as cackling laughter
joined the coughing, causing Amelia to fall over and twitch wildly on
the bed.  No explanation was forthcoming, but Vicky couldn’t help but
think she had missed something important. 

Chapter End Notes

I suppose another name for this thread could be ‘How to take over a city
in under thirty days by Weaver, Butcher XV’.  

In that time we saw a young herocome onto the scene in a big way, taking
the fight to the ABBafter the Butcherand Lungwere taken out by unknown
factors, only to then learn that the young hero, Weaver, was the Butcher
all alongand this was her trying to do what good she could until the
madness claimed her.  A noble goal, and she did so much until she snapped. 

Or did she?

After a disastrous attempt to capture the newest Butcher, she returned
to the Teeth in one of the most horrific announcementswe’ve ever seen. 
The Empire bled and Weaver showed just what it meant to cross her. 
Then, radio silence. 

Days later, the mayor’s niece is kidnappedthe same day that the
Undersiders graduated from smash and grabto armed bank robbery.  As you
can see from the link, it didn’t end well as Weaver just so happened to
be in the area and decided they were her minions now.  She proceeded to
fight the Brockton Wards singlehandedly, not harming a one, then doused
them in what has now been confirmedto have been pizza sauce. 

To add to matters, an unnamed member of the Teeth deliveredsaid missing
niece to Brockton General and Panacea’s care on Weaver’s behalf.  We
didn’t know the details until just days after the Empire’s fall where
Weaver revealed that Coilhad been behind both the kidnapping and the
Undersiders.  Part of their severance package for being accessories to
kidnapping was to sell out their boss and back the Teeth in his takedown. 

Weaver declined to commentbeyond that, offering only cryptic warningsto
the PRT. 

Then there was the Empire…  Holy hell was that a ride, from the Arena
attackto the following raids in Empire territory, a battle with the
Protectorate and New Wave, the attempted live streamingof a murder that
Weaver herself prevented, which then turned into murder of a different
sort as she killed both Cricketand Hookwolf in terrifying fashion. 

Then came the morning news…  Words can’t describe this one, just watch…

There were other battles hereand there, but suffice to say, the Teeth
now run the criminal side of Brockton Bay and it’s not clear if the
Heroes can actually do anything about it at this point even with the
excuse they’re using to bring everyonein. (Including Legend!)  So, I
guess I’ll just say it, all hail our new insect overlord?

announcement.  Despite the Empire’s constant recruitment attempts, now
permanently at an end, I could never have joined for a multitude of
reasons.  First and foremost, I am not white.  I am of Middle Eastern
descent and it is obvious.  Maybe someday I’ll unmask like New Wave, but
for now I’m okay saying that much.

The other reason?  I’m a proud lesbian in my civilian life, even if I
haven’t had the greatest of luck on that front.  (Thank God for the DM
restrictions on PHO for verified capes)

(Seriously, fuck Nazis and good riddance to bad rubbish)
