    Chapter 35: Consequence 4.1

Chapter Notes

See the end of the chapter for notes <#endnotes35>

/Saturday May 7th, 2011 /

“It’s too goddamn early for this shit,” Chrissie groaned. 

“Agreed,” I said, kissing her forehead.  “Damn morning people ruin
everything.” 

“Says the Noctis cape,” she muttered, drifting back off into Morpheus’
embrace.

My girlfriend was presently in costume, curled up against my armored
side as we drove along the early Saturday morning traffic towards the
meeting point.  I could have easily teleported myself there, but this
wasn’t supposed to be a hostile meeting; it was supposed to be a calm
and measured negotiation with the Elite.  So, of course it was pouring rain.

/“Bets on how long it takes the negotiations to go tits up?” /Butcher
mused. 

Naturally the promise of bets meant that the entire collective was soon
deep in their usual banter of wagering on what I would be eating over
the next week or so.  Sometimes I missed the simplicity of just grabbing
a fast food breakfast burrito on the way to school. 

Of course, that derailed every argument in my head in one horrified
moment of agreement from the collective.  Fast food burritos were a sin
against nature and all she stood for.  That thought seemed to mollify
the vultures and they promptly returned to their own bickering over how
stupid the Elite were going to be tonight. 

My own bet was on ‘pretty goddamn stupid.’

They were meeting us on the outskirts of the city, but on the ride over
I had already picked up three different buildings they were repurposing
into forward bases for their coming operations over the last few days. 
Needless to say, I was not amused. 

/“Why not?” / Knockout asked innocently.  His snickering did nothing to
help him.  /“It’s been how long since we had a good fight?  You know you
want this as much as we do.”  /

/What I want is for us to go at least two weeks without a crisis.  It’s
bad enough that Legend is / still /here and from what Madison has passed
on, there’s another wave arriving in a few hours. /

/“Visiting Wards from New York and Chicago,” / Alkaline stated.  /“We
don’t have much to worry about there.  It isn’t like they’re bringing in
more capes with reputations for trouble, we’re golden.”  /

/“Do you need a reminder of how many times children have inherited
before?” /Quarrel asked, sending me a glare. 

/Twice.  /

Myself and Alkaline were both underage when we inherited, and Alkaline
barely saw her twentieth before she too joined the chorus thanks to
Knockout being an asshole that just wanted to fight.  It was never too
early for me to think that I might soon find myself amongst their
esteemed company.

The distant chants of ‘one of us’ were promptly ignored. 

What did it say about my sanity that none of this felt weird to me
anymore?  In less than a month I had gone from stoic but shy Taylor to
the fuck mothering Butcher in name and deed.  I’d stripped the flesh
from men, played head games with their skulls, and used severed limbs to
beat down the opposition.  To any sane observer, I was a monster with
few equals outside of groups like the Nine, and yet… 

The city was on the upswing.  After Kaiser’s fall (I gave the now
cackling collective a quick shove before the Humpty Dumpty jokes started
again), we had managed to wrangle control of most of the city’s
organized crime from the few elements that managed to avoid imploding
after we followed the Allies’ example and purged our city of the Nazi
scourge. 

I had hoped that my antics would deter most groups from attempting to
set up shop in the same city where a man had been so thoroughly
dismantled on live TV, but no.  The greedy idiots within the Elite saw
that as an opportunity instead.

When they requested a meeting, Lisa happily agreed to it and negotiated
the date and time.  Thank god for her negotiating skills — the Elite
wanted it an hour earlier.  Soulless bastards, did they not know how
many school age capes I had recruited?

/“Probably a bad example if you are looking for the moral high
ground,” / Chisel murmured.

“At least I offered them a truce,” I whispered, careful not to wake up
my girlfriend.  This wasn’t a capital-T Truce, like an S-class threat,
but I had offered the Elite the opportunity to sit down and talk about
their designs on our city before there were any… misunderstandings.  It
was a damn sight more than any Butcher had done before and I had
(perhaps naively) expected them to want to avoid bloodshed.

Instead, the dirt had barely settled on the Empire capes’ unmarked
graves when the first of the Elite’s busybodies had shown up and started
poking around.  I had stayed my hand, partially so that I did not reveal
more of my powers, hoping that they were just scouts; new arrivals
accelerated once we made our offer of a truce.

And now they were going to learn the price of trying to double-cross
Butcher XV.

/“You know they will have counters for your powers,” /Stratego stated,
watching through my bugs as our various strike teams took up their
positions near the Elite unsafehouses.

Knockout laughed.  /“Let them try and counter our fists!”  /

/“The saving grace of it all,” / Damascian said, pausing dramatically
before shifting her voice, /“the negotiations should be short.”  /

The Butchers blinked in surprise.  /“Did you just quote Obi Wan to
us?” /Quarrel demanded. 

/“Paraphrased,” / Fester corrected before I could.  /“But yes, the bitch
absolutely did.”  /

/“You are all jealous that Wars has cooler tech than Trek,” /Damascian
said haughtily. 

/“Yet your power never let you make a lightsaber,” /Sabertooth reminded
her with a toothy grin. 

Damascian shrugged.  /“I would point out that the chainsword was a more
thematically appropriate weapon.”  /

I searched through her memories and confirmed that, yes, she had created
such a weapon, but that said blade had been destroyed in an early battle
with Lung.  Truly a waste, and worse, it seemed to be a running theme
when the past Butchers got their hands on Tinkertech or even anything
remotely fancy.  The twenty six remaining OTs-62s that Quarrel had
ordered were a testament to that.  Even heavily modified as they were,
they weren’t Tinkertech, which was a saving grace.  No maintenance
beyond the standard for a firearm. 

Ugh, I was letting my thoughts ramble again.  

The Elite were already arriving at the meeting point, three cars
divesting themselves of five capes and twelve armed normals.  If I were
them, I would have slipped an additional cape or two into the strike
force as a surprise.  The Empire had made good use of that tactic back
in the day with Skadi suddenly being in the midst of several battles. 
When used correctly, the effect was devastating. 

Not that it had ever dissuaded the young Robbie back before he earned
the ‘Big’.  Funny enough, he had earned that title by besting said
giantess when she transformed during a skirmish with our forces in the
mid-nineties.  He had earned his reputation long before his now famous
duel with Jack Slash.

That it ended in a draw spoke volumes, especially when Jack had struck
first.  Both walked away with new scars and grudges, and it wasn’t a
coincidence that the Nine had avoided coming anywhere close to the Teeth
ever since.  It was almost too bad the heroes would never be willing to
admit that.

I was almost insulted by the preparations of the Elite in that light —
five capes and twelve normals were not even close to enough to take me
down unless I was being incredibly arrogant.  They had even driven a
limousine to the meeting place!

/“Which you are if you don’t think this team wasn’t specifically built
to counter you,” /Ironsides grumbled, pushing a few memories forward of
similar issues in New York.

/No doubt.  Most will be immune to physical maladies, so changers or
Case 53s, / I mused. /  Tinkers might also be in play, but they should
be vulnerable to the pain blast. /

Alkaline snorted.  /“It’s an area-of-effect.  According to the PRT,
shouldn’t it be a pain shake?” /

/  /In that moment, I understood why my predecessors completely failed
to get anything productive done.

/“Projection based Masters might also be in play,” / Stratego noted,
ignoring her.  /“Those outside might be said Masters.” / 

/“He has a good point,” / Marauder reluctantly agreed. 

/“All the plans in the world mean nothing if contact with the enemy
breaks them.” /Knockout said, trying, and failing, to sound sagely. 

/“The plans or the enemy?” / Pyro asked with a grin. 

“Let us see who breaks,” I said aloud, startling Chrissie awake as our
car slowed to a stop. 

“Mmm ‘wake,” Chrissie muttered, stretching her limbs, causing her joints
to snap and pop. 

“Of course you are,” I said with a knowing smirk that quickly fell. 
“The Elite are already here.” 

“Joy,” Chrissie deadpanned.  “How much boring conversation am I going to
be forced to endure before the fun begins?” 

“Little to none would be my guess,” Lisa’s voice called over our comms. 
“Did you enjoy your nap?” 

“I will only answer that if you can confirm you lack a Pandemic curled
up in your lap at present,” my girlfriend countered. 

“Then we are at an impasse,” Lisa declared theatrically.  “Robbie’s team
is ready and the others will be in position within moments.” 

That confirmed what my swarm was telling me.  Across the city, I had
people in place and ready to move upon one of the Elite’s new redoubts. 
As for the other two strongholds… 

“Browbeat on standby.” 

I smiled, knowing the chaos that was to come. 

 

------------------------------------------------------------------------

 

“Butcher,” one of the Elite snarled as I stepped into the improvised
meeting room. 

It wasn’t anything special, consisting only of a long table with five
chairs on each side, the number we had agreed upon for this meeting.  I
had of course brought Chrissie with me, because there was nobody I
trusted more at my side in the entire city.  The other three positions
were occupied by members of Robbie’s team.

“Holdout,” I greeted without an inflection.  “You are the emissary the
Elite has sent to treat with us?” 

“We were told we were to meet a representative,” the man growled. 

/“They can’t be this stupid…” / Sabertooth grumbled. 

Butcher grunted in agreement.  /“Well, it looks like Stratego was
correct, they planned this meeting as nothing but an excuse and expected
us to behave like Teeth.” /

“I would say that as Weaver, I am rather representative of the Teeth as
a whole,” I said, stepping up to the table.  “Now, are we going to
discuss a business arrangement, or should I look for other partners?”

“That won’t be necessary,” another of the Elite stated.  “It would seem
the rumors of your eloquence were not exaggerated.” 

/“Oh goddess, not this insufferable ass,” / Damascian muttered. 

A multitude of memories surfaced at her prompting and I too suddenly
felt the urge to groan.  “Inviolable.” 

The Elite Tinker grinned.  “I take it Damascian hasn’t forgotten me if
the raw loathing seeping into your voice is any indication.” 

“Nope, and I can see you’re still pissed that she shot you down,” I
countered easily.    “She’s also laughing that you resorted to joining
the Elite.  Now, what does the Elite want in my city and why should I
grant it?” 

Inviolable chuckled and decided to take a seat at the table.  I hadn’t
given him permission to sit, which made this a slight against my
authority as the local warlord.  I was very tempted to hit him with a
localized pain blast centered on something sensitive. 

/“I would happily part with my food votes if you do so,” / Damascian
begged me. 

/First excuse he gives me, consider it done.  /

A quick cheer rang out in my head at the promise of pain and violence,
but I was more focused on the power play before me as two others took
seats beside the asshole.  The remainder of the Elite took their
positions behind them in a flanking guard formation.  I fought down a
sudden urge to shoot the bastards, and not all of it was from my
predecessors.

None of my people had taken a seat, as I was still standing. 

I could hear Chrissie’s teeth grinding beside me, her anger barely
concealed.    I began to call my swarm into the room, letting them
steadily grow in density until the Elite took notice.  I allowed myself
a smirk behind my mask when I saw Inviolable begin to panic.   
Bloodsight was great for learning to read people after all. 

“You seem awfully sure of yourself,” my swarm spoke as I leaned over the
table.    “You come to my city, disrespect me to my face, and worst of
all…”    I swept my gaze across all five of them, making sure they saw
my mask moving with me.    “You prepared daggers for my back, so why in
the hell should I treat with you?” 

“What daggers?” Holdout demanded. 

“Rock and roll,” Lisa’s voice called out over our coms.

Spree’s body exploded into clones halfway across the city as Hemorragia
let out a cheer that the Teeth with them answered.  Inside the building,
the Elite present all froze at the sound only to join in with their own
screams as Bitch and her dogs tore through the windows in a shower of
broken glass and shrieking metal. 

One of the dogs, her newest if I was parsing things correctly, grabbed
the first person she could and thrashed, severing him in twain.  The
horrified members of the Elite stood frozen for a single beat longer
before stampeding towards the stairs where they met the tide of Spree
clones and a grinning Hemorragia. 

“Evening gents.” She said casually.  “Do try to make your deaths worthy
of my collection.” 

It was almost sad how casually she dismembered them, none of these men
were fighters it seemed.  What a joke.  Did the Elite really think so
little of us that they brought such green idiots with them to tangle
with known killers? 

I would need to talk with Rachel about Chica, but a Chihuahua could only
be trained so well in two weeks time, and those were mean dogs on a base
level.  Make their bite as bad as they think it is and you have a recipe
for trouble.  I knew that personally, having been there to help restrain
the abused pup for her first enhancement.  If she got overly-
enthusiastic we could always placate her with Spree clones for a few
minutes until the transformation wore down.

That situation well enough in hand, I shifted my focus eastward, towards
what I hoped was a more amusing fight.

/“Well, that was disappointing,” / Marauder muttered. 

The heroes’ team was mildly more amusing.  Browbeat passed word along,
then darted forwards with Shadow Stalker and Vista scrambling to keep
up.  It said much that the youngest Ward had wanted to tag along on an
early-morning patrol without being in the loop (she had tried to call
Armsmaster, after all); Sophia was clearly excited for the upcoming
violence at the second location.

Stalker ghosted through the window of the safehouse where an Elite
Tinker, a Brute, and their goons were holed up, snapping off two shots
with her crossbows and dropping two of the goons in an instant.    A
brick opened the other window, allowing Browbeat to step through via a
knot of twisted space; they immediately started trading blows with the
other Brute.  The Tinker wasn’t much better off, reaching for their gear
only to convulse and fall to the floor in a twitching heap — Vista had /
finally / been given a taser.

/“That’s bad for us, idiot!” / Quarrel snapped.

Browbeat was a powerful Brute, and their limited telekinesis allowed
them to hold their own against someone much stronger and more durable. 
  It helped that Stalker was providing a distraction and ghosting
through their opponents’ blows to keep the Brute off guard.    Space
shimmered again and the Brute suddenly fell backwards… and upwards at
the same time before falling back to the floor head first. 

Browbeat and Stalker turned back to Vista who was checking her gloved
nails. 

/“Show off,” / Fester said with a smirk. 

The third site…  well, they had a large collection of drugs, and I
didn’t trust Damien anywhere close to it.    Todd’s team was on standby
to sort the haul, but other than that, it was Robbie’s second in command
leading a new team we had been training.    No capes had been observed
at this site, but we had tipped off New Wave to the location.    Amelia
claiming to have overheard something while healing was such a generic
excuse to pass on information, but it was one she had used before. 

Despite the time, Glory Girl and Laserdream were patrolling about half a
mile away — I assumed the only reason they were up this early on a
weekend was because Amelia had tipped off her sister explicitly.    It
didn’t feel right to rely on capes not technically involved with the
Teeth, but we wanted some deniability on the grander scale, plus it
would help the heroes look productive and proactive. 

Brockton Bay was a bit of a powder keg at the moment and overwhelming
force could easily unnerve the wrong people.    Still, the unpowered
Teeth swept through the building with a military precision, even if it
was a touch undisciplined and there were a few panicked shots that
resulted in some injured Elite.    Eh, no point crying over spilt blood. 

One minute after Lisa had called the start, it was pretty well over. 

I stood in silence, watching the Elite grow more and more uncomfortable
by the second.  They were likely waiting to hear status updates from
their goons before their own treachery could start, trying to execute a
plan that probably wouldn’t have accomplished much except make everyone
more angry.

/“The Elite never had a good answer for overwhelming force,” / Chisel
murmured, to Stratego’s rumbling agreement.

/“And I sincerely doubt they were expecting to have their operation
beheaded so dramatically.” /

A chorus of excitement grew, and I shook my head once (without letting
the Elite in front of me out of my sight).  /We are not beheading anyone! /

Once the Teeth started their post-battle trophy-taking at the first and
third site, I finally let myself start to laugh.  It grew into a
maniacal cackle rather quickly, and I focused on how the Elite tensed
instead of how Spree and Hemorrhagia were having Bitch’s dogs tear apart
screaming Elite capes for their bones.

“What daggers indeed,” I said, bringing my laughter under control. 
“Tell me, were you /planning / on losing the forces you scattered around
my city, or were they a housewarming gift of trophies for my capes?”

Immediately one of the flunkies pulled out a phone and began frantically
demanding answers.    The shock on his face was answer enough, but he
still leaned over and whispered something to Holdout.

“You tipped off the heroes!?” Holdout demanded.

I snorted.  “Don’t blame me for your men being sloppy.  We had to call
off one team when the Wards moved in.” 

“You lie!” 

Blatantly, but he didn’t need to know that.

“This is an outrage!” Inviolable exclaimed, standing up abruptly.  That
seemed to be some sort of signal: the Tinker’s armor started glowing,
which was followed immediately by Holdout throwing a pair of grenades
directly at me and the other Teeth.  The analytical part of my mind
recognized their strategy and moved to counteract it while the emotional
part was raging that they were legitimately trying to kill my girlfriend.

/“Rip their throats out!” / Marauder bellowed, and for once I was in
agreement.

Still, I had to deal with the grenades, first.  Using Quarrel’s power, I
swatted one of them directly into the face of one of the Elite capes. 
The second was too far out of my grasp, so I used one of my own force
fields to stop it short.  Vex followed up with a screen of her own that
was clearly designed to redirect the blast instead of stopping it.

“Down!” I yelled, grabbing Vex to my chest and pulling her down with
me.  Robbie’s men did likewise… but there was no explosion.  Instead,
both grenades erupted into a pile of all-too-familiar whitish
foam.  /“They’re not trying to kill you — they’re trying to give you to
the heroes!” / Sanguine realized.  I hardly needed the reminder.

Okay, no more Miss Nice Butcher.

I rolled with Vex to get some distance from the expanding foam, then
teleported practically on top of Holdout as he tried to go around the
pile.  Pain blasting the Elite capes only seemed to work on one woman
whose skin was turning green somehow; she went down in a heap.  Another
was trapped in their own foam grenade, leaving me with Holdout,
Inviolable, and a mystery cape.

/“They planned to confront you today,” / Stratego said unhelpfully.

“Tell me something I don’t already know!” I roared as the fight began in
earnest.

Even if they were immune to a few of my tricks — fuck, mystery cape
was /strong / — and unperturbed by the razor sharpness of Vex’s power,
they were still impeded by the force fields themselves.  And
unfortunately for the Elite, fighting me didn’t distract me from having
my swarm harass their men outside when they tried to bring in more foam.

/“We have additional help,” / Chisel murmured.  /“Unless those foam
grenades are pulling their own pins.” /

The Butchers laughed as another grenade went off, almost costing me a
blow to the head in the process.  “Do you mind?  I’m trying to fight
here!”  I pirouetted around a kick, then threw a retaliatory punch that
shattered the Case 53’s jaw in a spray of crystalline shards.

/“Making me PROUD!” / Knockout cheered.

The unpowered Teeth had pulled back to the corner of the room and were
taking occasional potshots with their guns while Vex corralled the now-
vulnerable Inviolable with a storm of her power.  He could break and
resist the force fields, but not faster than Vex could create them in
awkward locations.

/“Ooooh, ouch,” / Knockout hissed while Fester laughed her ass
off.  /“She’s getting better at that.” /

Meanwhile, I was having the time of my life fighting the two Brutes. 
Holdout shifted back and forth from stone remarkably quickly, forcing me
to dodge even his weak blows lest they turn into stone hammers when they
connected.  On the other hand, if the Case 53 had other powers besides
being seemingly made of crystalline something, I didn’t see it.

I was so caught up in the fight that I barely registered when backup
arrived, at least until Animos Kool-Aid manned through the wall with a
scream that dropped Holdout in combination with the pain blast.  Reaver
followed an instant later, his scythe taking off one of the Case 53’s
limbs above the wrist.  I caught a brief view of ruby veins in reddish
marble before I kicked the stone hand at Inviolable and nailed him right
on the forehead.

If he fell over into a mess of Vex’s power, that was his fault.

Despite the fact that the fight had lasted several long minutes, I still
found myself amped up on adrenaline and a desire for revenge against the
capes that would have dared to try to capture me and Vex.  The sight of
my enemies sprawled out on the floor and several deep breaths were
enough for me to calm myself down somewhat, and even the Butchers were
polite enough not to remind me of the last time someone tried this
particular stupidity.

/“You were right about one thing,” / Reflex said.  /“The negotiations
were short.” /

The Butchers giggled at that in my head, trading a few other movie
quotes back and forth, but my attention had drifted away from this
battlefield and to the other parts of the operation.  Part of me wanted
to go give even a surreptitious hand to the Wards out of some misplaced
sense of heroism — it wasn’t like Spree, Hemmy, and Rachel needed the
help, as they were already halfway back to the lair — but I didn’t want
to show my hand this soon.

/“I’m bored,” / Pyro complained.

I facepalmed.  “We literally just fought the Elite.”

/“Barely!  And you didn’t even teleport behind them and kill their HR
rep!” / she continued.

/“Their what?” / several Butchers asked, but their questioning was cut
short by Lisa’s voice in my ear.

“Shit fuck, boss!  We’ve got a problem!  The Wards ran into Bastard Son!”

/That / was very much a problem, and the chorus agreed loudly.  The
Elite’s most despised brawler had a reputation almost as bad as mine,
and he was perfectly happy to rough up Wards that crossed his path. 
“How?” I hissed, double-checking that all of my gear was ready.  “And
why wasn’t he here?”

Lisa made a pained noise.  “Ugh… suspected trouble, I think, but not
everywhere at once.  I guess the Wards got unlucky.”

/“Putting it mildly,” / Alkaline said seriously.  /“But Taylor…” /

“I’m just looking,” I replied absently, closing my eyes to focus on my
far away bugs.  The relays made it hard to see clearly, but I could get
a general sense of the battle.  Stalker was down but not out, taking
potshots /through / a wall while Browbeat carried Vista as they climbed
a fire escape.  On the street below were over a dozen people, all
presumably masters of some obscure object.

Luckily for everyone involved — especially the normal goons whose
mastery did not include bee immunity — the Wards did not appear to be in
grave danger.  Instead, the goons were protecting the downed Elite
capes.  If either of my admittedly competent bullies had been able to
really pull out the stops, I had no doubt they could have at least put
up a good showing, but Bastard Son had earned his name.

I was sincerely tempted to send a swarm of the nastiest bugs after the
asshole himself, standing confidently in the middle of the street as he
was, but instead I fought down my bloodlust and reached out to Lisa. 
“Can Vicky give them a hand?”

“I’ll send her over,” the Thinker said.  “The Protectorate is sending
Assault, too.”

Sending him for extraction only, she didn’t need to say.  I ground my
teeth in frustration — given the absurd firepower hanging around my
city, it was maddening that they weren’t willing to take this
opportunity to even just engage the Elite.  Their obsession with the
status quo was why we were in this position to begin with.

Thus, I had to watch as the Wards’ efforts were undone, the downed capes
recovered and dragged to Bastard Son.  They set up a defensive formation
immediately, possibly expecting the sane response of Legend dropping by
to see what was going on.  Stratego’s power pinged immediately, and to
my surprise Stalker lifted herself up to see out of the window.  She
fired a last group of bolts at the group, only for the shots to pass
through empty air as the Elite vanished in a flash.

/“What the ever loving fuck?” / Knockout said. 

/“A teleporter?” / Stratego wondered. 

/“Was it Tinkertech, or a cape we were unaware of?” / Alkaline asked. 

Damascian was uncharacteristically furious, yelling, /“Kick Inviolable
in the dick for this!” / 

Blinking, I couldn’t find the bugs I had been using to mark the group
anywhere with my swarm sense.    Throwing caution to the wind, I decided
to teleport to see if there was anything useful left.  Lisa had just
enough time to warn Browbeat before I arrived in a blast of flame,
though Stalker still snapped off a single arrow on reflex, which I
caught easily enough. 

“Do you mind?” I asked with a sigh.

Stalker just laughed, which turned into a pained cough.  “Shut the hell
up, Hebert.  We just fought Bastard Son for you, so excuse my twitchy
trigger finger.”

Alkaline rolled her eyes.  /“A convenient excuse.” /

/“Taylor would probably survive a shot to… most places,” / Sanguine
allowed.  /“So maybe it’s anger?” /

/“You think!?” /Ironsides retorted.

“Are you bleeding?” I asked, ignoring the byplay in my head.  “I can
help, if you want.”

I got the distinct feeling that Sophia blinked behind her mask.  “No,
I’m fine,” she said gruffly.  “Let’s go see what the hell happened.” 
She launched herself through the wall in a cloud of smoke, and I
followed her down with a teleport.

Browbeat and Vista joined us a moment later, leaping off of a roof that
was suddenly much shorter.  “What’s the word?” they asked, setting the
smaller Ward down.  “All done on your end?”  Vista sucked in a breath at
that, but was smart enough to keep her mouth shut.

“Yep.  Now, what’s this?”  Scanning the area for ‘strange things’ with
my bugs was tricky at best, but in this case I had been lucky.  A swarm
of ants brought a sparking piece of technology from nearby, dropping it
several yards away from where we were standing.  “Tinkertech?”

“Tinkertech,” Stalker agreed.  “Damn.”

I nodded slowly.  This was going to be a pain.  “Hey Teeth, the Elite
brought Tinkertech teleporters with them, possibly hidden.”

“Oh, so that’s what that was,” Reaver replied over the com.  “Might have
backups, too.”

“So what, we doin’ cavity searches now?” someone in group two asked,
triggering a round of snickers.

Vex jumped in with an immediate, “Get the heroes to do it.  They managed
to fit their heads up their own asses.”

The comment made me guffaw, and I had to wave off the heroes when they
gave me questioning looks.  “Look, I’ll leave you to your crime scene. 
I was in the middle of my own when Bastard Son showed his ugly mug.”

“That’s fair,” Browbeat said.    “Before you go, Console’s demanding to
know how close you were that you could just pop in like that.” 

I smirked, not that they could see it.    “Tell Clock to keep screaming,
because the answer is always ‘close enough’.” 

I twisted through that not-step and arrived back at the site of our
failed negotiations    While I was gone, the other Teeth secured the
capes, and I knew Lisa would call the PRT once we were done, but there
was one thing we intended to do. 

Imp was drawing on one of the Elite capes while Regent poked another
with his scepter.  Had she really brought a sharpie to a cape fight? 
Who was I kidding, of course she had.  The girl loved to live up to her
name, and she was proving it right now.

/“Oh, she did the grenades,” / Fester realized.  /“Damn.” /

/“Hell yeah she did!” / Pyro cheered.  /“That girl has style!” / 

“Huh, this one’s not a Changer,” Regent said, examining the first
casualty of the Elite’s foam attempts.    “I’m guessing Brute with pain
dampening or nullification.  Can I keep him?” 

“Ugh, that’s Sovereign,” Lisa said.    “Brute is right, but he has a
subrating of Changer or Stranger; the PRT are split on that.    He’s a
real piece of work, with a rap sheet almost as long as the Butcher as a
whole.” 

I couldn’t help but whistle, which was impressive as hell in a very
disturbing way.    “What sort of crimes?” 

“I wouldn’t lose sleep if Regent claimed him,” Lisa said with steel in
her voice, then eyed our own Changer.  “Or if Animos ate him.”  In
response, Animos let out an impressive belch.

“Pandemic?” I asked cautiously.    She was either still in Lisa’s lap or
at most next to her, and I wanted a second opinion.

“Yeah no,” the healer answered.    “If we didn’t have a better option, I
would say kill him.”

/“Something tells me that isn’t just our corrupting influence asserting
itself on the impressionable Panacea,” / Alkaline remarked.

“Show me.” 

Seconds of silence passed before my phone dinged, a single picture of
Lisa’s vast monitor setup showing the man’s open file.  Zooming in
proved to be a mistake as I instantly had a monstrous clamoring within
my skull demanding I kill the bastard.  The more I read, the more
disgusted I got over the whole thing. 

I drew my gun and fired two rounds into his skull. 

/“Christ, she actually did it!” /Butcher cheered.

Fester, however, snarled angrily.  /“Damn Brutes.” /

Aside from the minor scorching, his skull was perfectly intact — even
his hair seemed untouched by the explosive ammunition.  Pushing down the
roiling fury within me, I turned back towards Regent, who was now
standing alongside our newest recruit, Imp.  Right, she had been down
there helping deal with the rank and file.  Her power made it difficult
to track her at times, even with my weird sixth sense about her.

“Consider him a resource,” I said to the hidden Master.  “He forfeited
his humanity long ago.” 

Regent leaned over and patted the guy’s cheek.  “Hear that, fella?  Even
the Butcher thinks you’re scum.  I can’t wait to learn what you did to
set off that kind of reaction, because I’m going to have fun making you
live it yourself.” 

The declaration was made in the same casual tone Alec always used when
he spoke, and yet it sent a foreboding chill down my spine.  Promises
like that were nothing to scoff at, especially when delivered by a
member of Heartbreaker’s brood. 

/“Sucks to be him,” / Butcher said, wishing he could hawk a loogie on
the Brute. 

Pyro chuckled.  /“Please, he deserves whatever fucked up shit that kid
does.”  /

/That he does, / I agreed. 

Nobody should be able to do what he did and get away with it for so
long.  This was justice finally coming home to collect.  

Pity he only had one life to pay. 

 

------------------------------------------------------------------------

 

/“It’s really her,” /Reflex whispered, his voice trembling. 

/“Ha!  Reunited and you can’t do shit!” /Marauder mocked. 

I slammed him into the dark for it.   /Mocking someone for finally
meeting their loved one after literal decades trapped in our heads? 
What the fuck? /

/“Yeah, that’s a new low, even for you,” / Fester agreed.

Ashley Stillons had the dubious honor of being one of the dozen or so
living relatives of my predecessors; being related to the only hero of
us was offset by being a villain herself.  Not that I was judging — to
be honest, I was flattered that she came up to the Bay to meet me
following my letter on Reflex’s behalf.

However, friendly overtones or no, the young woman lounging on my sofa
like she owned the place was very obviously tense.  Every movement of
her hands was measured, and she was taking great care to keep her
fingers pointed away from me or the other Teeth.  I appreciated the
effort; Damsel of Distress had one the most destructive and poorly
controlled abilities I had ever read about.

In a fit of what I hoped was /not / drug-addled inspiration earlier this
week, Amelia had done /something / to Ashley’s hands that would help
with her control.  The effectiveness remained to be seen.

/“She obviously doesn’t want the power, or she would have just offed you
immediately,” / Knockout said unhelpfully.

/“Or she’s trying to determine just how sane Taylor is,” / Stratego rumbled.

Damascian huffed.  /“This girl does not strike me as a fool.  Such
proclivities are beneath her.  She is a wielder of guile.” /

I rolled my eyes, Ashley Stillons was many things, but straightforward
wasn’t one of them. 

/“Yeah, nothing straight about this one,” / Fester agreed.

If we needed any justification for that statement, I just needed to
follow Ashley’s line of sight.  She was ignoring all the room of
dangerous capes to stare at the framed picture of Victoria’s face from
when Amelia had revealed the identity of her sister’s hookup.  The
reaction had been spectacular.

“My thanks for sending the video of Victoria’s response, though I do
wish I had been able to reveal myself on my own time.”  Ashley gave her
wineglass a swirl — /“Where did she get that?” / — then focused her
attention back on me.  “You are not what I expected, Weaver.”

“Please, call me Taylor when I’m out of uniform,” I found myself saying,
the platinum-blonde villainess’ formality drawing some of Damascian’s
own speech patterns out of me.  “I take it you left Boston due to the
letter?”

Her answering smirk was rather distracting.  No wonder she had been able
to win over Victoria.  “Indeed.  Completely coincidentally, my partner
at the time decided that we would have a… rather explosive breakup.”

/“She didn’t,” / Alkaline muttered. 

Ashley then grinned.  “Bakuda wasn’t amused when I accidentally
vaporized half her lab.”

“You’re telling me the second Boston Games was caused by a lover’s
spat?” I asked, trying and failing to not gape at the scope of what
chaos had been unleashed. 

/“A truly bombastic, sapphic breakup at that!” /Pyro exclaimed.

“Bakuda has a delightful intensity, but she proved far too temperamental
for my goals.” Ashley said with a shrug. 

/“Why, because she goes off as easily as you do?” /Pyro sniped.

“And what goals are those?” I asked, casually shoving Pyro down into the
dark.  “Besides bedding Victoria, I mean.” 

Ashley snorted, cracking her mask for an instant.  “So upfront.  I can
appreciate that, so I shall honor you with the same.  I want to carve
out my own territory, to be a major player in the city I call home.” 

“Which will be Brockton Bay going forward?” 

“I imagine so, since there likely won’t be a Boston given another month
of the ongoing conflict.” 

I winced.  The fighting was still ongoing, now having lasted almost two
weeks with no signs of slowing.  Accord was backed into a corner and had
the cape advantage, but Bakuda’s bombs were a great equalizer.  A Brute
rating meant nothing when she could turn capes to glass.  That power had
been enough to gather capes under her banner and claim a third of the
city for her own, and she was poised to rout Accord for good. 

“Lisa had similar fears,” I admitted.  “Even with the heroes rotating
in, they are making little headway.  We’ve already had to run off the
Red Hand and Elite, and I think Damien won a bet now that you’re here.” 
I trailed off, watching her face as she studied me, there was a tension
there as though she was still expecting danger.  “You’re surprised that
my lucidity hadn’t lapsed during our conversation.” 

“It is certainly a surprise,” Ashley agreed, setting her glass down
carefully.  “Your predecessors retained the name ‘Butcher’ for a
reason.  The curse you have seemingly conquered claimed my uncle as its
first documented victim.” 

I nodded.  Reflex had been the first to experience the supposed madness
when he   suddenly had the screeching voices of two villains in his
head.  Butcher and Sanguine were friends out of costume, they were both
in agreement about leading the Teeth.  Reflex had not shared those
opinions, and so they tag teamed him and drove him mad. 

Nobody really understood what had happened, then Fester came along weeks
later and claimed the mantle.  She proved no more resilient to the
madness, and soon everyone knew then that killing the Butcher was to
doom oneself to the curse.  That I hadn’t fallen like my predecessors
was a miracle in itself, and people were slow to believe me. 

I really couldn’t blame them. 

“I won’t say that I haven’t been affected,” I began cautiously, “but
I’ve been the Butcher for a month now.  My most violent act remains the
murder of Kaiser for the attempt on my    father’s life.” 

“Your battle certainly seemed personal,” Ashley admitted.  “Family is
important after all.” 

“It is, which is why I’m protective of mine.  The Teeth are my family,
and I worry about them.  I’m their leader, and I take that
responsibility seriously.  I won’t stand for any threats to my family. 
So, tell me Ashley, are you a threat to my family?” 

“I am here on account of family,” she answered.  “Family I thought lost
forever.  I am certainly not here for the Teeth.” 

“Reflex,” I said.

“Yes.  Which makes us family in a way,” she replied. 

“I suppose it does,” I answered, finally pouring myself a glass of
wine.  “I’ll be honest, Ashley, I know you don’t want to join the Teeth,
which is why I’m offering you an alternative arrangement.” 

“I’m listening,” Ashley said cautiously. 

“The Teeth are out of people to fight here in the Bay,” I said, taking a
sip of wine.  “They’re getting restless and need an outlet.  Sure, we
have the Elite at present, but eventually people will stop trying to
take the city from us.  So, I need someone who is familiar with
mercenary work to get our foot in the door and Faultline can offer
that.  Normally I’d throw the problem at Lisa and call it a day, but
those two have some bad blood.  That’s where you come in.” 

“You want me to be your contact with Faultline.” 

I grinned.  “I do.  You’d technically work for both of us, she provides
you with jobs that might not suit her own team’s interests, and you pass
those along to us for the quest board.  Faultline gets a cut, you get a
cut, the team gets the rest.” 

“An… intriguing offer, I’ll admit,” she said, though it was difficult to
tell how seriously she was considering taking it.  “However, it hardly
suits my own goals.  I value my independence, a sentiment you likely
share, and I find the idea of subservience… repugnant.  I also find your
Teeth’s aesthetic distasteful as well, and associating myself with your
cabal of degenerates would cause undue harm to my own image. 
Devastating as my own power may be, I am not some mindless thug, and I
fail to see how you could possibly compensate me appropriately to lower
myself to your level.  So, what do I gain from this venture? Why should
I accept such an offer?” 

All fifteen Butchers blinked at that tirade, delivered in one of the
best ‘evil supervillain has the heroes at her feet’ voices we had ever
heard.  Still, I managed a little titter of amusement borrowed from one
of Damascian’s favorite British dramas for my own response.  “You’re
telling me you would turn down the club life being offered to you on a
silver platter like this?  The Teeth are only going to grow in number
and influence, and once Faultline gets a reputation for expanded
services, she’s going to be rolling in jobs and money.  If you accept
this offer, you would have power and influence within the city.  Amelia
is Teeth, despite what she claims, and Victoria is family by extension. 
Which now that I say it out loud sounds kinda creepy given your relation
to Reflex.”

/“Now I hope you never meet my parents,” / Chisel murmured, but Knockout
just guffawed.

/“Please call my brothers — they would love it here!” /

Ashley laughed at my bad attempt at humor.  “You would consider me
protected as family if I did this.  Which loops us back around to my
reason for coming to the Bay in the first place.” 

“You’re already family, Ashley.  I’m only offering you this opportunity
on account of that truth.  Your identity is flimsier than mine, yet your
relations aren’t well known outside our circles.  You need a clear tie
to our group simply to ensure the unwashed masses know you’re protected
by us.”  

Ashley scoffed, waving her wine glass dismissively.  “I do not need your
protection, nor do I wish to be tied down.”

“As I tell all of my capes, you are free to refuse my offer, or resign
at any moment.”

She arched a single white eyebrow.  “Even Lisa?  I understand she is
quite entwined with your operations now.”

/“She’s quite entwined with —” /  I gave Fester a shove, and she
devolved into laughter.

I let myself smile, because Ashley wasn’t wrong.  “Yes, even Lisa.  I
don’t keep the unwilling in my service — it’s bad for your lifespan.” 

“I suppose you would be concerned about that, given how many have held
your title before,” Ashley stated.  “I am assuming your approaching me
means there aren’t many suited within the Teeth at present?”

“You would be correct,” I said, letting out a frustrated sigh and
ignoring the chorus’ cheers.  “The Teeth aren’t the best when it comes
to administrative things.  I’ve gained people that are suited to that
over time, but as we expand I recognize that we need further assistance.” 

“Which you seek from me,” Ashley said with a sneer.  “Benefits or no, I
hardly feel like being a secretary.”

“You’re displaced from your home, you’re setting roots here.  I simply
wanted to offer you something to start over with.  You have ties to us
already, like it or not.  I won’t ask for an answer today, the offer
will remain open, as I don’t have anyone else in mind to fill it as of
present.  I digress, you are here to speak of family, would you like to
speak with him?” 

Beside our sitting area, a column of insects formed into a humanoid
shape.  It was old hat at this point, but it still surprised those not
used to it.  This would take focus, which is why I kept all the voices
silenced save one. 

/The floor’s all yours.  /

The clone’s head turned to me and nodded before turning back to the
tense girl seated across from me.  

“Hello Ashley,” Reflex said softly through the hum of a million insects.

 

------------------------------------------------------------------------

 

While those two caught up, I excused myself, keeping the entire thing in
the back of my mind where it didn’t feel like I was intruding too much. 
It had taken some practice to do this effectively — I was still aware of
them talking about Reflex’s family, but I was mostly able to ignore the
conversation.  That was made easier if I could focus on something else.

Across the room, Chrissie was leaning over the railing, watching a fight
in the pits.  I made a quick stop at the fridge to grab myself a wine
cooler and Chrissie her favorite beer before I stepped up beside her and
planted a kiss on her exposed shoulder that now bore a new tattoo. 

The design was rather blatant: a spider’s web with a large black widow
perched on the threads, the widow’s back bearing my number in red.  It
was her third Butcher themed tattoo: along the same arm were a quiver of
arrows set to resemble the numeral XIV and a set of knives resembling
XIII.  She had joined under Damascian, and can now boast to have seen
three Butcher’s reigns.  It was a distinction and a mark of honor among
the Teeth to carry that many with her. 

“It suits you,” I said softly. 

“Amelia does good work,” Chrissie answered with a grin.  “You should get
one too!”

I gave my girlfriend a flat look.  “I’m trying to not make it super
obvious.”

Chrissie rolled her eyes.  “Not having any tattoos makes you stand out. 
Even a giant XV on your back wouldn’t be too conspicuous.” 

“You’re just saying that because you want to show me off,” I replied,
matching her own toothy grin.

“Naturally we’ll need Parian to make you a backless dress to flaunt it.” 

“Naturally,” I agreed, clinking my bottle to hers.  “Maybe Amelia can
make it bioluminescent so it glows in the dark too.” 

“That would be fucking sweet!” 

We both laughed at the mental image as Michael stepped into the arena. 
He was in full gear and brought his weapon into the ring, which made the
Butchers perk up considerably from their place in the dark.  Across from
him, the Teeth herded a protesting Holdout into the arena, using two of
my hypersharp spears like cattle prods.  The soon-to-be-former Elite
cape had been stripped of his costume, but I doubted it would help him
against Michael.  

“Any progress with the Damsel?” Chrissie asked after a moment. 

I let out a frustrated sigh.  “I don’t think she’s going to accept the
offer.  Too proud.  She didn’t even want to associate with us.”

“Damn,” Chrissie said.  “Back to square one then.  What about sending
one of us?”

I gave the railing a few taps with my finger.  “Alice would be best
suited, but she has her hands full keeping everyone on task as it is. 
Damien won’t give up his drugs long enough to not be taken advantage of
in negotiations, and while Michael is a strong candidate, his maturity
leaves much to be desired.”

“Not even considering Elliot?” Chrissie asked with a smirk. 

I shook my head.  “He’s mellowed out since his challenge, but he’s
hardly a people person.  But… the added responsibility could do Michael
some good,” I mused.  “I’ll run it by him, see what he thinks of the idea.” 

“Does it have to be a cape?” my dad asked, joining us but pointedly
ignoring the fight about to happen below.  “Sorry, I overheard the last
bit of your conversation.”

“It helps them be taken seriously, and it doesn’t help that Faultline is
already cautious of the arrangement I proposed.  Meeting her in person
was quite the experience.” 

“You look conflicted Danny,” Chrissie said.

His eyes drifted over the common area, and he seemed to age five years
before answering.  “My daughter is affecting major changes across our
city, it’s a lot to take in.  I don’t think I’ll ever get used to this.” 

“I’m just glad you’re trying,” I said, giving him a one-armed hug.  “It
can’t be easy for you.” 

Dad hugged me back firmly.  “It would be harder if I lost you.” 

A hard impact drew our attention back to the arena beneath us.  Holdout
had just backhanded Reaver across the arena, and he had not landed
well.  Anger ignited within me at seeing one of my Teeth injured like that.

“Chrissie, hold my beer,” I said, passing it over to her and vaulting
down into the pit.  Holdout barely had time to turn around before I
twisted midair and kicked him in the side of the head.  “Round two,
motherfucker.”

/“More like round DONE!” / Knockout cheered. 

I let a smile come to my face as Holdout pulled himself to his feet, his
skin rippling as it became decidedly less human.  The roar of the crowd
sent shivers of excitement coursing through my veins, and a feral grin
curled on my lips.  I waited until he was fully transformed, towering
three feet over me and looking more like a walking volcanic mountainside
than a person. 

/“Where the fuck did the name Holdout come from?” / Pyro asked. 

Stratego tapped his chin.  /“He likely didn’t want his name to give away
too much about his own powers.” / 

/“Makes as much sense as anything else,” / Ironsides said in agreement. 

I rolled my neck, adjusting my own biology with Sabertooth’s power so
each motion made it crack.  My nails extended into claws and I let fangs
grow in as I grinned at my prey.  A quick pulse of the pain and rage
blasts showed him to be unaffected by those powers, which meant I got to
do this the old fashioned way.  I had no costume, no weapons — just me
and my bare hands versus a mountain.  A subtle check with bloodsight
showed nothing, so I instead flicked my eyes to be more animalistic. 

The chorus and crowd cheered as I took up a loose boxing-like stance;
above me, my dad was now gripping the railing with white knuckles.  My
swarm wouldn’t do much good against this bastard, but they could still
serve a purpose.  I had every fly and gnat I could spare help map out
his body to my senses.  Damasican’s combat precognition kicked in as a
shadow of the future began to move forward, enhanced by the feedback
from my bugs. 

My smile was savage and primal as I surged forward, ducking before the
shadow even passed over me and landing a quick flurry of blows into his
stone torso.  Holdout staggered back, and I pressed forward with my
attack.  A hard punch to the solar plexus did next to nothing, and
Fester’s touch worked like ass on stone.  Worse, it didn’t register as
inorganic to Chisel’s power.

/“Just fucking claw him!” / Sabertooth roared.  /“Enough of these
tricks!” / 

The lack of even my inconvenient powers made the fight all that more
exciting, and I danced around blows, lashed out in recompense, and
relished a fight that I couldn’t just steamroll.  Holdout was shouting
in inarticulate rage as I continued to hammer away at him while he
failed to land a single counter blow.  

Ever so slowly I was pushing him back towards the wall, and just before
he reached it, I set the trap.  He tripped on a surprise forcefield
behind his left leg, and I pounced as soon as he started to fall.  My
leap didn’t quite carry me above his head, but I still used my momentum
and lashed out with a punch empowered by every Brute package I had. 
Holdout’s head snapped back, bounced off the steel wall marking the edge
of our pits, and hit the ground with a thud. 

I landed atop Holdout’s fallen form and grabbed his arm, using my legs
for extra force as I pulled and twisted.  With the sound of an
avalanche, I wrested his arm free.  For the first time, Holdout screamed
in agony. 

I flipped his arm in the air and took hold of the wrist, a flicker of
disappointment passed through me when Chisel’s power still didn’t want
to touch it.  The stone wasn’t reverting, which gave me a marvelous new
tool.  I slammed his arm across the stone visage of his face.  Again. 
And Again.  Shrapnel splintered with each blow, chips and shards
impacting my skin with enough force that a non-Brute would have been
covered with cuts. 

I didn’t let up my assault against the man that had spat on my
hospitality, hurt my Teeth, and tried to capture me /again /.  I kept
going, even as his face turned to gravel, even as his form reverted back
to human.  One final swing and his skull caved like a festive
watermelon.  The crowd cheered as I held his arm over my head in
victory, blood dripping from the appendage as it too finally reverted
back to a mangled human limb.  I let out a primal roar as everyone
chanted my name.

The chorus was cheering too, my entire form now dripping with blood and
gore rather than stone and dust.  I couldn’t help but smile wider as
Chrissie wolf whistled, though my dad looked haunted.  Whatever — he
knew who I was, he had to accept that this was part of it.  

I was the Butcher, and I wasn’t going to let anyone forget it.

    similar in scope to Fistful that I plan to work between arcs of
    Inheritance as well.
