    Chapter 36: Interlude 4.l

Chapter Notes

See the end of the chapter for notes <#endnotes36>

/Saturday May 7th, 2011 /

The roar of the rotors sounded behind her, whipping her hair into a
frenzy that would no doubt be a pain to comb out later.  Lily wasn’t
sure when she would get the time — moving to a new city always started
with a bunch of activities that often stretched into the night.  She was
used to it, of course, as the PRT had shuffled her all over the country
over the course of her Wards career.

She had rarely stayed long enough in one place to make friends.

She hated it. 

Even now, coming to Brockton Bay for ‘joint training’ with the leader of
her NYC Wards team, she knew her transfer would be pushed through and
she’d once again be in a new city with barely an acquaintance to call
upon.  Sure, she’d already signed off on the plan, mostly because it let
her get away from Cass, but it still stung.

Hopefully turning eighteen would allow her some choice in the matter —
nobody sane wanted to be in the same city as the Butcher, especially
after such a gruesome live execution.  Not that Lily was going to cry
over a dead Nazi, but it did mean that the Teeth were the only
significant gang presence remaining in Brockton Bay.  

Lily had been to enough PR events to immediately realize that the
Protectorate were trying to show the flag, reminding the people that the
city wasn’t lost to the madness of the post-apocalyptic band of
cannibals.  Flooding the city with semi-famous capes was one way to do
it, though she wouldn’t be surprised if there was a new Butcher before
it was all said and done. 

How did one even fight someone like that?  Anything short of lethal was
ineffective and lethal force just made the Butcher stronger.  Lily
didn’t even want to consider what the Butcher would become if she
herself wound up killing them, never mind the thought of fifteen
screaming murderers in her head.

She couldn’t help but wonder if Cass had managed to get her on the short
list for this shit assignment. 

…

That was hateful and more than a bit unfair.  Lily tried to not throw
all of her heartache on her ex, but they did have one hell of a messy
breakup.  Best not to dwell on it, though — Lily was in Brockton for a
purpose, and that meant meeting the local Wards team.  She followed her
fellow Lancer Team member and captain to the elevator.

“Jouster, good to see you again,” a brawny man in red said — Aegis, if
Lily remembered correctly.  At this point, all of the briefing packets
ran together in her head.

“You as well,” Jouster responded, clasping wrists with his counterpart
as men often did.  

Aegis released his grip and his smile fell away, opening the elevator
for their little group.  Lily followed Jouster, Aegis, Shadow Stalker,
Vista and Kid Win (she wondered who approved that name) into the
elevator, only for the red-clad Brute to let out an explosive sigh.  
“Look, I’m really glad you guys are here, don’t get me wrong.  Even
though we’re just waving the flag, we can really use any help we can get.”

“We’re happy to be here,” Jouster tried, but Aegis shook his head.

“I’ll be blunt.  The brass is scared shitless of Weaver and I can’t say
they’re wrong.  In the last month, the Teeth have… let’s say ‘removed’
all other major gang presences from the city.  Everyone is worried the
PRT is next.”

Jouster chuckled, though it sounded forced.  “Thanks for being honest. 
I had a feeling that the situation here had degenerated.” 

“It could be worse,” Aegis stated.  “Weaver and her Teeth have yet to
even target any heroes outside of our own causing them grievous
injuries.  Even then, they never needed more than a few minutes with
Panacea to be back on their feet.”

“Not to mention the Teeth have publicly declared Panacea as sacrosanct,”
Kid Win said.  “They /claimed / it was so that they could keep robbing
rich tourists, but…”

“But what?” Lily asked.  “I mean, that’s not the Teeth’s usual MO, but I
guess I can see it.”

The Brockton Wards squirmed slightly, and an uneasy feeling settled in
the elevator.  “There’s, uh, extenuating circumstances,” Kid Win
replied.  “But they said anyone who messed with her would envy Kaiser.”

Well, that was a chilling threat.  /Note to self, don’t flirt with the
cute healer even to tease her. /

“Now that does sound like the Teeth,” Jouster said as the elevator doors
opened with a ding to reveal a hall with a large door at the end. 
“Luckily for you guys, I have quite a lot of experience fighting those
maniacs.  I’m sure that —”

“What makes you think we’ll be fighting the Teeth?” Shadow Stalker
sneered, causing the whole group to pause in the hallway and spin on
her.  “Don’t look at me like that.  Everyone here knows the truth — the
PRT aren’t afraid of Weaver.  They’re afraid of Weaver making them look
bad.”

“Stalker, don’t —” Aegis tried.

“Or what?” the other Ward retorted acidly.  “I’m already on the PRT’s
shit list because I fucked up and messed with Weaver in civvies. 
Nothing you or anyone can say or do will ever compare to that.”

“What!?” Lily blurted, mind reeling at the idea of the Butcher in
civvies.  “How are you still alive?”

Shadow Stalker gave an exaggerated shrug and started back down the
hallway.  “No fuckin’ clue.  But Weaver didn’t care when I tagged along
with Browbeat on their early morning patrol, so I guess we’re friends now.”

“Wait, you knew that the Elite were there?” Vista demanded, taking a
power-assisted step in front of the door and crossing her arms.  Lily
thought that the gesture looked a little silly on the younger girl, but
there was real heat in her voice.  “I thought you got stuck on that
because Miss Militia wasn’t around to go with Browbeat on their crazy
morning thing?”

Shadow Stalker snorted, then hit the mask-up alarm attached to the
door.  “Hell no.  And before you ask, no, we didn’t know Bastard Son was
there.”

“Bastard Son is here too?” Jouster demanded.  “And what do you mean,
‘friends?’  Why would Butcher care or even know about Wards patrol
routes?  Just what the hell is going on here?”

“I wish I knew,” Aegis muttered.  Lily really wasn’t sure what to make
of that admission, and going by what she could see of Jouster’s face, he
didn’t know either.  Lily had only fought the Teeth a few times, but
that was more than enough to know that they were not the type of people
to be reasoned with.

Then again… Lily /had / read the Butcher’s AMA.  The responses had not
read like the crazed ramblings of fifteen pounds of insane murderer in a
one pound bag.  No, they had read like a /teenager /, albeit one with
far too much experience in cape life for being about Lily’s age.  There
had also been an abundance of dry wit and amused confidence that just
screamed ‘look at my new public persona’ that frankly disturbed Lily
when applied to Butcher XV.

When the door opened to reveal the rest of the Wards team, Lily’s
immediate thought was ‘not enough girls.’  Browbeat, Gallant, and
Clockblocker rounded out the local team; they were joined by Tecton and
Cuff from Chicago and Weld from Boston.  Aegis did a round of
introductions, followed by the customary unmasking.

Lily was then treated to the Changer Surprise when Browbeat started to
deflate, having clearly forgotten part of the briefing packet again. 
With Madison’s reveal as a petite and /really / cute girl, at least the
gender ratio in the Wards ENE had moved mostly equalized.

“So, let’s talk about the elephant in the room,” Everett (Tecton) said
once the initial pleasantries had tapered off.  Martin (Jouster, and
never ‘Marty’), Weld, and Carlos all gave him nods, and the Tinker made
an immediate beeline for a whiteboard.  “Now, I’ve never dealt with the
Teeth myself, so I’m obviously lacking context.”  He picked up a marker
and considered it for a moment.  “At the same time, it means I’m here
without any preconceptions.  A fresh look.”

“You did read Weaver’s AMA,” Ava (Cuff, and rather cute) pointed out
with a laugh.

“Has anyone /not / read that?” Lily asked as Everett started writing on
the board, dividing it into four quadrants.  “I mean, it must have been
the craziest thing on PHO all year.”

Martin groaned in annoyance, but the rest of the group made various
sounds of agreement.  “Good,” Everett said.  The board had been divided
into two rows, ‘PRT’ and ‘Teeth’, along with two columns, ‘Goals’ and
‘Opposition.’  In the Teeth goals box, he immediately wrote ‘Prove
Weaver is sane.’

“You have to be fucking kidding me!  Do you have any idea —” Martin
snapped, only to be cut off by Weld raising his hand.

“At the risk of letting our strong emotions on the subject get the
better of us, I want to voice my agreement with Martin.  This is the
Butcher we’re talking about.”

Lily also wanted to agree, but she had been surreptitiously checking out
Madison and Sophia — both of them had nodded along with Everett’s
description.  Everett obviously noticed too, turning back to the
whiteboard and writing ‘Stability’ under the PRT’s goals and ‘Butcher is
crazy’ under Teeth opposition.  “These are just my opinions after doing
some research, so feel free to correct me.”

“Put ‘murder’ under the Teeth goals,” Martin snapped.  “Or ‘sell drugs,’
or whatever awful thing they’re doing today.”

Sophia rolled her eyes dramatically.  “If you’re going to be a dick like
that, then put ‘sell merch’ under the PRT’s goals, because that’s
clearly all they give a shit about around here.”  Ava and Everett gave
her shocked looks, and Sophia threw her hands up in disgust.  “Hey,
Weaver kills Nazis.  We don’t.  Do the fucking math.”

“She also has been recruiting capes,” Dean said, and Everett wrote that
down.  “Usually the Teeth expand by finding, um, like-minded people. 
But Weaver has absorbed the Undersiders, and Tattletale hasn’t killed
anyone as far as we know.”

“The Thinker, right?” Lily asked.

“Yeah, Thinker 7 officially,” Chris said, “though Assault keeps saying
it should be a 5 after she missed Panacea being in the bank.” 

“Is that why Assault’s page on the Protectorate website keeps getting
hacked?” Dennis asked with a smile.

“She did that as cover for restoring her rating after the whiteboard
incident,” Chris replied.  “She also changed Weaver’s rating to ‘fuck
around and find out.’” 

“That checks,” Shadow Stalker said, annoyed, then phased through one of
the dorm doors without further explanation.

“What happened to her?” Ava asked. 

Madison barely glanced up from her phone.  “She found out.”

The comment hung in the room for a long minute, which gave Sophia enough
time to change into exercise clothes and ghost back into the common
area.  Lily’s eyes immediately snapped to the athletic girl’s fitted
blue-gray tank top emblazoned with the PRT logo and white athletic
shorts, noting that at least /some / of the Wards here took physical
training seriously.  It was worrying that Sophia was leaving the
meeting, but Lily loved watching her go.

“Is she going to be okay?” Martin asked, giving Lily a knowing (and
unimpressed) look.  “This is kind of important…”

“Yep, this is normal,” Dennis said flippantly.  “She’s our resident
honey badger with a very unique view on life and love.”  The last was
definitely aimed at Lily, who blushed before turning her attention back
to the whiteboard.

“And violence,” Missy added with a hint of bitterness.  “The Teeth
aren’t the only people who maim Nazis.”

Lily opened her mouth to say something suitably heroic, but what came
out was, “That’s alright, I wouldn’t be allowed to come here if the
Empire was still around.”

Madison barked out a laugh at the comment, then devolved into further
giggles when the more responsible Wards shot her annoyed glares. 
Madison waved them off, though Lily didn’t miss the apocalyptic heat of
the glare Missy was sending Madison’s way. 

“No, they aren’t,” Missy muttered, but enough heard it that it stilled
the room. 

Madison sat bolt upright in a clear challenge to the pint sized Shaker. 
“Don’t even start.  Yes, I’ve gone out and fucked up Nazis.  As most of
you have refused to notice, I’m not exactly cis here.” 

“Non-binary?” Lily guessed, a bit taken back by the outburst. 

“More gender fluid thanks to my powers,” Madison said, wiggling her hand
as her form shifted again, but not to the masculine Browbeat.  No, this
person looked decidedly like they could be Madison’s twin brother. 
“Unfortunately,” wow, that was a deep voice, “PR doesn’t like the fact
that I can shift form so completely, so the Browbeat persona was the
compromise we reached.  They/them are preferred when I take that form.” 

“Noted,” Ava said, looking rather uncomfortable with the whole thing. 
“I can understand the animosity you probably had with the Nazis then.” 

“Animosity doesn’t even begin to describe it,” the Changer said,
standing up and walking off.  “Let me know when it’s time to go play PR
mascot again, I’ll be in the gym with Sophia.” 

“Right,” Everett said, trying to get the meeting back on track.  “Let’s
talk about the event in the park this afternoon…”

Lily only listened with half of her brain.  The other half was wondering
just what the hell she had been signed up for in this town.

 

------------------------------------------------------------------------

 

Lily had rarely been in such a strange briefing as the one she had just
escaped by put into an equally strange PR event.  No matter how much
everyone had hemmed and hawed as Everett filled up the white board with
unpleasant facts — or yelled, for that matter — it seemed that the
Chicago Ward had been right on the mark with the powder keg that was
Brockton Bay.

The first shocking realization was that they needed a separate
‘Protectorate’ row from the PRT.  The former was explicitly working
towards descelation and stability, while the latter may have blown the
only chance to bring the Butcher’s power to the side of the heroes.

The second was that Teeth weren’t actively trying to light the powder
keg while sitting on it.  Madison and Sophia had, with some reluctance,
admitted that they knew Weaver’s civilian identity.  According to them,
Weaver was very invested in keeping her civilian life intact, and thus
unlikely to start stuff — especially while Legend was in town.

The third (and thankfully final) realization was that Legend and the
rest of the Protectorate bigwigs basically agreed with Everett’s
assessment, commending him on doing his research and reiterating that
they were here on a peacekeeping mission.  Internally, they wanted to
show Weaver that the Protectorate was serious about enforcing order in
the city while simultaneously not blowing up Teeth HQ.

Externally…

“Thank you Miss Flech-etty!” the girl said, taking the signed postcard
and running back to her waiting mom.  Lily gave them a little wave
before turning to the next fan, a teenage boy in a Protectorate shirt. 
He handed over the postcard with a mumbled greeting, trying and very
obviously failing not to check Lily out in her costume.

“So, anything you want to know about the heroes?” she asked, giving the
boy a PR-approved smile.  “You Brocktonites seem to have so many questions.”

He stammered out a negative, followed by thanks for her autograph, which
made their interactions one of the shortest so far.  In New York, Lily
often found that there was this unbridgeable distance between the normal
people and the heroes, largely due to the way that the PR machine put
the latter on a pedestal.  That made these sorts of events awkward as
all hell — Lily hated feeling like an outcast by kids her age, just
because she had powers.

In Brockton Bay, however, people were relatively fearless.  Lily chalked
it up to the reality of living in one of the most cape-dense parts of
the country, where supervillains were just a fact of life and the
Protectorate lived out on a goddamn oil rig.  Sophia’s attitude had
pissed Martin off something fierce, but Lily certainly didn’t feel like
some untouchable paragon of virtue when interacting with the people here.

Case in point, there was a tall, wiry ravenette arguing with Jouster and
Cuff right now, arguing about some technical details of powers and the
history of capes in Boston.  That would never have happened in New York,
and Lily knew that Jouster would be lamenting being unable to get the
girl’s number when they were done.  Even Cuff seemed to be getting into
their discussion, which was notable given her nerves.

It certainly did not hurt that the girl was pretty good-looking.

“Flechette, right?”  Lily was pulled out of her daydreaming by a voice,
turning to give a smile to the redheaded punk girl who had walked up to
her.  “Cool name.  Whatcha think of the Bay?”

Punk redhead had an alarming collection of scars on her face and hands,
and Lily absently wondered what her jacket covered apart from seriously
impressive biceps.  “It’s refreshing,” she replied.  “I arrived this
morning, so I haven’t had the chance to see much.”

“Well, I hate to be the bearer of bad news,” the girl said with a wink,
“but we don’t have parties like this all the time.”

‘Party’ was one word for it — with the arrival of Wards ostensibly for
‘cross-training,’ the PRT had arranged for a two-day long meet-and-greet
fair/party that took up the entirety of a major park near downtown. 
Lily suspected that Glenn Chambers had been largely responsible for the
event, given how much it mirrored smaller events in New York.

What the PRT’s spin master did /not / arrange, however, was the food
trucks.  A veritable fleet of the things had appeared right before
lunch, each of them presenting the correct paperwork to set up shop on
the streets across from the park.  Lily had discovered this despite
eating at the PRT base before the event.

Of course, when a bunch of food trucks appeared from all over the
northeast repainted in scarlet and gray, the PRT was obviously going to
get involved.  None of the heroes were particularly pleased to be
providing the entertainment at a party catered by the Teeth.

“It’s certainly a production,” Lily agreed.  “Did you want an
autograph?  Or to ask a question?”

For some reason, that brought a grin to the redhead’s face, and Lily
wasn’t totally sure she liked it.  “Nah, thanks though.  It’s just fun
to meet heroes, and my friends are busy talking your teammates’ ears
off.”  She waved lazily towards Jouster, where a cute blonde girl had
joined the discussion.  Lily noted that both girls had their hair in
complicated braids.

The redhead made some more smalltalk before wandering away, and Lily had
maybe a minute of respite before the next fan approached.  It was
another teenage boy, but unlike the last one, he was very excited to
talk to Lily about her powers and power interactions.  Unfortunately, he
was wrong about almost all of it, forcing Lily to attempt to gently
correct his misconceptions one at a time.

It was exhausting, but he eventually moved on to harassing Ava.  Lily
felt a little bad for her, but at least he wasn’t bothering her with
crack PHO theories anymore.  Up next was a demure young woman with
tanned skin and black hair, sporting a smile that set her chest aflutter.  

“Hello, Flechette,” the woman said, offering an adorable curtsy.  “I’m
glad I got to see you today.” 

“You are?” Lily blurted, cursing her traitorous mouth as she cleared her
throat.  “I mean, it’s always nice to meet a fan.” 

“I was hoping to be a bit more than a fan,” the woman murmured with a
giggle.  Damn, this woman was actually flirting with her!  “We do have a
date planned for later this evening, after all.” 

Oh shit, this cutie was Parian!  Lily hadn’t expected the rogue to just
walk up like this after her message about avoiding the fair to maintain
her image of neutrality.  Civvies was certainly an acceptable work
around and her choice of outfit was rather appealing. 

“You aren’t worried about people overhearing you?”  Lily asked, dropping
the PR voice for something more subtle. 

“With the Nazis gone, why would I?” she asked, sounding genuinely
confused.  “Didn’t someone explain the Rules to you when you arrived?” 

Lily glanced around, watching as the ravenette giggled at something
Jouster said.  Lily was honestly wondering if that girl would end up
with his actual number before this was all said and done.  He’d done so
once before, which had caused a mountain of headaches and NDAs to be
thrown around when they crashed and burned less than a week later. 

“I mean, the rules in New York were mostly enforced by Legend.  The last
time a Ward was attacked out of costume, Legend dropped the entire New
York Protectorate on their ass.” 

Sabah nodded, her smile turning hard.  “Same thing happens here, only
it’s the Teeth… and at least they buy my stuff.” 

That was the second time Lily was hearing that from a local, and it
wasn’t hard to agree after the whole thing with the resident Nazis. 
Weaver ripped that move right out of Legend’s playbook, just with a
characteristic Teeth level of violence added on.  To Lily’s amazement
and horror, Madison and Sophia knew Weaver in civvies, so maybe she
could ask them for a more detailed rundown once back on base for the
night.  

Lily turned her attention back to Sabah, who was studying the curves of
her costume with unrestrained longing.  Smiling at being caught, Sabah
pulled a small card from her pocket and handed it to Lily.  It was a
business card for ‘The Doll House’ and held an address and phone number,
with the addition of red lip prints on it. 

“Be seeing you, cutie,” Sabah said with a wink and slipped out of line.

Or in the morning.  Learning more about Weaver could definitely wait
until the morning. 

 

------------------------------------------------------------------------

 

While the PR fair event would run until sundown, the Wards were let off
early with the intention that they engaged in some out-of-costume
bonding activity.  Lily was actually looking forward to the experience
for once, and not just because there were cute girls on the local team. 
Indeed, she suspected that she was going to be in the Bay for longer
than usual, which would hopefully give her the chance to make some real
friends.

“Honestly, I would need to ask a… friend about bookstores,” Madison
admitted with a sigh as they walked back towards the park.  “She’s the
nerdy one at school and is a literature nut to boot.”

“Is she cute?” Martin asked with a smirk.  “I mean, I’m mostly asking
for Lily, but…”  The jibe got a few chuckles out of the group, including
Lily herself.

“Hey, I wouldn’t say no to meeting cute girls either,” Dennis added.

Ava rolled her eyes.  “Can we worry about getting Lily a date /after /
dinner?  I’m not sure about you guys, but I’m hungry and those
sandwiches earlier weren’t enough.”

The group murmured in agreement at that, though in truth Lily didn't
need help in that regard right now.  Sabah had given her a card for her
soon-to-open shop, which had been made possible by a donation from a
local business owner that was interested in seeing neutral capes succeed
without falling under either the PRT or the Teeth.  They were going to
have a bit of tea before heading downtown to eat at one of the most
expensive restaurants in town.

The other Wards didn’t need to know about Lily’s plans, however, not yet
at least.  She could brag after the fact, but for now that didn’t mean
she couldn’t look whenever someone pointed out a cute girl to her.  It
wasn’t like Brockton Bay had any shortage of those, even the briefing on
the Teeth roster had been rather distracting at times. 

A flash of white in the corner of Lily’s eye had her scanning the sky —
looking up was a necessary habit in New York.  It was Glory Girl, flying
with a civilian in her arms; Lily watched as the two of them touched
down somewhere in the park.  Madison was also watching the local
celebrity flier, and her expression turned cryptic when Lily caught her eye.

“So what is it really like, living with the Teeth?” Ava asked suddenly.

“Were you not paying attention at the briefing?” Martin replied, only
for Ava to groan in annoyance.

“That’s not… not what I meant.  We all know that the PRT doesn’t tell us
everything, and hearing the news from the outside is really different
than…”  Ava gestured around with two hands.  “It’s like the people who
say ‘come to Chicago for the food, stay because you were murdered.’”

“With the Butcher, you were murdered because you /were / the food,”
Martin started, only for Madison to cut him off.

“That was once and Marauder was high on bath salts,” they said,
exasperated.  “Ava is right — people overexaggerate and fling a lot of
shit, but it’s really not that bad.  Yeah, the Teeth are violent, but
they’re not Nazis and not sex slavers.  Weaver has them, well, not
contained /per se /, but at least less immediately likely to burn down
the city.”

“A ringing endorsement,” Martin grumbled.

Lily didn’t share Martin’s skepticism, though neither did she share
Madison’s flippency.  What she had seen of the Bay wasn’t in great
shape, but that wasn’t the Teeth’s fault… and they did kick out the
Empire.  The Teeth weren’t likely to harass her on the sidewalk, but
Lily had seen the results of their clashes in New York with other gangs
and she wasn’t eager to repeat the experience.

“What sort of villains do you have in Chicago?” Dennis asked, obviously
looking to change topics.  Ava seemed happy enough to oblige, telling
stories about a group called the Folk and the issues they caused.  It
carried the group until they arrived at the food trucks, at which point
everyone split up.

While waiting in line for pizza at her favorite (if suspiciously
repainted) pizza truck from New York, Lily once again caught sight of
the unreasonably attractive Glory Girl.  Perhaps unsurprisingly, she was
surrounded by a crowd of adoring fans, but Lily’s attention was
eventually drawn to the girl in civvies standing slightly apart from the
flying brick.  The displeased, freckled other girl had fans of her own,
and it took Lily a long minute of staring to realize that the girl was
Panacea.

“Hey, you want some pizza or what?”

Right, New Yorkers.  Lily grabbed her pizza and made her way towards the
picnic area, discovering that Martin and the others had picked a table
next to a cute girl with a small army’s worth of food in front of her. 
Said girl was munching on an onion ring with an amused expression on her
face when Lily walked up, and the Ward froze when she recognized the
girl as the cape geek from earlier.

This was a bad idea.

“Who’s this?” Lily asked as she sat down.  Bad idea or no, she would
still be polite.

“Lily, meet Taylor.  She’s the friend I was talking about earlier,”
Madison replied.  “The literature fan who can tell you about bookstores.”

“She’s also a hell of a cape geek,” Martin added with a smile.  “I was
asking her about some of the heroes here today and she knows more than
anyone I’ve ever met.”

“I’m not anyone special, I just read between the lines on the PHO wiki,”
Taylor retorted.  “And good choice, going for Gino’s.  Better than
anything local, that’s for sure.”

Lily blinked.  Was Taylor flirting with her now, too?  “Yeah, it's my
favorite.”

“So you’ve been to New York?” Martin asked.

Taylor nodded.  “Once or twice, for work.  Community organizing, before
you ask.”

“That’s awesome,” Martin said.  “I’ve done some of that myself…”

Lily couldn’t help but frown at Taylor’s answer, since the other girl
seemed much too young to have a job that would require her to travel
like that.  Had Lily been that far off the mark about her age?  Thoughts
for later; Lily was honestly looking forward to seeing how Martin would
try to talk around being a Ward.  Unfortunately, they were interrupted
by three girls making a beeline for the other table.  

“Hey Taytay!” the redhead from earlier said, and she was followed by a
very attractive blonde girl with green eyes.

The third was Panacea.

Strangely, they all had their own food, leaving Taylor to her veritable
feast.  The blonde girl saw Lily’s confusion and snorted.  “Don't be
that surprised.  Taylor conquered Fugly Bob’s Challenger recently.”

“That’s impressive,” Martin said immediately.  “Oh, I’m Martin, by the way.”

As Lily hid her jealousy at Taylor’s metabolism, a full round of
introductions followed.  Ava did a double-take when Amelia (not Amy,
apparently) gave her name.  

“Wait,” the Chicago Ward said.  “Amelia… Dallon?  You’re Panacea?”

“No,” Amelia replied, completely deadpan.  “I’m Pandemic.”

The whole table burst into laughter at that, including Madison doing a
spit take that barely avoided spraying Lily with Coke.  The only person
who wasn't amused, naturally, was Martin.  “That’s not funny,” he said
seriously.  “You’re an amazing hero, and it’s an insult that the Teeth —”

“Given that it’s my name, I’m allowed to decide for myself if it’s
insulting or not,” Amelia replied acidly.

“Taylor, back me up here,” he tried, but Taylor shook her head.

“Sorry, she’s the internationally famous cape.  I’ll defer to her
judgment.” 

“Sooo… has anyone read any good books lately?” Dennis asked, looking
slightly frazzled.

“Tay got me to start the Black Company,” Chrissie said.  “A bit rough at
the beginning but it gets pretty good.”

Ava brightened up at that.  “Oh, I just finished the first book!  I
expected dark fantasy, but that was a bit much even for me.”

Lily had not read the books, so she checked out of their conversation
and focused on her pizza.  After a few bites, Lisa leaned over and
asked, “How do you like the Bay so far?”

“So far?” Lily replied, confused.

“Well, you’re obviously not from around here with that accent.”  The
blonde shrugged and gestured with a French fry.  “New York, obviously,
but I hear some west coast in there, too.”

“I’ve, um, moved around a lot,” Lily replied.  That was one of the perks
of being an orphan and Ward of the state in both terms of the word. 

Lisa nodded.  “Well you’ve picked a good time to come here, now that the
Empire and ABB have both been exterminated.”  Her following wink made
it /very / clear to Lily why the Empire being gone was good.

Of course, Martin had to break out of his conversation to object to
that.  “Sure, but they were replaced by the Teeth, who are equally bad!”

“As a lesbian who almost got shanked at school by Nazis for being gay
and was rescued by Weaver, you can go fuck yourself,” Chrissie said with
fake lightness.

“No way,” Ava sputtered.

“Yes way,” Madison said while gesturing with their chili dog at Chrissie
and Taylor.  “We go to school together.  That actually happened.”

Having a Ward confirm a story that absurd took some of the wind out of
Martin’s sails, and Taylor followed up with, “The Teeth aren’t quite as
bad as you think.”

“That seems to be a common opinion among a lot of the local people we’ve
met,” Ava said before glancing at Dennis.  “Not everyone of course, but
enough to make me curious as to why.”

“That’s simple,” Lisa said, her smile growing.  “The people happy the
Teeth are in charge are mostly a part of the LGBT community, or aren’t
white.” 

“No more hate crimes,” Madison said with a nod.  “Pretty big perk right
there.” 

“Plus,” Taylor said with a full mouth, quickly swallowing.  “Weaver
defends her own, and the entire city now qualifies.” 

“Even with all the heroes here?” Ava asked, gesturing to the fair
surrounding them.  “Seems to me the Teeth aren’t as in control as you
think.” 

“Then why haven’t the heroes walked into the Teeth arena and demanded
their surrender?” Chrissie asked.  “Unlike the Nazis, the Teeth never
hid away in the dark.” 

“Quite right,” Taylor agreed, pecking a kiss on the girl’s cheek.  Damn,
Martin never stood a chance, did he?  “Also, we can do that in public
without worry, unlike how things were just a month back, all because of
the Teeth.” 

“That doesn’t change what the Teeth are,” Martin bit out, possibly
forgetting that he was trying to flirt with Taylor.  “Why defend the
savages like this?”

In response, Taylor stuck out her hand like she was looking at her
nails.  Lily’s breath caught when two black spiders with red accents
crawled out of her sleeve and started winding around her fingers, and
then nearly choked when they started playing pattycake with each other.  

“No particular reason,” she said offhandedly.

The table full of heroes froze at the little display, and it wasn’t
until Taylor put the spiders back in her hair that Martin jumped to his
feet and spluttered, “Y-you!  You… you’re the —”

“Hey, we’re trying to eat here,” Amelia snapped.  “Sit down and shut up.”

Before anyone could respond, Lisa added, “And don’t do anything stupid
like calling the heroes.  Weaver is rather particular about the
Unwritten Rules.”

While Martin continued to gawk and splutter, Lily turned her attention
to the other three Wards.  Ava looked just as shocked and horrified as
Lily felt, as did Dennis, but Madison was… not surprised at all?  Oh
right, they had mentioned knowing Weaver in  civvies before.  Why the
hell had Madison allowed a cluster of Wards to just casually sit down at
a table with literally the Butcher?

Something must have shown on Lily’s face, because Madison’s lips quirked
into a self-deprecating smile.  “What?  Everything I told you is still
true.  It just explains why she’s such a cape geek.”

“And how she can eat like that and keep her sexy bod, right Tay?”
Chrissie said, pinching at Taylor’s waist.  A few PHO snippets and
pictures went through Lily's head, and she almost choked a second time. 
Chrissie was almost certainly Vex, which made Lisa… Tattletale?

Then why was she holding Amelia’s hand —

Oh.  Shit.

Martin drew the connection at the same time.  “No.  No, this is wrong. 
Panacea is a hero, I'm calling the PRT, you must have Mastered her.”

Taylor rolled her eyes and pulled out her phone.  “Then use mine,
because at least I’ll have a recording of them laughing at you.  You
don’t seriously think the Protectorate doesn’t know about me?  They
literally shot up a sleepover at my house.”

“And did you just imply that I’m an insect?” Amelia asked sarcastically.

“Taylor’s power covers more than just insects,” Lisa pointed out. 
“Spiders, for example.”

“Wait, spiders aren’t insects?” Ava blurted, then winced when Taylor
glanced in her direction.

“Nope.  Same phylum, different class.”  Then Taylor — no, Butcher XV,
Lily had to remember — turned her attention back to her meal, pointedly
ignoring Martin as he just gaped at her.  Frankly, Lily wasn’t far off
herself, but it was just so hard to reconcile the cute, nerdy girl in
front of her with the east coast’s insane boogeyman.

Well, boogiegirl, at least, because /holy shit / Butcher really was a
fifteen year old girl.  Taylor was younger than Lily herself!

Oh, and Lily had totally been flirting with the Butcher.  Fuck.

They ate in shocked, uncomfortable silence for a few minutes while
Martin murmured into his phone, at least until he yelled, “What do you…
no, no.  No, don’t hang up on—”

“Told you,” Lisa said with a smug smile.  “If it helps, the PRTeam is
just as displeased with the situation as you are.  Why do you think we
have all these visiting bigwigs?”

“They’re pissy that we’ve set ourselves up like the Elite, which we’re
also keeping out of the city,” Taylor said casually between bites. 
“We’re their best option and they know it.” 

“Then why did they bring in Legend and friends?” Lily asked. 

“They don’t want people to think they lost control of the city.  They're
the PRTeam for a reason.” 

“Shame they couldn’t find this kind of support when they were dealing
with literal Nazis,” Lisa added. 

“Yeah, an LGBT-heavy gang kicks the Nazis to the curb and suddenly its
all hands on deck,” Amelia said heatedly.  “It’s a fucking disgrace.” 

“Yes, the heroes should be quite ashamed,” Chrissie added with a snicker. 

“Play nice,” Taylor said and Lily found herself gulping at the tone. 

Lisa pouted at the Butcher of all people.  “Let me have my fun, Tay.” 

Madison snorted.  “Your version of fun usually leads to years of
mandatory therapy.” 

Lisa shrugged.  “Dean will get over it, not my fault his parents were
Nazi supporters and he defended them.” 

“Or that he tried to help them muscle in on Medhall,” Amelia added.  “Or
that I was borderline suicidal and he chose to ignore it…”

Dean, aka Gallant, whose coming transfer suddenly made sense.

Amelia’s comment dumped a bucket of cold water on the argument between
the Teeth as all the girls seated on that side of the table drew Amelia
into a hug.  Part of Lily was concerned that Madison seemed to be on
such familiar terms with the villains; no doubt Martin would give their
superiors a full debrief once back on the rig.  

Dennis eventually restarted the conversation with a question of his
own.  “What do you actually want, then?”

“That is a complicated question,” Weaver said with a teasing smile and a
vicious glint to her eyes.  Oh no, why did Lily find that so hot? 
“Overall, I want my city to be peaceful.  The Teeth can keep the rest of
the gangs out and maintain a status quo that hasn’t been seen here in my
lifetime…  Ugh, I said /my / lifetime, you assholes.” 

Right, no matter what else, no matter how calm and rational she could
pretend to be, Taylor still had fourteen killers sharing brain-space
with her.  There was no way to know just how much influence they had
over her, even if she could maintain the illusion of control.  Just
watching the videos that came out during her first week after killing
Quarrel were enough to convince anyone that Weaver had changed fast and
hard from a timid girl into a hardened killer that showed no fear. 

“I can’t deal with this,” Martin declared before stalking away.  The
heroes watched him go; the Teeth didn't seem to give a fuck.  Lily
realized that the (far too friendly) villains were likely aware that she
and her friends were capes, which made Butcher’s nonchalance even more
frightening.  She simply didn't register them as a threat.

Or… she really believed that she could uphold the Unwritten Rules,
basically by herself.

A traitorous part of Lily's mind noted that those Rules and a lack of
Nazis would make it much easier to date as a lesbian and cape.  A glance
at Amelia and Lisa’s joined hands, and that traitorous part became much
louder.

Chrissie had been watching Martin storm off, and once he was gone her
face split into a sharp grin.  “So Tay, did he actually give you his
number?” 

Taylor produced a slip of paper from her pocket, much to the horror of
Lily and the other Wards that weren’t clearly familiar with Weaver.  She
waved it around, put it back in her pocket, and took another bite from
her artery-choking fried fair food.  “I’ll probably write it on some
grungy bathroom walls or something.”

Even Ava laughed at that remark, and Lily giggled despite herself. 
Despite the situation, too — depending on how one counted Amelia (and
wasn’t that horrifying itself…), the Wards were outnumbered by villains
at the table.  And yet, they were all just laughing and joking like
Taylor was not at the head of a bloody crusade for control of the Bay.

At least Parian seemed to be —

Lily’s eyes went wide as the realization hit her like a ton of bricks. 
She fished the card from Sabah out of her pocket and gaped at it, mind
whirling in a hurricane of horror and gay.  The Teeth bought Parian's
stuff.  Did it count if Weaver was just protecting the doll cape?  Sabah
was too much Lily’s type to not at least go on a single date, but…

Watching the other Wards laugh as Amelia angrily tried to stick a French
fry up Chrissie's nose, Lily realized that this was how the Teeth hooked
people.

And she was too late.

They already had her.
