    Chapter 37: Consequence 4.2

Chapter by Pendragoon <https://archiveofourown.org/users/Pendragoon/
pseuds/Pendragoon>

Chapter Notes

See the end of the chapter for notes <#endnotes37>

/Saturday May 7th, 2011 /

/“I forgot how good food trucks can be.” /  Ironsides’ comments were met
with various rumblings of approval from the rest of us, and I could
honestly say that I didn’t regret any of the money Lisa had spent
convincing all of our favorites to drive up from New York and Boston. 
Based on the less-than-amused looks on a few heroes’ faces, the new
color schemes were equally worth the cost.

/Yeah, it was good.  I’ve never had real New York pizza. /

/“Gino’s is not bad,” /Knockout agreed, only to have Alkaline start up
their perpetual argument.

/“Why didn’t we get a deep dish pizza truck?” / she asked for the tenth
time.  /“Do they not exist?” /

/“I saw one selling phở, which isn’t that far off,” /Knockout retorted,
and they descended into pointless bickering once again.  At this point,
my predecessors were largely polite enough to keep their arguments in
the back of my brain — whatever that meant — so I was free to think
about the Protectorate’s most recent PR stunt while walking home with
Chrissie, Lisa, and Amelia.

Chrissie squeezed my hand, flashing me a mischievous smile.  “That
wasn’t half bad, huh?  Good food, fun times screwing with the heroes,
cute girls…”

I nodded.  “We can’t let this stand.”

“No way in hell,” Lisa agreed.

“Can you three stop being supervillains for ten fucking minutes?” Amelia
complained.  “Just let them have their fun.”

“Says the hero who spent her entire time today avoiding her adoring
fans.”  Chrissie’s dripping sarcasm earned her a glare from the surly
healer, but honestly I felt a little bad for Amelia.

Conversation for the rest of the walk to our lair was half Amelia
venting about those fans and half random musings about the impromptu
fair.  I ended up relaying several of the Butchers’ observations to the
others, mostly concerning food and the various people they had fought
over the years.

“Have any of you guys actually fought in civvies before?” Chrissie asked.

“Chisel did, once,” I relayed.  “She went to a concert that the others
wanted to see badly enough that they mostly shut up for a night, only to
get into a fight at the bar later.  It went, uh, poorly.”

/“What do you mean, poorly?” / Stratego rumbled.  /“She nailed a guy to
the fucking ceiling with pool cues!” /

Despite everything, I nearly missed a step when Chisel brought that
memory to the foreground.  Fester started cackling to herself, and when
I sent a metaphorical raised eyebrow her way, she managed to cough
out, /“Oh, the asshole who groped your butt!” /

/“Tried to,” / Chisel said, though there was a definite smirk in her voice.

“Anyways,” I said, clapping my hands together and ignoring the laughter
in my head.  “Plans for the rest of the evening?”

“I’ve been on my feet all day,” Amelia said.  “So I veto any plans that
don’t involve sitting down.”

“Easy night in?” Lisa suggested.  “I’m sure we can find ways to…
entertain ourselves.”

Chrissie wiggling her eyebrows at me was expected, but Amelia’s blush
was not.  I knew that Lisa was poking fun to get a reaction out of
everyone — I was /definitely / not blushing a tiny bit myself — but it
was nevertheless strange to see the embarrassed look on the usually
grumpy healer.

My girlfriend came to the rescue.  “Amelia, didn’t you say you invented
something new?  Maybe we should celebrate with that,” Chrissie tried. 
“Taytay here could definitely use some relaxation.”

Relaxation sounded nice, actually — keeping my persona up and messing
with the heroes was mentally taxing, and not just because half of the
Butchers complained nonstop.

/“More than half,” / Sabertooth growled.  /“You own this damn city!  If
I had managed that —” /

/“You would still have fucked it up!” / Pyro yelled back.  /“As much as
I want XV to go light someone on fire, even I’m not dumb enough to
suggest doing that while Legend is in town.” /

/“Coward,” / Sabertooth spat.

/“Says the moron who hired the Nine!” /

/“Do you two ever argue about anything else?” / Ironsides bellowed,
dragging the two offenders and several others into yet another shouting
match that I pushed into the dark depths of my mind.

/“Truly, the essence of this purgatory is being party to the same
arguments repeated ad infinitum,” / Damascian said.

/“It’s like being trapped on an internet forum,” / Quarrel muttered,
eliciting a round of surprised murmurs that she agreed with the Tinker
about anything.  /“What?  Tell me I’m wrong.” /

Alkaline shrugged.  /“Dunno, the internet was shitty when I was kid. 
All we had was drugs.  Speaking of, you had better try that new stuff
Amelia cooked up.  Girl has a career as a drug designer!” /

/I feel bad for corrupting her. /

/“You shut the hell up,” / Alkaline retorted with faux-seriousness.

Chrissie squeezed my hand, and I realized that I had zoned out while
listening to the Butchers again.  “Sorry, what?” I asked, wondering what
I had missed in the other conversation.

“We didn’t say anything,” Amelia said, raising an eyebrow at me.  “Need
us to talk about something more interesting?”

I blinked at the offer.  “Uh, sure.”

“Well, I started reading that Black Company book you left on the
throne,” Chrissie started.  At Lisa’s snicker, she shot a glare towards
the Thinker.  “What?  Am I not allowed to share my girlfriend’s
hobbies?  Besides, that book is badass.”

The discussion on the book filled the rest of the walk back to the
base.  The Butchers kept quiet for the most part, occasionally chipping
in commentary from my own read through.  I had actually picked it on
Sanguine’s recommendation, which was probably why they mostly let me
read without interruptions.

“Where is everyone?” Amelia wondered when we finally reached the main
party room and found it empty.  Poking my swarm told me that even Alec
and Rachel were gone, and while I was tempted to try to find them
through my muddy relayed senses, nothing seemed to be going wrong that
might be their fault.  Jokes about how ‘Bug Sister was watching’ were
only funny up to a point.

I flopped down onto the couch.  “Out doing their own thing, I guess. 
So, uh… what did you invent this time?”  Chrissie snorted, then flopped
down on top of me.

Amelia’s eyes practically lit up at my question, to Alkaline’s great
interest.  “Have any of the Butchers ever done mescaline?” the healer
asked, trying and mostly failing to keep the excitement out of her voice.

/“Hell yes I did!” / Alkaline cheered.  /“Cactus is great!” /

/“Tastes godawful,” / Stratego complained.

I nodded, grimacing at the memory of the flavor.  Only the Teeth would
mix cactus, peanut butter, and Sprite in a blender and try to drink it. 
“Yeah, what of it?  I don’t really want to experience that myself.” 

“Inspiration, mostly,” Amelia said, waving a hand.  “Some crazy chemist
in the seventies figured out how to synthesize the active molecule and
wrote a book.  Lisa got me a copy” cue smugness “and, well…”

Some part of me knew that corrupting the only actual hero in the city
might end up being the most damning thing I ever end up doing, but it
was hard to deny that the freckled girl seemed to be less unhappy now
than when she started hanging out with us.  Lisa gave me a
conspiratorial wink as soon as the thought crossed my mind, and I made a
mental note to figure out just what the Thinker was thinking.

“It’s not going to be as powerful, right?” I asked, remembering a Dunkin
Donuts and one of Accord’s capes.  “The Butcher and drugs don’t really
mix well.”

/“Bah, a few bad trips —” / Marauder started, only to get instantly
shouted into oblivion by the others.

Chrissie gave me a pat on the head.  “You’ll be fine, trust us.  I did
acid once and this is nothing close.”

After a moment of deliberation, I agreed; Amelia vanished into her room
and returned with a handful of blunts, a disturbing spring in her step. 
She even produced a rainbow zippo for a light, and far sooner than I
ever expected I was doing actual drugs.

The Butchers cheered in my head.

“It’s not terrible,” I said, falling back on someone’s habits and using
two fingers to gesture with the blunt.  One of my powers helped keep me
from coughing and hacking too much when I smoked weed, which was a
godsend after my early attempts.  “What’s supposed to happen?”

“Not a lot more than normal weed,” Amelia said. “No offense, but I don’t
want to be in the same room while you’re tripping balls.  It should be
noticeable eventually.”

“Me neither.”  Even after Alkaline and the others had painstakingly
explained the difference between psychedelics and hard drugs to me, I
had still found the prospect of altered mental states to be too
terrifying with my numerous destructive powers.  Weed was one thing;
some of my predecessors’ multi-day benders on exotic substances were the
stuff of literal nightmares.

But Amelia was just as concerned as I was, and if I couldn’t trust
Panacea, then who?

The blunts were soon gone, and I was joined on the couch by Chrissie,
Amy, and Lisa.  My girlfriend took her customary spot on my lap, but the
other two ended up much closer than usual.  I understood why a few
minutes later when the effects of Amelia’s creation started to kick in —
cuddling was way better for some reason and I wasn’t going to complain.

“This is nice,” Chrissie murmured.

“We like it too,” I said, relaying the sentiments of my peanut gallery. 
Amelia just hummed in response and snuggled up next to us.

At some point, Lisa put on a nature documentary and brought us a bowl of
popcorn, and we were joined by a few of the nearby Teeth who still
seemed rather confused by the Butcher lounging on a couch instead of
whatever we usually did.  Either that or they were also high as shit,
which was just as likely given that they were Teeth.

Like me.

/“Oh no you don’t,” / Fester said.  /“Right now, Taylor, you are
enjoying yourself.  You can’t be the conquering warlord all the time, so
save your introspection and worries for the time you can actually do
something about it.” /

I knew that I was supposed to object to that, but honestly?  Watching
baby elephants falling over and giggling with the rest of my friends was
vastly preferable to contemplating the horror show that my life had
become in the past few weeks.  Becoming Butcher XV should not have
improved my life, and I really shouldn’t be enjoying my time with the Teeth.

Then Chrissie turned and gave me a kiss, and I put those thoughts out of
my mind.

We sat like that for indeterminate time — laughing, cuddling, eating
(and throwing) popcorn, and generally acting like teenage girls who
didn’t wear the bones of their enemies.  I ended up with both Amelia and
Chrissie practically on top of me, with Lisa snuggled up next to the
former.  Someone was scratching the top of my head, but intertwined as
we were, I couldn’t tell who nor did I particularly care.

Of course, the Teeth and tranquility went together like the Teeth and
basically anything else, meaning that our quiet afternoon was brutally
murdered in an alley by a loud disturbance making its way through the
lair.  The only consolation was that they were headed to the arena
instead of the common room, so I didn’t need to upend an entire couch of
teenaged supervillains in haste.

I tried diplomacy first.  “Let me up.”

“Too comfy,” Chrissie whined.

I didn’t need my bugs to know when the group of hopefully Teeth banged
open the arena doors and brought in their struggling payload. 
Eventually my curiosity won out over my patience while trying to
dislodge myself, and I just teleported down to see what my minions had
procured.  My sudden disappearance left the other girls in a tangled pile.

The group of unpowered Teeth hauling three tied-up burly guys barely
flinched, but said burly guys ceased their struggles immediately when I
appeared in a blast of sound and flame.  “What the hell is going on? 
You’re interrupting my relaxation time.”

“Sorry boss,” one of the Teeth said quickly.  “But, uh, crooked cops. 
Empire supporters, based on the tattoos.”

The Butchers immediately started howling for blood in my head, dredging
up some of Stratego’s less pleasant memories that did nothing but stoke
the fires of my righteous anger.  I had made it /extremely / obvious
that the Empire and their ilk were not welcome in my city any longer, so
finding that there were still sympathizers hiding behind the law and
each other made me almost see red.

“Any last words?” I asked my soon-to-be opponents, flashing them a smile
of too-sharp teeth.

“Fuck you cannibal freaks!” one of the men said.  “You may have beaten
Kaiser, but there’s real Americans out there who will stop you!”

/“Good, life is getting kind of boring around here,” / Knockout
muttered, somehow audible despite the others yelling at me to fight.

I hoisted the one who had spoken and set him against the wall, using
Chisel’s power on the ropes to ensure that he didn’t go anywhere.  “He
gets to watch,” I spat.  “Mind if I tag in?”

“Uh, no problem, boss,” one of the Teeth said, untying the other two
crooked cops.  One immediately pulled a knife from his pocket and
lunged; I backhanded him across the arena, sending the knife flying.

“Wait for the sig— shit.”  The Butchers roared with laughter in my head
as I realized what I had done: I hadn’t contained my strength even a
little bit, and my slap had torn the guy’s head clean off.

/“Holy shit XV, what was that?” / Pyro yelled.  /“And don’t you dare say
‘accident!’” /

It had been an accident, but I didn’t want to dwell on that right now. 
Instead, I turned my attention to the remaining combatant, though that
term was perhaps too generous.  My unpowered minions were making quick
work of the Empire sympathizer, hounding him like a pack of feral
animals.  I debated getting involved, but they really didn’t need my help.

“Monsters!” The first cop snarled, straining against his bonds while the
Teeth disemboweled his other friend in front of him.  “You’re monsters!”

“Says the neo-Nazi,” I spat back.  If I was being totally honest, he
wasn’t totally wrong — corpses behind me certainly didn’t show up dead —
but I wasn’t going to take insults from a guy who probably would have
swept Chrissie’s murder under the rug had those Empire kids from school
succeeded.  “So… what should we do with you?”

“Target practice!” Chrissie called from the balcony, and I looked up to
see her leaning on the railing.  “We need to teach the newbies how to
throw knives, and it looks like the boys found us a volunteer!”

/“Buwaha, I knew why I loved her,” / Butcher laughed.  /“If only all of
our capes had such spunk!” /

I gave my girlfriend a thumbs up, then teleported down to the clear area
in my workshop.  One of the workbenches held an astonishing collection
of low-grade (for me) knives, and I carefully picked up a dozen and
dropped them into a box.  When I returned to the arena, Chrissie had
brought Amelia and Lisa down; two of the guys were double checking the
Chisel reinforced restraints.

“Now, Tay can’t actually teach you shit because she cheats,” Chrissie
said, ignoring my raised finger while carefully picking a knife from the
box.  “If you’re just going to stab a bitch, hold it however you want. 
But if you’re going to throw it…”

Over the next twenty minutes, both of our new capes tried with various
levels of success to sink my Tinkertech knives into the loudly
complaining racist cop.  He stopped complaining when I used Chisel’s
power to mold some of the rope into his mouth.

/“Oooh, nice shot!” / Pyro cheered as Lisa finally hit the guy in the
stomach.  Truth be told, I wasn’t particularly enthusiastic about this
activity, but based on the number of Teeth watching in the stands, it
was rather popular.  Amelia had a rather worrying grin on her face, but
I had been around Lisa enough to recognize the tightness around her eyes.

/“Neither has actually killed anyone in combat,” / Stratego
rumbled.  /“Tradition —” /

/Is whatever I say it is, / I snapped, giving him a shove.  /The Butcher
leads the Teeth! /

My predecessors went back to watching and grumbling.  Then Amelia
finally landed a hit herself, nailing the guy directly in the crotch,
and even I chuckled aloud with the rest of the Teeth when they burst
into laughter.  The same sound echoed in my head, but I was suddenly
aware of someone who wasn’t laughing.

My dad was up on the balcony, arms crossed with a stony expression on
his face.  When I turned to face him and fought down another round of
giggles, that expression turned thunderous.  Still, he managed to not do
something stupid, instead hooking his chin towards my room and walked away.

/“Busted!” / Sanguine said with mock seriousness.

/“For fuck’s sake, you’re the Butcher,” / Ironsides
complained.  /“You’re not really going to go to your room like a
misbehaving child, are you!?” /

“Maybe he has something important to say,” I murmured, then raised my
voice.  “Nice shot, Amelia.  I’ll be back in a moment, Dad’s here.”  If
I teleported into the hallway not a dozen feet ahead of my dad, well, he
was the one who wanted to see me, right?

“Holy shit Taylor,” he gasped, nearly falling over.  “Don’t do that!” 

I leveled an annoyed glare at him, then spun on a heel and stalked
towards my room.  He followed without further comment, even waiting
until I had shut the door securely behind us before assuming a slightly
more threatening stance.  The rush of information from Stratego’s power
had me blinking — was Dad aware how his body language shifted when
angry?  I assume so, given his obvious attempts to control himself, but
it had been so long since I had seen him truly furious. 

However, in his attempts to calm himself, his wandering gaze landed on
the replica of Kaiser’s skull hanging on the wall.  “Taylor, please tell
me that isn’t what I think it is.”

“It’s a replica,” I replied, flopping down into the comfy chair Chrissie
and I had stolen (and then broken in).  “Amelia grew it after we burned
the original.”

In a fit of historical mockery and crime, Spree and Hemorrhagia had
taken a bunch of Teeth to steal a garbage hauling barge from /
somewhere /, bringing it back to the Bay for us to use as Kaiser’s
pyre.  While the smell had been atrocious and actually maneuvering the
thing had required me to stick the Coast Guard with warning arrows, the
real Teeth-worthy part had been the fireworks onboard that launched
sideways and started several more fires on the Docks.

Despite the twitch in the corner of his mouth, I knew Dad was still mad
about that particular shitshow.  “That is exactly my point, Taylor,” he
said, pinching his nose in exasperation.  “When was the last time you
sat down and took stock of… everything?  I know that I can’t even
comprehend your situation, which is something no parent ever wants to
say, but… just look at yourself!”

I looked down at my shirt — was there blood on it that I didn’t see?

/“You turned the blood into a dagger,” / Sanguine reminded me.

“Taylor, this is serious.  I’m—I can’t just stand here and watch my
little girl turn into a axe-crazy murderer, Butcher or no.  You’re
better than that, I know you are, and it hurts to see you enjoying
hurting other people.”

“They’re neo-Nazis Dad, they don’t count.”  Several Butchers agreed and
the rest nodded.

“Taylor!  What would your mother say if she heard you saying that!?”

The bottom fell out of my stomach.  Dad hadn’t /ever / pulled that line
since Mom died, and it burned all the worse because I knew that there
was a time where she would have agreed with me.  Fester’s unhinged
ranting in the back of my head barely registered in comparison to the
incredulous shock that he would pull that line here and now.  It took
everything I had to not give in to any of the rather inventive things
Fester was demanding I do to answer that. 

Dad took my strained silence as an opportunity to keep going.  “You know
that I love you Taylor.  But the violence, the bloodshed… this isn’t
you.  I know that you’re trying to make the Teeth better —”

“They are better,” I cut in, working to keep my own anger under a lid.

“Are they?  Because it doesn’t seem like it from here.”

I waved an arm.  “You don’t see them just randomly killing people on the
street anymore, do you?”

“I don’t care about them, I care about you!  And what they’re doing to you!”

“They are my first friends in years!”

“They’re supervillains!”

“You didn’t give a shit about this two weeks ago!”

Dad reeled as if slapped.  “That’s not the point,” he said, the wind
taken out of his sails.  “Taylor, I had just found out that you were the
Butcher.  I was relieved that you were able to hide that from me,
because it meant that you weren’t insane like the others.  But the more
that I think about it, the more worried I’ve become.”

/“He’s worried / now /?” / Fester hissed.  /“Not two months ago?  Two
years?” /

/“Still, he’s got balls,” / Knockout admitted.

I jumped out of my chair, trying to work off some of the anger and
irritation by pacing.  “I have everything under control.  The Butchers,
the Teeth…  In case you haven’t noticed, the Protectorate is in town, so
I’m trying to get everyone to chill out for a bit so we don’t all get
blasted into little bits.  You, coming here?  Making that much harder.”

Dad didn’t have a response for that immediately, but I could tell that
he was winding himself up for another pointless argument.  That made me
more angry in response, and after another minute of fuming I realized
that I needed to walk away before I did something Dad would regret.  A
quick check revealed that Chrissie, Amelia, and Lisa were once again
passed out in a tangle on the couch, and so I chose door number two —
find literally anything else to do in the city than listen to my dad
lecture me.

“Taylor…” Dad tried, only to trail off when I walked over to my costume
and gave him a pointed stare.  “Young lady, don’t you dare —”

/“Oh she fuckin’ dares!” / Alkaline yelled.

“Turn around, Dad,” I said, voice flat.

“I’m not going to let you just —”

/“What, he’s going to send you to your room?  Ground you?” / Sanguine
asked.  /“Does he have a plan here?” /

/“Be angry,” / Quarrel retorted.  /“Just like how we’re angry that you
are listening to him!” /

I didn’t find out what he wasn’t going to ‘let me just’ as I teleported
down into my lab after grabbing an extra-large pair of sweats and a
beat-up zippered hoodie.  My bugs reported Dad’s inarticulate scream of
frustration, but I finished changing before he could do more than stalk
out of my room.  The sweats and hoodie went on over my costume so that I
could at least grab a bite to eat from a food truck before I did…
whatever I was going to do.

Primarily, not be anywhere near my father.

Secondarily, food.  The Butchers clamored in my head, trying to cash in
their food votes, and I eventually relented.  I picked a bug that
dropped me in an alley not too far from the Protectorate’s event,
knowing full well that the teleport was both loud and distinctive.  As
expected, several heroes were searching around the street nearby when I
walked out of the mouth of the alley.

Part of me almost wished that they would do something stupid so we could
finally just have this fight that had been brewing since they arrived,
but unfortunately for me, the heroes were being reasonable today.

/“Boo, talking,” / Knockout yelled.  /“Just fucking punch them already!” /

“Excuse me miss,” a boy in unfamiliar power armor said.  Tecton, a
Chicago Ward — none of my predecessors had actually tangled with him, so
I had needed to look up his power online.  “Have you seen… a…”

His brain seemed to short circuit while giving me a less-than-subtle
once over.  A downward glance revealed why: my hoodie was open and
lightly smoking.

We both froze.

Then I slowly and deliberately zipped it up, holding his gaze the whole
time.  “Have I seen what?” I asked calmly.

The poor Ward blinked at me in confusion, but to his credit he didn’t do
anything immediately stupid.  In my head, the Butchers laughed their
collective asses off in between calls to start the fight, but I kept my
expression level and only raised an inquisitive eyebrow.

Tecton cleared his throat.  “We heard an explosion, and we were worried —”

“It was probably the Butcher,” I said, deadpan.  “When you live in the
Bay, you come to recognize the sound.”

“The Butcher,” Tecton repeated, voice weak.

“Haven’t seen her.”  If it wasn’t for the fact that they didn’t need
air, I would have worried that several of my headmates would die of
laughter-induced asphyxiation.

Tecton nodded quickly.  “Right, sure.  Thanks, um, citizen.”  He turned
and practically sprinted away, heading towards a group of Protectorate
and Wards that were presumably here for me.  Several of them turned my
way as I walked past, including Jouster, so I gave them a cheeky wave
and watched with Sanguine’s power as their blood pressure and heart rate
went through the roof.

I couldn’t help it — I giggled, which turned into an unhinged laugh of
my own.

Luckily for them, none of the heroes made the questionably-sane choice
of picking a fight with me in a stone’s throw from a park full of
civilians, evil supervillain cackle or no.  Part of me was disappointed,
as I still had the pent-up energy from the confrontation with Dad and a
fight would have been a great way to blow off some steam.

Instead, I was left alone to follow my predecessors' directions as I
picked up food from three different food trucks and carried it over to
one of the unoccupied picnic tables.  Loaded potato skins, some sort of
grilled cheese monstrosity, and yet more pizza.

/“Do you think Amelia’s drug is giving us the munchies?” / Fester asked.

I took a bite of potato and considered that.  “Maybe?  I don’t feel
particularly hungry.”

/“Hungry for a fight, maybe,” / Knockout said, cracking his metaphorical
knuckles.  /“Come on, the heroes are / right there! /  You don’t even
need to hurt them that much!” /

/“How you survived as a cape with survival instincts like that, I will
never know,” / Chisel shot back.  /“Thank god Taylor has a brain in her
head.” /

/“Oh fuck you —” /

“Shut up,” I hissed, aware that my earlier outburst had drawn a few
eyes.  If any of the onlookers recognized me, they didn't do anything
obvious like jumping up and running in fear.  Thus, I was able to eat in
relative peace… at least on the outside.

Internally, I was still fuming about the conversation with Dad.  If I
was being honest with myself, I wasn't even angry at Dad himself — he
was always going to object to my new existence, and the conversation had
been overdue.  No, I was upset about the fact that I wanted /more / of
the very behavior that he was complaining about, and yet my restraint /
still / wasn't good enough for him.

/“You didn’t even kill all of the Elite capes who tried to backstab
you!” /Sanguine added unhelpfully.

More importantly, it wasn’t enough for the Protectorate.  They couldn’t
just leave us alone to finish evicting the undesirable criminals from
the city; no, they had to waltz in with their heavy hitters and throw a
party on my lawn.  I already had enough issues keeping the Teeth
occupied — case in point, I needed Faultline’s help, maybe I should
throw Dad at her to keep him busy — that this sort of pointless
posturing was going to get someone killed. 

I wasn't even worried about that person being me, which was its own can
of worms.

What I /was / worried about was that a large part of me /wanted / a
fight, even when I discounted the Butchers.  Fighting the Elite,
fighting the Empire… cape combat was a thrill that I would never have
expected before really getting into the business.  It was invigorating
to actually make a positive change on the world with my powers, helping
eliminate the fuckers that had plagued the Bay for so long.

/“Damn straight,” /Butcher agreed.

/“You need more practice with my bow,” / Quarrel complained.  /“Your
bugs are terrifying, but you haven’t experienced the fun of raining
death down onto your enemies.” /

/“Or pick a melee weapon,” / Chisel suggested, sending a memory of how
she fought with a pair of wicked, serrated knives.

Damascian did the mental equivalent of rubbing her hands
together.  /“The Wolf Slayer is a fine armament, but surely we can
improve…” /

/You’re not helping! /

The chorus chuckled as I gave them all a firm shove, but the thoughts
they summoned were harder to banish.  It was true that I tended to
prefer my own power for its sheer versatility and terror factor, but
there was a perverse pleasure in simple, knock-down brawls with the
Brute powers.  Taking down Hookwolf had been one hell of a rush.  But
Quarrel was right, the bow was fun… 

And I was doing it again.

I wasn’t supposed to enjoy being the Butcher.

/“If it helps, a lot of other people don’t enjoy you being the Butcher,
either," / Alkaline added.  /“You’re too damn good at it.” /

I didn’t want to open that can of worms either, so I focused back on my
food.  I distracted the peanut gallery with another round (and thus
vote), but it was impossible to actually relax with the goddamn heroes
wandering around while I was eating.  Unfortunately, I couldn't just
leave when they knew I was here, so I had to swallow my frustration
alongside the funnel cake.

The only distraction I was afforded came in the form of a simple
mugging, five blocks from the park.  Said mugger attempted to escape the
swarm, only to trip on a conveniently located silk line and receive
several kicks from their would-be victim.  Then the Butchers’ laughs
were cut off by another movement of my bugs — the heroes were mobilizing.

/“It’s just a damn mugger,” / Ironsides complained, but Damascian cut
him off.

/“They are clearly uninterested in Taylor’s vigilantism, based on their
heading.” /

/“Oh shit!” / several Butchers said in unison, and I followed their
attention to the heroes’ likely destination.  My bug senses were crap at
those distances, but I realized that something was on fire downtown… and
several of my capes were unaccounted for.

Fuck.

 

------------------------------------------------------------------------

 

Teleporting directly into the epicenter of a cape fight wasn't exactly a
sane move, but I was fuckmothering Butcher and this was my goddamn
city.  If the idiots involved had not wanted me to show up, then they
should have taken their fight literally anywhere else.  Now I had to
figure out a way to de-escalate everything without killing anyone so
that the Protectorate didn’t have a good excuse to dismantle the Teeth
and do… /something / with me.

At least, that’s what the rational part of my brain was trying to say. 
The less rational part was currently dominated by the clamoring voices
of the collective ready to sate their bloodlust. 

/“Fucking finally!”  “All this tension, finally coming to a head.” 
“Talk about one hell of a case of edging.”  “Now get in there and fuck
their shit!”  /

I wasn’t particularly listening, focused on my current fight as I was —
Mouse Protector had been one of my favorite heroes growing up.  A much
younger me had loved her witticisms and silly fighting style, laughing
along with the show as the infamous hero teleported around like a maniac
with a goofy smile on her face.  That adoration was probably why I had
jumped headfirst into the fight against the mousy heroine, blue balling
Reaver… but he could go play with someone else.

/“Were we even aware she was in town?”  “Don’t recall her being
mentioned in the boring as fuck strategy meetings.”  “Those meetings are
of the utmost importance.”  “Utmost your ass!”  /

Stratego’s power was happy to inform me that Mouse was a /very / skilled
swordswoman, forcing me to rely on all of my Thinker powers to keep
ahead of her with the mockery of a blade I had made out of some rebar
with Chisel’s power.  With an actual weapon, the fight would have been
easier, but I was an idiot and hadn’t brought my weapon harness.  Thus,
I was up close and personal; I could see the brittleness in her smile,
the tightness around her eyes that spoke of far too many years fighting
supervillains like me.

Still, Mouse managed a few of her signature taunts.  “So, if you’ve got
all of those crazy people in your head, does that make you the big
cheese platter?  You certainly stink like one!”  I parried her strike
and tried to mount my own offensive, but Mouse just teleported a few
feet away and waved her sword at me.  “You’ll need to be faster to catch
this mouse!”

/“Just fucking pain blast her already!” / Butcher screeched, to the
halfhearted cheers of the others.

“I’m not doing that, assholes.”  My retort made Mouse blink in
confusion, and I darted forward, sword raised.  She managed to block my
attack, turning it aside with a flashy riposte that brought back
memories with a laugh.  That seemed to unnerve Mouse, but nevertheless
we fell back into our teleport-aided back-and-forth. 

Our Mover abilities seemed to have similar cooldown periods, which was
making the fight an incredibly fun back and forth… for me.  I could
easily end the fight at any point, but I was enjoying myself far too
much to just quit now.  I would find out who started this mess later,
punish them appropriately, but for now I’d be content to let everyone
burn off some steam and deal with the property damage later. 

Mouse’s blade narrowly missed my mask, snapping my attention back to the
fight.  Damascian’s precog ability and Reflex’s namesake saved me from
becoming sliced provolone… 

/“Oh god, it’s contagious.”  /

“You know Mousey,” I said as I returned the favor, following her escape
teleport with one of my own, “if I had known you were here, I would have
rolled out the Windsor carpet, filled my hammer space with nacho cheese,
and robbed Brockton of all the cheddar.” 

/“Someone please kill us.” /

“Then surrender to the side of gouda!” she declared, darting forward
only to disengage at my riposte. 

Mouse backpedaled right past Armsmaster, who had taken up the fight with
Reaver in Mouse’s place.  All around us, little fights and skirmishes
were happening between the Elite’s goons, the Teeth, and the various
heroes that had shown up far too late to stop the first two from setting
at least one building on fire.  Had I been paying attention, my bugs
would likely have revealed a clusterfuck of epic proportions.

At least Chrissie hadn’t been drawn into this mess, though I suspected
that neither of us would have minded terribly when I would have had to
‘punish’ her.  The Butchers snickered at the mental image as I
teleported to the other side of Armsy, not wanting to give him an excuse
to take a swipe at me.  A moment later, Animos slammed into a storefront
at the hands of some Elite cape I didn’t recognize. 

I paused in our duel, my swarm overhead increasing in volume.  “Stop
wrecking the city, dumbass!  Property damage comes out of your pay!” 

It said something that each of my capes involved in this mess actually
paused in their fighting at my stern warning.  The fighting resumed a
beat later, but it was clear the Teeth, at least, were heeding my words
given how each of them had shifted away from the storefronts and towards
the intersections of the streets. 

“Weaver!  Call them off!” Armsmaster demanded. 

“You first!” I shouted back.  “That or do something about the damn Elite!” 

I ducked and dodged Mouse’s sword as she once again pressed the attack. 
The heroine seemed more relaxed since I had begun to banter with her,
though the sharpness of her focus hadn’t diminished in the slightest. 
Absently I noticed the Wards group from earlier arriving on the
battlefield, Tecton immediately giving orders to Vista and Jouster that
I really didn’t care about. 

“You do know your cheese brains started this,” Mouse said playfully. 
“Maybe you should listen to the beard master.” 

“Eh, let everyone have some fun first,” I countered.  “The tension in
this city was so thick that even my knives would have struggled to cut
the resulting romano.” 

“You really are just cheesing it up!” Mouse said, hopping away.  “Why
else would you play along?” 

I shrugged, gesturing with my terrible sword.  “Because it’s fun?” 

“You turned a cape into cottage cheese eight hours ago.” 

“He was an asshole,” I said simply, lunging forward only to have her
teleport away, denying me my fun once more.  “Now, come on!  Fight me!” 

“No, it’s what you want,” Mouse said, sheathing her sword.  “Armsy,
we’re leaving!” 

“Like hell,” I spat as Mouse vanished from the battlefield. 

I teleported down to the street where most of my capes were fighting. 
Spree had the area choked down in his clones, giving Assault and Battery
hell when I arrived in a flash of fire.  The fighting once again paused
as I glared at the capes around me.  I tossed the nearly ruined sword
aside and squared up with Assault, hoping for another good fight and
knowing he could deliver it — unlike the pansy girl down the road
throwing red lightning at Myrddin. 

“Spree, you’re banned from bath salts for life,” I said to the frothing
mess of a man, then charged at Assault, grabbing a Spree clone by the
leg and using it as a bat against the kinetic manipulator.  The
resulting splatter was glorious as Assault let the momentum carry him
off, leaving his wife behind to get covered in a spray of gore. 

/“Let’s see if he’s brave enough to earn those red wings!” /Marauder
snarked. 

I took a step forward only to have the Gandalf knock-off interpose
himself between me and my prey.  At that same moment, Animos was sent
tumbling down the road by the arrival of Chevalier.

Good, this party was starting to get a bit dull. 

That was when something unseen enveloped me and I found myself
airborne.  Myrddin must have pulled out one of his bullshit tricks
because I couldn’t orient myself even with my swarm sense.  Then he was
flying beside me, staff twirling in the air under its own volition. 

“Fight fair you bastard!” I yelled, only for him to swat me with another
invisible wave of force. 

Finally, I grasped my swarm sense, picked a bug, and flashed to it in a
ball of fire.  I stumbled across the bow of one of the ships in the
graveyard, fighting the urge to vomit.  Between Myrddin’s nonsense and
jumping too far, too fast, that teleport was easily the worst ride any
of us had ever been on, and luckily I had been mostly sober for it. 
That would have been hell if I were drunk, or worse, on acid. 

Before I’d even shaken off the aftereffects of my own ride, Animos
crashed into the back of the ship and it became clear what was
happening.  I reached for all the bugs along my relays and had them form
shapeless clones to relay my words. 

“The heroes are dividing us up, disengage and regroup at the Graveyard. 
They want a fight, let’s get something out of it.” 

I grabbed a handrail and ripped it free, shaping the tip into a shitty
spear just so I had a weapon in hand as Myrddin once again appeared in
the sky above me.  Elliot groaned, having fallen unconscious from his
short flight and abrupt stop.  He was once again human shaped and rather
nude.  I was tempted to make a joke about how it wasn’t /that /cold when
other heroes began to arrive. 

Assault and Battery were always good Movers, so that was no surprise,
but the land bridge being operated by Vista was a bit of an eye opener. 
That girl was so underutilized in the Wards, though I was surprised they
let her keep the stun gun that Aisha had gifted the girl.  Following her
were Tecton, Jouster, Armsmaster, Mouse Protector and Chevalier. 

They were accompanied by streaks of white across the sky as Photon Mom
and Laserdream arrived.  I was a bit disappointed that Brandish wasn’t
with them — the resulting ass-kicking would have been a great source of
catharsis. 

Still, I was staring down over a dozen capes now, and rather than admit
defeat, I wanted nothing more than to prove how wrong they were to
underestimate me.

“Animos, go home,” I said, grinning at the prospect of taking them all
on,  I spun the spear and leveled it upon the assembled heroes.  “Come
on then!  Collateral don’t mean shit for dick here and may as well be a
public service, so let’s cut loose and fuck some shit up because Butcher
needs to express some rage!” 

Before any of them could answer, I teleported right into their midst and
let just a splash of Marauder’s rage aura wash over the group.  It
served its purpose, just enough to light the spark as Damascian’s precog
swam into motion, letting me see a dozen attacks coming at once.  I
twisted and flexed, letting Sabertooth’s shapeshifting work on my joints
as I flexed around each blow and parried the blasts with Knockout’s
shields. 

Blinding lights washed over the melee as my foot connected with one hero
and my spear swept the feet out from another.  My bugs were having
difficulties tagging Armsmaster and Chevalier, likely some Tinker device
he had come up with, but amped up as I was, it only made the situation
more exciting.  The clamor in the back of my mind was only drowned out
by my own gleeful cackling. 

/“At least your supervillain laugh is coming along nicely…” /Reflex
said, cutting through the fog. 

/“Shut the fuck up!” /rang out from the other fourteen of us. 

I wasn’t sure if I had said that aloud or not and frankly I didn’t care
— this was the most fun I have had since I fought Hookwolf.  Sure, Dad’s
life had been on the line, but the fight itself was the most visceral
moment of my life and I wanted more of that.  None of these assholes
wanted me dead, but I was determined to push them to the limits all the
same. 

A jolt ran through me and I smiled; Vista was fearless and more than a
little vicious in a fight.  I set my swarm upon her, but made sure none
bit or stung the young Ward.  Dinah and Aisha would have been upset with
me otherwise. 

I ducked under a wild swing from Chevalier, laughing as I landed a punch
on his armored torso and actually dented the fucking thing.  Granted, my
hand was reduced to mush after that, but it was totally worth it.  I
stepped back, shuffling and ducking other attacks, then used my spear to
disarm Jouster of his own.  The man staggered after his unnecessarily
phallic weapon as I blew him a kiss, and I could practically smell the
fury radiating off of him. 

Yeah, I was totally putting his number in the Teeth restrooms. 

Sabertooth’s regen was taking forever to repair my hand, but even with
the damage I could at least move my fingers.  I wouldn’t need to bother
Amelia with healing it, which was a good thing.  Unfortunately, it meant
that hand was now useless in this fight.  

That was when Battery caught me with a punch of her own, delivered with
a full charge that sent me tearing through the hull of at least two
ships before I came to a stop, embedded in the steel of another.  I
coughed, knowing it would have been a spray of red if not for my mask.

The heroes regrouped around me, ready to keep the game going.  I could
feel the blood dripping down my chin and leaking from my mask, which was
hella intimidating if the Ward’s reactions were accurate.  I ripped my
arms loose of the rusted hull, the groaning steel causing more than a
few to wince at the sound. 

Thus freed, I landed on the ground with a thud, pulling my mask aside
with my good hand and spitting out globs of blood.  Battery had gotten
me good, yet all I wanted was to continue, to push them further, see if
they could make me feel something even close to pain. 

“Enough.” 

I groaned as I turned my focus skyward, finding Legend floating there
and acting as a living bug zapper for my swarm.  Goodie, the fun police
had arrived.  Worse, he was accompanied by Glory Girl, who had her
sister in a princess carry… and Amelia looked pissed. 

/“Do fun nazis count for trophies?”  “I doubt they have the same tattoos
that we loved to tan.”  /

“Good to know I’m a higher priority than the Elite trying to set up
shop,” I coughed out, leaning back against the hull with as much
nonchalance as I could manage.  “Seriously, how many captures did you
get tonight?” 

“Avoiding civilian casualties is always the priority,” Legend responded.

“Translation, none,” I growled, wishing I had my bow or a gun right
about now.  “Maybe next time you can do something about the assholes
trying to set up shop and cause more problems than the assholes who are
already here and on their best behavior.” 

“She calls /this / their best behavior?” Tecton whispered, only to be
elbowed by Vista. 

“Well, up until whatever the Elite were pulling,” I said cheerfully.  I
glanced at Amelia — if she wanted to give up what little remained of her
plausible deniability, that was on her.  To my surprise, she scowled at
me before stomping over and grabbing my arm.  While she fumbled with my
glove, I took my consolation prize from the fight: the expressions on
the heroes’ faces.  “What’s the diagnosis?” 

“No more cactus for you,” she said sternly even as I felt my hand
knitting back together and a rib or three pop back into place.  “Your
adrenaline and hormones are all kinds of fucked up.”  Then she did /
something / that nearly took my feet out from under me as the world
turned fuzzy at the edges.  “Teleport home, get some damn sleep.  I’ll
be back in the morning.”

She practically slammed me back against the hull and turned to the
heroes, yelling something about excessive force and… the number
sixteen?  The other Butchers made similar noises and complaints, but my
head felt fuzzy and I couldn’t focus.

Oh, she had put me to sleep.

The quiet, rational part of my brain cheered and did an awkward dance as
I barely managed to find the correct bug through the relays and
teleported home.  To my surprise, Chrissie was waiting there, and caught
me as I stumbled.  Rather than resist, I allowed her to carry me back to
our room. 

Chapter End Notes

    Chapter 38: Consequence 4.3

Chapter Notes

See the end of the chapter for notes <#endnotes38>

/Sunday May 8th 2011 /

I awoke to a pulsing pressure in my skull that would have been a
migraine if I could still feel pain.  Worse, I woke up alone in my bed
in the lair, but at least I was in my pajamas.  I needed coffee — tea
just wasn’t going to cut it after whatever the hell happened last
night.  Most of my… activities were shrouded in fog, starting vaguely
after smoking something Amelia had made and just chilling on the couch. 
Things got /funky / after that.. 

/Did I actually play pattycake with Mouse Protector, or was that the
drugs? /

/“If by ‘pattycake’ you mean had a bitchin’ sword fight, then yes,” /
Marauder said with something like approval.

/Just what the hell did we do yesterday? /

/“You took twelve people at the same time!” /Butcher said cheerfully. 

What the hell was he on about, twelve people?  I doubt Chrissie would
have allowed an orgy, not with how things were currently between us no
matter the drugs involved.  Just who had I — wait, Mouse Protector, I
had fought her?  Oh god, I had fought the heroes on a drug induced bender…

Fuck, I was turning into Alkaline, or worse, Marauder.

/“Hey!” /

/“At least I didn’t eat someone!” /

I pushed them into the dark before their complaints even started.  Shit,
I needed to find Chrissie (and preferably Lisa), then figure out just
what the hell happened last night.  My predecessors were going to
complain, but there was no way in hell that I was ever going to let
myself go like this.  My powers were too dangerous, even before becoming
the Butcher, and the idea of them off the leash —

Oh FUCK.

Had I killed anyone under the influence?  How much damage had I done to
my efforts with the city over one drug fueled rampage?

I sought out my swarm and searched the arena; I was surprised to see an
all hands on deck meeting happening in the lounge.  Lisa had Amelia in
her lap with Chrissie next to them on the couch, while all of the more
senior capes were spread out among the remaining furniture.  Even Robbie
was there, arms crossed and scowling at the room.

At least the brats weren’t present.  Dinah and Aisha were supposed to
enjoy their weekend after their involvement with the Elite raids and
should be asleep regardless.  As much as I wished that Dinah had warned
us about all this, I didn’t want to contribute to further migraines in
the poor Thinker.  She was with us /specifically / so that we didn’t
abuse her power, unlike certain less scrupulous government paramilitary
organizations.

With a heavy sigh, I teleported directly from my bed to the lounge,
immediately holding up a finger and silencing the room in the wake of my
explosive arrival.  Upon shuffling to the coffee machine, I was relieved
to find coffee brewed from Amelia’s personal stash.  She had expensive
tastes, and right now I just wanted something strong and bitter to wash
away whatever remained from last night. 

Some distant part of me registered the absurdity of this situation — I
was surrounded by killers, schemers, and one of the most dangerous capes
in the whole goddamn world, and yet they were watching quietly as I
shuffled back to the couch and sat down.  The whole situation was eerie
as hell, even ignoring the fact that it was eight in the morning on a
Sunday.

It was Sunday, right?

/“Hell if we know,” / Ironsides grumbled.

The moment was ruined by the fact that the free spot on the couch left
me firmly wedged between Chrissie and Amelia.  My girlfriend carefully
threaded her arm around my lower back while I took a first contented sip
of the glorious bean juice, but it wasn’t until I let out a contented
sigh that everyone, Robbie included, visibly relaxed.

“Alright.  Last night was a clusterfuck of frankly epic proportions.  I
don’t even know where to start because my memory is muddled as shit.”

Several unreadable glances flashed around the room; while Alice
snickered slightly and Elliot just groaned, no one was volunteering to
be the one to be forthcoming.  My addled brain immediately assumed the
worst: I had either done something /extremely / stupid, or worse,
actually killed someone who wasn’t a deserving fucker like Holdout.

Poorly concealed amusement echoed up from the back of my brain, and I
shot my mental roommates an annoyed glance.  /Not gonna fill me in on
that one?  /

/“Nah, we want to see how you react without further spoilers,” /
Sabertooth said. 

/Assholes.  Just for that you can all sit in the dark for a while. /

Mental laughter aside as I pushed them all down, I knew it was going to
be bad when Lisa began with,  “Do you, uh, want chronological order, or
order of most damage to our rep?”

“All I remember clearly at the moment is getting into it with Mouse
Protector,” I said, pinching my nose.  “And even then it’s muddy as
hell.  From now on, keep whatever it was that you created /far / away
from me.” 

The ghost of a smirk passed over Amelia’s face, but it seemed that even
she wasn’t up for schadenfreude right now.  “Already done.  In my
defense, it worked great for the rest of us.  You, on the other hand,
seemed to have some issues with inhibition.”

“You don’t say,” I muttered.  “How many people did I kill?”

Both Lisa and Amelia flinched at that.  “You, personally?  Just one Nazi
cop.”  The memory of the ‘fight’ bubbled up, but Lisa kept going.  “The
boys killed another, and…”

“We used a third as a throwing knife target,” Chrissie finished.  Her
nonchalance was in stark contrast to the other two girls, both of whom
looked actually perturbed.  The senior capes didn’t seem to give a shit,
though Alice did catch my eye and pointedly look the other way.

/“Are your compatriots simply useful, or does she harbor genuine
concern?” / Damascian mused.

/“Hard to tell,” / Chisel admitted.

It wasn’t hard to deduce what the girls had been thinking, given that
Lisa was still on shaky ground with the Teeth as a whole.  Putting on a
spectacle like that was actually pretty clever, but I suspected that
there had been some prodding by Chrissie.  Worse, I couldn’t really
blame her for wanting to help Lisa and Amelia.

Was… was this my fault?  The part of me that had longed to be a hero
(and maybe still did, deep down) felt guilty over corrupting Amelia,
doubly so for getting her entangled with the Teeth.  Lisa had been a
villain already and likely understood what reputation meant in a group
like Teeth, but she wasn’t a killer like… the rest of us.

Lisa’s hand on my leg yanked me back to the present.  “Tay, it’s fine. 
I mean, it’s not /fine / — I’m not a big fan of torture, even if it is
Nazi cops — but it’s definitely not your fault.”  She paused, holding my
gaze until I nodded.  “We’ll just take this as a learning experience,
yeah?  We’re all responsible adults here who can make our own decisions.”

Surprisingly, that elicited a round of murmured agreement from capes and
Butchers alike.  /“She’s right — don’t you dare go all mopey on us,” /
Fester chided.  /“It’s just Nazis.” /

The Thinker continued to stare at me until I nodded again.  Chrissie
followed that up with a supportive squeeze before asking, “Yeah yeah,
we’re all fuckups here.  What was so important downtown that Damien went
along, despite being high on bath salts?”

“Elite fuckin’ with our people,” Elliot grumbled.  “Bastard Son must’ve
been nearby, there were juiced-up goons and capes both.  Killed another
cape, then you showed up and it all went to hell.”

The Butchers cheered at that, but I wasn’t feeling it.  “Alright.  Did
we kill any heroes?”

“Nope,” Alice said, popping the p.

Tension left me that I hadn’t even noticed building up, and I sagged
into Chrissie’s embrace.  “That’s good.  I already faced Legend once,
and I would rather not do it again.”  The last few memories I had from
the night ran through my head.  “Oh, hell.  Amelia —”

“Don’t worry about it,” the grumpy healer(?) replied.  “Crystal and
Sarah were pissed, but not enough to tell Carol, so I haven’t been
kicked out of my house yet.  I can’t tell if Vicky was amused or
horrified when I asked for a lift to detox the Butcher.”

/“Of course the heroes are the goddamn fun police,” / Alkaline groused.

/“Are they heroes, though?” / Sanguine mused.  /“I mean, Amelia is here,
not home…” /

Lisa chewed on her lip for a second before sighing.  “It was your Dad,
actually, who called us.  We were still on this couch watching cartoons
and ignoring pretty much everything.  We sobered up, Chrissie checked
her phone —”

“You were doing awesome, by the way,” my girlfriend said.  “But I
figured you forgot about the whole ‘keep our heads down,’ so I sent a
reminder.”  She reached over and rubbed Amelia’s head, prompting a scowl
and a blush from the freckled girl.  “Thanks for saving my cuddlebug.  I
don’t think any of us want Butcher XVI yet.”

The chorus snickered at that; I ignored both that and the tingle that
ran down my spine.  “Me neither.  Look, it’s fuckass early, and I’m the
only Noctis cape here.  I’m going to head home and clean myself up.  Oh,
and new rule.”  That made everyone tense up, with the senior capes
shooting me death glares.  “Butcher sticks to weed.”

 

------------------------------------------------------------------------

 

Leaving the lair for home was harder than I expected.  After my
declaration, I had tried to enjoy my coffee in peace but instead had
been cuddle-piled by Chrissie, Amelia, and Lisa.  Maybe it was the
morning-after effects of Amelia’s invention, maybe it was the temporary
jaunt into ‘insane Butcher’ land, or maybe it was the fleeting brush
with death the night before, but I found myself just as intoxicated by
the positive human contact.

Alkaline rambled about oxytocin and MDMA in the back of my head, but
otherwise the Butchers had also been largely content to just sit quietly
and enjoy the ambience.  It was nice, but I couldn’t help but wonder if
they were only quiescent because of the violence the night before.

I resolved to refuse to indulge for their sake.

Eventually Lisa had actually fallen asleep, and I managed to free myself
without teleporting out from under Chrissie.  We made plans to meet up
at the park later, and then three quick teleports took me most of the
way home.  The sound really was distinctive, so I usually tried to walk
a few blocks to at least keep up the pretense that the Butcher didn’t
live nearby.

As I walked, the fog from the night before slowly began to clear.  While
I wanted to rage and scream at the pile of complications I had
recklessly created for my ‘show Butcher XV is sane’ scheme, the most I
could summon was a mild annoyance.  I had kept collateral damage to a
minimum, I had avoided pain blasting people — hell, I had even bantered
with Mouse Protector!

/“Pain shake,” / Quarrel provided unhelpfully, only to be shouted at by
all of the others.

Yeah.  Last night was /fun /.

That was a problem.

Still, I could do a bit of damage control right now, so as I turned onto
my street, I pulled out my cell phone and thumbed through the contacts. 
I considered calling the ex-villain in question, but even I hadn’t
fallen so far as to wake people up early.  Thus, I was rather surprised
when he responded quickly.

 

/T - Hey, sorry about last night.  Wanna grab a beer and talk about it?/

/A - Blerrgh… so damn early.  Weaver, I respect the hell out of you
sometimes, but a beer isn’t going to cut it after last night./

/T - How about at Somer’s Rock?/

/A - Okay, that’s probably a good idea./

/T - Civvies?  Reduce the chance of a repeat./

/A - I’ll kick it up the chain.  Now let me sleep./

 

Chisel nodded in approval at the tactic.  /“I doubt that the heroes
would have done something stupid, but Legend is in town and the Teeth
aren’t exactly laser-proof.” /  Several of the more tactically-minded
Butchers murmured in agreement, but there was a conspicuous voice missing.

/Reflex? /

/“Try to avoid further conflict,” / he muttered, then shut right up.  I
got the sense that he had retreated, somehow, into the back of my head.

/“Reflex?” / Damascian asked, only to be met with further
silence.  /“Ah, that is… worrying.” /

I didn’t have much time to consider that unfortunate development, having
arrived at my front porch.  With my frankly absurd range, I had known
that Dad was home and awake.  In fact, he was anxiously pacing in the
living room, occasionally stopping to take a sip of his coffee.

/“You could just go back to the lair,” / Fester offered.  /“Chrissie is
there, not to mention Amelia.  I’m sure they would be happy to take your
mind off of things.” /

/“Can you imagine the look on her old man’s face if he ever found out
that his daughter slept with the Butcher?” / Sanguine said with a laugh.

“Quiet,” I muttered under my breath.

/“Kid, you’re being absurd,” / Marauder tried, but I punted him into the
dark before he could continue.  Then, before any of the others could
raise an objection, I opened the door and prepared myself for yet
another unpleasant conversation with my father.

“Taylor?” Dad yelled as soon as I stepped inside.  He darted into the
hallway only to hesitate, looking as though he wanted to give me a hug
but couldn’t figure out how to approach me.  “You came home.”

Beetles had already untied my shoes, letting me hop from one foot to the
other to pull them off.  “Uh, yeah?”

“Why?”

I tilted my head at Dad.  “To get clothes and books?  We’re going to —”

“Damn it Taylor, that’s not what I meant!” he retorted, suddenly angry
but also clearly exhausted.  “I want to know why you did… everything
that you did last night.  Why were you fighting the heroes?  You said
you were trying to be better!  And let’s not get started on those men
that you maimed.  Nazis or no, it’s wrong to torture people like that!”

/“Is… is he serious right now?”  “I think so.”  “How did Annette ever —” /

“Shut the hell up,” I barked, waving my hand around my head.  “Not you,
Dad.  These assholes.”

The casual reminder of my personal hell seemed to take the wind of his
sails momentarily, but Dad rallied, crossing his arms and doing his
damnedest to glare at me.  “Taylor, look, I understand that —”

“Do you?” I cut in.  “I could have sworn we already had this
conversation, and it was abundantly clear that you didn’t understand.”

“Young lady, do not cut me off.  After seeing you brutally murder a man
yesterday, I am very concerned about your behavior and what you have
been doing in costume.  I know that you have… them, in your head, but
that doesn’t give you a license to just do whatever you want.”

/“I’m pretty sure being the Butcher is exactly that,” / Pyro said
enthusiastically.  /“What’s the fuckin’ point, otherwise?” /

Dad obviously couldn’t hear her rejoinder, but he could see the smile on
my face and clearly didn’t like it.  “Taylor, take this seriously!  You…
you don’t even realize how much you have changed, do you?  Please,
please tell me that you still recognize that killing people is wrong.”

“Kind of a low bar there, Dad.  Thanks for that,” I said, twirling the
end of my braid around in a circle.  “But believe it or not, I really
don’t like killing people.  The other Butchers make fun of me for it,
actually.”

He frowned at me, but there was something less than pleased in his
eyes.  “Just yesterday, I saw you backhand a man’s head clean off his
shoulders.”

I pushed down the Butchers’ cheers at the reminder.  “Yeah, that was an
accident.”

“An accident.”

“In my defense —”

“Taylor.”  Dad’s voice carried an odd finality.  “Please, before you
come up with an excuse, let me ask you: what would your mother say?”

/“That asshole!” / Fester screeched.  /“Taylor, let me outta here like
you did for Reflex so I can sting his stupid ass!” /

Tempting as it was to just send Dad a literal pointed reminder of my
situation, I wasn’t about to send my bugs after my own father.  Instead,
I pulled together a swarm next to me and did my best to shape it like
Fester when she had been alive.  Putting the minor mental effort into
channeling one of the voices’ thoughts without thinking too carefully
about it, I let Fester talk.

“Oh, I have been /waiting / for this moment,” Fester buzzed gleefully. 
“Hello, Daniel.”

Dad actually gulped at that, taking a step back from the construct.  “K-
kimmie?”

“The one and fuckin’ only!” she replied.  “What’s this shit about trying
to guilt Taylor with her dead mother?  You knew Annette as well as I
did, and she would be /cheering / to see Kaiser impaled up the butt with
a flagpole!”

“Kim—”

“They’re Nazis, you dumb motherfucker!  Literal /fucking / Nazis!  Krieg
wore a goddamn SS uniform!  Killing them is an American tradition as old
as racism and the patriarchy!”

I almost rolled my eyes at Fester’s comments, but I knew she was doing
it just to wind Dad up and frankly he deserved it after the second
comment about Mom in as many days.

“I don’t give a shit about Nazis, Kim!  I’m worried about /Taylor /, and
what you maniacs are doing to her!  Can’t you see how much she has
changed!?”

“How someone as smart as Annette married a dumbass like you, I’ll never
know.”  I had the bug construct cross its arms.  “Everyone changes,
dipshit, it’s called growing up and capes get it especially bad. 
Remember that time you got drunk as a teenager and crashed your dad’s
truck into a telephone pole?”  Dad winced, which I was not expecting. 
“Big fuckin’ deal.  Taylor tried some drugs and forgot to pull her
punches.  And we /both / know that Annette would have been in the
stands, cheering.”

Dad seemed to deflate at that.  “Kim, please.”

“Please what?  I don’t —”  I dismissed the bug construct at that, and
while Fester just burst into laughter in my head, I didn’t find it hard
to keep the mirth off of my face.

“Look, Dad, I didn’t even hurt the heroes yesterday… much, anyways,” I
admitted, thinking about Chevalier.  “I got high, there was a weird
interaction.  I spent most of the time on the couch cuddling with
Chrissie.  I fought the heroes, but only because they were fighting us
instead of getting rid of Bastard Son and the other Elite.  Now can
you /please / stop bringing up Mom when you’re angry at me?”

/“Or you could just pain blast him when he does,” / Sabertooth growled. 
I was definitely not doing that.

Dad stared at me for a long minute after that, a series of conflicting
emotions playing out over his face.  “Taylor, you… your Mom may not be
here, but I know she would be proud of you right now.  Even with the whole…”

I rolled my eyes, mostly to ignore the sudden wetness.  “Yeah, I’m
Butcher XV.  Kind of hard to forget it.”

/“For your enemies, as well,” / Stratego added.

“Yes, that.  And it’s true that both of us lived, ah, interesting lives
before you were born, but the most important thing that a parent wants
is to leave a better world for their kids than the one they grew up in. 
Is this really the legacy you want to leave for your kids?”

“Not really, but it’s the legacy that has been handed to me.  I’m going
to make the most of the hand I was dealt.” 

“And how many bodies will be laid at the foundation of that legacy?” 

I scowled at Dad, and to his credit, he didn’t look away.  “Too many,
and at the same time, not enough.  There are people that deserve to die
— I killed one of them yesterday, and I’m sure there will be others that
don’t deserve it too.”  I leaned against the wall, fighting the urge to
slump to the floor and instead looking to the ceiling.  “I can remember
thousands of murders, from their point of view and others.  I remember
what it was like to have a knife pierce someone’s heart, or for it to
pierce my own.  I can vividly recall a certain brunette caving in a
rapist’s skull while her girlfriend laughed about it.  Did you know that
Mom killed people?  I certainly didn’t before I inherited.” 

“Of course I knew,” Dad said, sounding defeated.  “I just wanted better
for you.” 

“I wanted better for me too,” I said softly.  “That ship has sailed, but
I’ll be damned if I don’t do what I can to make life better for the
people who live here in the Bay.” 

“Then be better!” Dad snapped.  “Rise above those who refuse to act,
don’t succumb to the temptations to do things the easy way.  Be someone
your children can be proud of.”

Children.  Having kids of my own was not something I had /ever /
considered, even before having a bunch of assholes move into my head.  A
few of the Butchers had been fathers, but none were mothers.  Thus, I
had some memories of bright eyed kids looking up at their father with
unfettered affection.

My mind drifted back to the unambiguously nice part of yesterday —
Chrissie, Amelia, Lisa, and me cuddled up on the couch.

In my mind’s eye, I could suddenly see miniature versions of each of
them running around the lounge while an exasperated Robbie helped Dinah
arrange poisonous flowers in her hair for prom.  Through it all, I
brushed the hair of a girl that had unruly curls but a bright smile.  It
was a rose tinted picture of the future, one I was almost certain to
never see, but at the same time… 

I wanted it for myself.

“I can’t make promises, but I can try.” 

Dad’s eyes flashed with something, but I didn’t stick around, not
wanting him to see the emotion within my own.  His rambling had gotten
to me in a way few had; not even Emma at her worst had managed to stir
up my emotions quite like this.  I hadn’t dared to hope for a better
future in so long that it had taken angry mentions of Mom to remind me
that such a thing might exist.

Then again, no Butcher had lasted for more than a few years once the
inheritance became known.

To my delight, when I finally teleported back into the lounge, I found
Chrissie and the others asleep where I had left them.  Lisa woke up just
long enough to raise a single inquisitive eyebrow, but instead of
unnecessary smugness and probing questions, she just shifted around so
that I could crawl back into the pile.

“Fair at 1pm,” she murmured.  “I set an alarm.”

That was good enough for me.

 

------------------------------------------------------------------------

 

“I know I’m not supposed to enjoy this, but I am,” Amelia complained
around a mouthful of funnel cake.  She made an annoyed gesture at the
food truck selling fried everything behind us, ‘Sinful Treats,’ which
had been obviously repainted in red and gray recently.  “I know subtlety
doesn’t mean anything to us, but —”

“Us?” Chrissie interjected, munching on her own fried butter.  “Can’t be
a full member until you kill someone.”

Amelia grabbed at Chrissie, deadpanning, “Are you volunteering?”  My
girlfriend dodged the biokinetic’s first swipe, but Amelia wasn’t
deterred and they started a chase in earnest.  Lisa rolled her eyes at
the antics; I didn’t bother to hide my own amusement mixed with my
predecessors’ smug enjoyment.  I was sure that Chrissie wearing her VX
hoodie in public had nothing to do with it.

/“Marquis would be so proud,” / Sabertooth said, drawing up a few
memories of the man.  /“Still can’t believe he had a kid.” /

/“I can’t believe he went to the Birdcage over her,” / Fester agreed. 
For all that she hated the other villain, her opinion of him had
improved when Lisa revealed just how the Brigade had ‘defeated’ him. 
None of us had any doubt that he would have raised Amelia as a
supervillain, but joining the Teeth?  Even we were still a little surprised.

Speaking of surprise, I had not been able to contain my laughter when
the first of the food trucks that the Teeth had ‘acquired’ from New York
and Boston rolled into the Protectorate’s desperate attempt to control
the narrative yesterday.  I had been on a roof at the time, listening
through my bugs as the displeased authorities discovered that all of the
paperwork had been filed correctly, though Lisa had timed everything so
that the trucks arrived just in time for lunch.

They had all, of course, been repainted in our colors and rebranded
appropriately.

Sending them home was not an option at that point, as the crowd milling
about to meet the so-called heroes had descended on the food like bugs
on local pharmaceutical executives.  Watching the New York Wards drag
the local team (along with the other visiting Wards) to their favorite
pizza truck had put all of us into a fit of side-splitting laughter.

Of course, that hadn’t compared to the amusement of seeing Jouster not
only give me his civilian number, but also drag the rest of the Wards
over to sit with us.  I hadn’t even needed Madison to manipulate things
to make it happen, the horny bastard did it all for us.

The other impressive bit of planning was Charlotte, summoning a whole
swarm of our less murderous but no less dedicated teenage members
(mostly from Winslow) for this second day of events.  They had come
dressed tastefully in our colors or various insect-themed attire,
meaning that I didn’t stick out very much with a black t-shirt lined
with spider webbing and jeans with my XV hoodie around my waist, topped
off with oversized aviator sunglasses.  My hair was currently in a
ponytail rather than a braid just for the added step of removal after
last night, which may have been a mistake.

I had inspired a new hairstyle — braids were almost universally in,
apparently, given that the Butcher wore her hair as such.  I had used
Damascian’s various complicated four strand patterns mostly out of
muscle memory, and girls around the Bay had taken that as a challenge to
find their own ornate designs… provided that their hair was long
enough.  Others had copied Chrissie’s shorter punk style, something she
complained about constantly.

“I really need to buy Charlotte a nice bottle of wine or something,”
Lisa said as we walked through the overrun park.  Her hoodie was the
classic red on gray, with a stylized purple all-seeing-eye on the back
under her last name.  It had been a fight to manage that much, as she
wanted the whole thing in purple until Chrissie reminded her how much
that would stand out.  “I’m pretty sure Battery is about to blow a
gasket; she looks up to Legend big time and we’re making her look
terrible today.  Triumph isn’t happy either, but that’s not new… If not
for console telling him off, I think Jouster would have done something
stupid.”

/“The Wards are also going around in twos and threes, when a typical
event is often solo practice for the older Wards,” /Stratego said.  I
relayed the observation to Lisa, who snorted in amusement.

“Some of the visiting Wards didn’t appreciate just how fucked they are
until now.”  She pointed to Amelia and Chrissie, as the former was being
confronted by a fan of her own and the latter was laughing her ass off. 
“And New Wave’s absence is certainly conspicuous.”

/“Forget the Wards, all of the visiting muscle is here today,” / Chisel
murmured.  /“Chevalier is annoying but manageable and tough as any
Brute.  Legend obviously has to pull his punches if he doesn’t want to
become XVI.  Myrddin, however, loves his tricks, which you saw first
hand last night.” /

/“Cowards,” / Knockout spat.  /“Won’t fight like a real man.” /  I
pushed him away for the comment, so he kept his irritation to mumbles.

We wandered like that, occasionally stopping at a food truck for some of
the Butchers’ requests as they burned their food votes for old
favorites.  Lisa’s smirk answered my unasked question about why she
hunted down these specific food trucks, which turned into a genuine grin
when Amelia and Chrissie eventually reappeared.  The healer had switched
to wearing her own personalized hoodie — her last name was apparently
‘Lavere’ — with an obviously venomous snake wrapping the Rod of
Asclepius on the back.

/  /“I’m so sick of people,” Amelia hissed from inside her hood.  “It’s
usually Vicky’s job to deal with the fans and bullshit, but of course
the heroes have to have a stick in their ass about New Wave after last
night and so she’s off making out with Ashley or whatever.”

I cocked a single eyebrow at Chrissie, who returned it with a shrug and
a smile.  “Hey, don’t look at me.  I’m pretty sure I scared off a few,
but if they’re brave enough to come annoy the healer, what should I do?”

Marauder started ranting about how Chrissie should have just cut them,
but we had already decided to avoid any and all power usage this

sure what would happen, but I didn’t think any of us would like it.

Lisa reached a hand into Amelia’s hood and started scratching, prompting
a noise from her girlfriend that was probably not fit for public. 
“Fuuuucccck, I hate being an outed cape,” Amelia complained.

“At least the heroes are leaving you alone,” I pointed out.  “I half
expected them to jump my ass already after last night.” 

Amelia rolled her eyes before leaning into Lisa’s scratching.  “Don’t
give them any ideas.  Jouster recognized me, I think, which is why I

“Funnel cake,” Lisa replied immediately.

“Sometimes I hate your know-it-all ass,” Amelia grumbled.

“Well, most of them will be sticking around…” the Thinker said, only for

Taylor… but I think Chevalier has you figured out.”

“What?” I hissed, echoing the sentiment of the now clamoring Butchers. 
“I mean, we’re not exactly hiding, but he’s halfway across the park!” 
Indeed, my bugs reported that he was with the gaggle of senior heroes
signing autographs near the middle of the park, but I couldn’t bring

Lisa shook her head slowly.  “Not sure how he did it… hm, they’re not
surprised that you’re here, or at least they aren’t scrambling to do
something stupid.”

“That’s a first,” Chrissie said with an exaggerated eye roll.

“I’ll need to get closer to see more… want to go meet the heroes?”

I tapped the side of my head.  “Pretty sure I’ve met them all at least
once, but sure.”

With unnecessary flourish, Lisa reached into her bag and produced a
stack of postcards.  “It would be suspicious if we just walked right up
to them, so we need to do the rounds, first.”

Amelia groaned.  “/That’s / why you wanted those New Wave postcards?”

“Yep,” Lisa said.  “Plus I’ve got a few commemorating the Nazi defeat in
WWII, some Mouse Protector cards, some PR internal blanks with things
like ‘action photo here’ or ‘catchphrase two,’ and finally… anti-
bullying pamphlets used by the PRT in NYC!”

My initial laughter died an awkward death at the last reveal, though the
Butchers continued in my head like the assholes they were.  Lisa’s eyes
went wide with panic, and she quickly said, “Wait, sorry Tay, I knew
this was a sore subject, but —”

School might be tolerable now, but that did nothing to erase the memories.

/“Oh come on, it’s just a joke,” / Sanguine started, followed by Alkaline.

/“It’s clever, too.  And she doesn’t —” /

I shook my head, pushing the Butchers away like so many annoying gnats
and taking a deep breath.  Chrissie enveloped me in a hug, which
honestly helped more than any number of breathing exercises.  “It’s
fine.  Appropriate, even, and I hope that Legend notices.  Do you think
they know?”

“I know they know,” Lisa said carefully.

“Then good, give me a stack.”  Lisa fished the piles of stationary out
of her pockets and gave each of us a marker.  Against my better
judgment, I stole a glance at the bullying pamphlet — they were as
filled with meaningless platitudes as I expected.  ‘Don’t be afraid to
reach out to the authorities’ really didn’t mean much when it was the
authorities doing the bullying.

“Even I know this is dumb as hell,” Amelia said, waving one of the
pamphlets.  “But the New Wave ones are great.  I’m going to get them to
sign my own.”

With that, we set off.  My disguise wasn’t perfect, apparently, but it
was good enough to fool everyone else.  The park wasn’t so full that we
were shoulder-to-shoulder with other people, but the clusters around
each hero were dense enough that I almost missed having everyone leap
out of my way.  Amelia was in a similar situation, but I felt that she
would be complaining either way — showing up in costume would have been
a mild problem.

Her Panacea costume, that is; showing up in her Pandemic costume would
be much more problematic.

/“One must wonder if the PRT is aware of her dual identity,” / Damascian
mused.  /“They are not known for their flexibility in that regard, even
if Amelia hasn’t committed any crimes.” /

/“They’ll just invent some charges,” / Ironsides grumbled.

“So is being a hero really all it’s cracked up to be?” Chrissie asked as
we waited to meet the first group: Madison and Lily.  I only knew the
latter’s name after having met her the other afternoon, but she had
seemed like a nice enough girl.

“Fuck no,” Amelia spat.  “Well, maybe at first, but it gets old
quickly.  Vicky loves it, so make of that what you will.  There’s a lot
of dealing with /people /.”  I was amazed at how much bitterness and
disappointment could be crammed into one word, and even Chrissie

Lisa clutched her chest.  “But think about the merchandising!”

“You say that until little kids are wearing branded underwear,” Amelia
said softly.  “The PR disaster over Armsmaster branded panties is the

“Oh yeah, I had a pack of those,” I said, tapping my chin.  

“Seriously?” Amelia asked.  “Those never made it to the public, they
were recalled.” 

I shrugged.  “Perk of having a father working the docks, he got me a
pack before they made it to the PRT gift shop.” 

“You still have them?” Chrissie asked with a twinkle in her eye.  “Just
imagine the shitstorm on PHO if it got out that Weaver had a pair.” 

“I will pay you millions if you do it,” Lisa suddenly said.  “Just think
of the trolling we could do.  Think of asking him to autograph them.  I
need this in my life, Tay.”

“Down girl,” Amelia said, pulling at Lisa’s own jacket.  “Let’s just
stick to postcards and plushies for now.  Bad enough the hospitals have

Lisa sighed.  “Fucking Carol, you aren’t even seeing a dime of the
merchandising revenue from that either.” 

“Part of why I’m glad nobody would buy a Pandemic plushie.” She muttered
