    Chapter 40: Consequence 4.4

Chapter Notes

    We're back, baby!

See the end of the chapter for more notes <#endnotes40>

/Monday May 9th, 2011 /

“You wanted to see me, Principal Blackwell?” 

The stern woman looked up from her computer as I strode into her office,
her face twisted into a scowl when she saw my shirt.  The ‘Skulls for
the Skull Throne’ tee had been a great find at the fair and I was
wearing it proudly under my unzipped hoodie.

/“We have merch now,” / Chisel said for the eighth time, faint
wonderment in her normally stoic voice.  /“How did we end up with merch?” /

/By doing the same shit we are right now, / I thought back with a
smirk. /  The best part is, I don’t have to say ‘told you so.’ /

The Butchers grumbled at that, but they mostly quieted down so I could
deal with whatever bullshit the school wanted this time.  “Ms. Hebert,
please have a seat,” Blackwell said, gesturing to the chair across from
her desk.

“I hope this won’t take long,” I replied as I took the offered seat.  “I
have extracurriculars this morning that I am missing to talk to you.” 

/“Missing, riiight,” / Marauder said with a snort.

Fester rolled her eyes.  /“Oh come on, look at them, they’re thrilled to
have a bug clone standing in.” /

/“Chrissie’s even cuddling with it,” / Sabertooth noted. 

Alkaline huffed.  /“We’re missing out on Amelia’s weed though!” / 

/I took a hit before we left, so you aren’t missing anything. /

“I’m sure,” Principal Blackwell said.  “Now, it is my understanding
you’ve been taking steps to transfer to Arcadia and were placed on their
waitlist.”  She then slid a small stack of papers across her desk. 
“Congratulations, you’ve been accepted and they’re willing to work you
in, starting next week.” 

/“What?” / several voices said at once, and horror of horrors, my gut
reaction was not excitement.  Even just six weeks ago I would have been
thrilled to have an escape from Winslow in any form, never mind my dream
transfer to a school with heroes and teachers that cared.  But now, with
Chrissie and the rest of the Teeth — /my / Teeth — stuck here, I found
myself eying the stack of paper with some trepidation.

“Who submitted the request?” I asked as I began to thumb through the
forms.  All of them were filled out digitally and lacked either my or my
father’s signature.  “The last request I made for a transfer was made in
the fall of twenty ten and your secretary refused to process the
paperwork.” 

/“Well, depending on one’s definition of ‘processed,’” / Damascian said
with a scowl.

“She must have done so, if this was completed,” Principal Blackwell said
as she turned her attention back to the computer.  “It shows the
application was processed on April twenty fifth and approved this
Friday.  That is unusual.”

I couldn’t help but laugh, which was echoed in my own head.  “Oh Chevy,
you misguided fool.”

/“Legend’s also a possibility,” / Quarrel said.  /“You better not be
thinking about leaving our guys behind —” /

/Obviously not. /

“Chevy?  Is that a nickname for someone?” Principal Blackwell asked. 

/“Holy shit, she doesn’t know!” / Butcher cheered. 

/“You better make this count!” / Knockout added. 

I leaned back in my chair, propping it up on two legs.  “Chevalier, head
of the Protectorate down in Philly.  He’s mildly well known.  The date
matches when he arrived in town after the Kaiser special,” I said while
shaking my head.  “Hm… he probably thinks that the Arcadia Wards would
be a better influence on me than the remaining Winslow Wards.  Or Armsy
finally decided that I’m a bad influence on them, could be either.” 

“There are no Wards at Winslow,” Principal Blackwell said a bit too quickly.

I grinned unnaturally wide with the help of Sabertooth’s power.  “Oh
come now, Principal Blackwell.  I know that the truth is not usually
high on your list of priorities when dealing with me, but even you can’t
be that blind.  I’m sure that Maddy’s sudden decision to treat me as a
person is completely uncorrelated with Emma’s mental breakdown after she
and Sophia tried to corner me in a bathroom again.”

“No —” she spluttered, but I bulldozed right over her.

“I mean, Emma is obviously not doing so hot at the moment, but she hit
me hard enough to cave my face in if I had been a normal person.”  I
gestured to my still-sharp teeth.  “As you might have finally noticed,
I’m not.”

“I doubt that…” Principal Blackwell said, but trailed off after glancing
at me again.

Rather than answer, I had a bug activate the intercom.  “Madison
Clements, please report to Principal Blackwell’s office.” 

“How did you?” she muttered, staring at the button atop her desk,
unaware of the bugs within the guts of the device.  “What game is this?” 

“You haven’t been paying much attention, have you?” I asked as I stood. 
A small fraction of my swarm made their way to me from the shadows of
Blackwell’s office, coalescing around me in a tiny storm of clicks and
hisses.  The spiders that usually lived in my hair crawled out, and I
held up a finger to let one escape from my cheekbone to the back of my
hand.  “It’s not like I’m hiding, you know,” I said along with my
swarm.  “You’d have to be willfully ignorant to miss the new reality of
Winslow now that I’ve taken over.”

Principal Blackwell’s eyes widened, her breath coming in increasingly
short huffs.  Luckily Madison appeared before she could have a heart
attack, and I set about banishing the swarm as the Ward opened the
door.  “Principal Blackwell?” they asked, only to blink in confusion
upon seeing me standing there, covered in my swarm.  “Taylor, knock it
off with the plagues of Egypt schtick.  This is a school and those bugs
are disgusting.”

“Hey Maddy,” I said cheerfully as the buzzing stopped and the bugs
themselves disappeared.  “Sorry to drag you into this, but Blackwell has
questions and I figured this was faster.”

“Of course she does,” Madison muttered and took the other empty seat. 
“Don’t let Taylor scare you, she’s all bluster until you give her an
actual reason to act.” 

I hummed, but couldn’t resist dropping a barb.  “Like covering up my
trigger event?  Would that count?” 

Madison glared at me while Principal Blackwell paled.  “No, what counted
was when Hookwolf went after your father.  If you were going to extract
your pound of flesh from us, you would have already done so.” 

/“Just for that you should rot their face off,” / Fester said. 

/“Can’t let people say the Butcher is predictable,” / Marauder added. 

Alkaline scoffed.  /“That’s exactly what they want, dumbass.” / 

I rolled my eyes at the usual banter and pressed on.  “True enough. 
Anyway, apparently our friends from out of town think it would be a good
idea to transfer me to Arcadia and put it all through without my
permission.”

“Are they stupid?” Madison said, pinching their nose.  “Aren’t they
worried that, I don’t know, Weaver will take offense to this?  I doubt
she will appreciate having one of her capes relocated under, uh, false
pretenses.”

It took me a long second of thinking — not helped by the Butchers’
riotous laughter — to parse that statement.  Were they implying that I
was a different cape?  Or that I was pretending to be a cape and that
Weaver… might find out?  Did that count as violating the Unwritten
Rules, even if I was masquerading as myself?

A quick glance at Madison showed that they were just as confused.

/“This is what happens when the Teeth try to get clever,” / Butcher
sneered.  /“Just punch her in the face!” /

Luckily, Blackwell was just as confused, so I was able to snatch up the
whole stack of paper and work Fester’s power on it.  “Well, whatever the
issue, I’m turning this down.  I was hoping that the heroes would be
better behaved than this, but I suppose that is what I get for meeting
my idols.  I’ll need to get in touch with Tattletale today, get this
mess straightened out and make our plans for Winslow clear.” 

“Plans?” Principal Blackwell squeaked. 

/“Almost forgot she was here,” / Knockout muttered. 

/“You’re just easily distracted,” / Stratego said.  /“Do you want to
risk the plan being disturbed because you told her?” / 

/If anything, Blackwell will jump on it for the increased funding.  /

/“You hope,” / Damascian cautioned.  /“Do not jeopardize your goals for
short term satisfaction.” /

/“Yes, mom,” / the chorus answered as Damascian grumbled. 

Tapping my finger on the desk, I sent ripples through the wood with
Chisel’s power.  “Keeping it vague — the Teeth are going to funnel money
into Winslow to help elevate it to the same standards as Arcadia.  This
will mean oversight from our Thinkers to make sure you aren’t
squandering funds like you are currently.” 

“So no embezzling beyond the money allocated to pay her off, right?”
Madison asked. 

“Basically,” I agreed.  I could tell Madison was amused that I just
admitted to planning a federal crime so casually.  “Tats has it worked
out and is figuring out the best way to make it look legit on the
surface.  She should have it all lined up by summer break.”

For the first time this entire conversation, I /finally / seemed to have
grabbed Blackwell’s full attention.  I found it darkly amusing that she
was more interested in money and potential crimes than the literal
Butcher sitting across the desk from her.  “You’re blackmailing me,”
Principal Blackwell muttered as she slumped back in her chair and let
out a mirthless chuckle.  “Fuck it, I’m being blackmailed by the Butcher
and a Ward is helping her.” 

“Weaver,” Madison and I said at the same moment.  

I rolled my eyes.  “Well, I’ve pretty much embraced my role as the
Butcher, but I do still prefer to be called Weaver.  I do hope you
respect that.” 

“It’s not like remembering preferred names and gender is difficult,”
Madison snarked. 

“Quite right!” I said cheerfully.  “So, Principal Blackwell, you’re
going to call Arcadia and tell them I’ve declined the invitation.  Then
you’re going to call your contact at the PRT and ask why they thought it
was a good idea to try to bend the Rules.  Tell them Weaver was curious.” 

I stared the odious woman in the eyes until she finally sagged onto her
desk, looking a decade older.  “I can do that,” Principal Blackwell said
weakly. 

“Excellent!” I said and stood.  Outside, my bug clone dispersed as the
meeting with the rest of the Teeth adjourned.  “If that’s all, I have
classes to attend.  I need to set a good example for my people and
encourage them to get a proper education.” 

/“You’ll cut our number of recruits with this plan,” / Sanguine complained. 

/“It will also increase those sympathetic to us within influential
stations,” / Stratego stated. 

Pyro chuckled.  /“Never thought I’d see the day that the Teeth became
the next Marche.” / 

/“The man would be proud, especially of his daughter,” / Butcher said. 

“Madison,” Blackwell said before we stepped out.  “Is she a threat?  Are
you being coerced?” 

I turned, raising an eyebrow at the principal, but she didn’t wilt
nearly as much as I expected to have my attention on her; Madison
sighed.  “No, Taylor is not influencing me other than being a friend. 
Not that you’ll believe me since she is standing right here, but you can
talk to Assault if you’re concerned.” 

We left Blackwell to her silent consideration, giving the secretary a
wasp sting on the inside of her nose when she tried to stop us.  Petty,
maybe, but she had been just as bad (if not worse) than her boss — I
couldn’t help but snicker a bit, thinking about all of my stuff she had
shredded.  “Mm, I think that there’s still doughnuts,” I mused, sending
some bugs to inspect the bag in Chrissie’s hands.  “Do you have munchies
too?”

Madison was silent for a few steps, long enough that I spun to face them
to make sure that everything was alright.  “Taylor… Why did you sting
that secretary?”

/“Why not?”  “I mean, come on —” “Should have pain blasted her.”  “Or
set her on fire!” /

“Well, she —”

Madison shook their head.  “No.  Stop and /think / for a second.  Was
that really necessary?  You /laughed / at her!”

“She laughed at me!” I retorted, only to find myself being dragged
bodily by the telekinetic down the hall and into an empty classroom. 
Even without teleporting, I had a half dozen ways I could have freed
myself from the Ward’s vice-like grip, but to be honest I found their
sudden insistence confusing enough to just follow along.  It wasn’t like
they could really do much to me.

/“Except become Butcher XVI,” / Sanguine offered unhelpfully.  /“Might
be nice to have a real Changer power again.” /

/“Yeah, maybe we wouldn’t be allergic to bees!” / Alkaline added.  She
and Knockout started making buzzing noises at Quarrel again, and the
resulting shouting match distracted me until Madison was shutting the
classroom door behind us.

Some part of them must have recognized that they had just manhandled the
Butcher out of costume, because Madison spent the next minute or two
just pacing out of arm's reach from me.  I used a small cluster of bugs
to tell Chrissie to drop a doughnut off at Mrs. Knott’s classroom before
Madison finally spoke up.  “I didn’t want to bring this up with an
audience, and it’s going to sound rich coming from /me / of all people,
but have you… Have you noticed how much you have changed in the last month?”

/“Pain blast that bitch!” / Butcher roared, only to get punted into the
dark.

Knockout had a different idea.  /“Nah, punch ‘em in their sanctimonious
face!” /  He joined Butcher in the void.  I agreed with the sentiment,
though — a very loud part of me wanted to smack that concerned look
right off of Madison’s face for having the gall to approach me on MY
attitude.

Memories of Blackwell’s self-satisfied smirk surfaced in my mind, and
that of her fucking secretary.  Those evil, self-interested fucks
probably would have let the literal heroes kill me if it meant not
disrupting their corrupt little fiefdom.  It took me becoming one of the
scariest supervillains in the country to actually get them to treat me
with something even approaching respect.

What the hell was a wasp sting against ruining my future?  If I had to
throw around the Butcher’s weight to get them to actually treat the less
popular or important kids with the respect they deserved, then I was
perfectly happy to do so.  Someone had to make sure that kids could
actually learn around here, and the fact that it had to be /me / was —

/“They have a point,” / Stratego rumbled suddenly, drawing me out of my
cycle of anger and back to Madison’s original point.

Chisel nodded.  /“Every Butcher changes, it’s sort of in the job
description.” /

/“As a point of fact, you have changed considerably less than us,” /
Damascian said, sending memories of her downward spiral and
mine.  /“Although that is hardly reassuring in the present company.” /

“Taylor?”

“What?” I snapped.  “I’m aware —”

/“Madison is right to be concerned,” / Reflex cut in quietly.  /“Don’t
try to rationalize it.” /

Scowling, I sent a mental glare back to my headmate while the other
Butchers shouted him back into oblivion… only to have a memory of /me /
shouting the hero down alongside the rest of the collective during my
drug induced bender nudged right back. 

Fuck.

I took a deep breath, forcing myself to relax by leaning against the
wall.  “You… aren’t the first to bring it up.  I’ve always had a temper,
and becoming the Butcher hasn’t really done me any favors in that
regard… Not to mention that I’m not really sure anymore where ‘Taylor’
ends and ‘Butcher XV’ begins.”

/“Don’t you dare go soft on us now!” / Marauder bellowed.

/Shut up. /

While I glared the last few stragglers into submission, Madison seemed
to deflate as my words registered in their head.  Only then did I
realize that Stratego’s power had been subtly pinging me about their
combat readiness; I might have had several good reasons to hurt Madison,
but I had mostly put that behind me… right?

Then why did I sting the secretary?

“I won’t pretend to know what it’s like to have all of those voices and
memories,” Madison said slowly.  “I don’t even know if there’s anything
I can say or do at this point to help you, assuming you even want help. 
This is sort of the point of the Wards — surround unstable young
teenagers with power with friends so that they’re marginally less likely
to go crazy.”

The Butchers actually stopped arguing long enough to laugh at that, but
for once, I didn’t feel it.  “I have the Teeth.”

Madison rolled their eyes.  “Don’t insult both of our intelligence. 
They want Butcher and are literally willing to kill for it.  Chrissie…
you’ve sort of changed her mind, I think.  She likes you more than she
likes Butcher now, but she’ll be right next to you on the road to hell. 
Honestly I would suggest Lisa or Amelia, but given their little fiasco
with the knife throwing…”

“Fiasco?”

“This is what I mean!” Madison snapped.  “They tortured those cops
because it was fun.  A+ Teeth behavior, F- being a human, and I think
I’m qualified to make the latter statement.”  A grimace rolled over
their features.  “Lisa is scared shitless that one day you’ll decide
that since she hasn’t killed someone, you’ll force her to do so or
something equally drastic.  Amelia is worse — she doesn’t have any real
friends of her own other than the Teeth.  You and Lisa are the first
people in her life to actually give a shit about her as a person in a
long time.”

/“What the hell does this have to do with us?” / Fester hissed.

I relayed the thought, and Madison pinched their nose.  “It’s…
goddamnit, okay listen.  Taylor, they’re your /friends /.  You should
care about them doing shit like that, and you should absolutely not be
encouraging them!”

“Like Emma encouraged you?” I bit out, and Madison reeled as if slapped.

“Yes, exactly like that,” they said tiredly.  “Emma, Sophia, and I
didn’t start off as shitty people, but we sure as hell got there because
no one was willing to stand up and tell us ‘no.’  It was a game, a
persona that we put on, and look what it took to get us to see just how
fucked up we had become!”

/“Shoulda joined the Teeth,” / Marauder complained.

I opened my mouth to retort that at least I hadn’t killed anyone at
school, only to remember that was only technically true because I had
those neo Nazi would-be murderers hauled to the Arena instead.  I had
done that early, too, before all of the really crazy shit had happened.

Once upon a time, I had sworn I would never use my powers to just sting
people I didn’t like.  I thought myself better than them, so what had
changed?  Certainly my predecessors hadn’t found a bar they wouldn’t try
to tunnel beneath or a line they wouldn’t try to leap across (apart from
sex crimes, thank fuck), but I had tried to avoid sinking to their level.

As though to punctuate that thought, they raged and screeched in my head
at the mere mention that I was trying to keep them contained.  I knew
that there was leakage — hell, I had my hair in a braid right now — but
Madison wasn’t wrong.  I just wish they had picked a better way to say it.

“I’m doing a damn sight better than Quarrel,” I grumbled.

“Yeah, you are,” Madison agreed, stepping around me towards the door. 
“Trust me — everyone prefers Weaver to Butcher XV.  But do /you / prefer
Taylor… or Butcher?”

/“Talk about a mic drop,” / Ironsides muttered as the door shut behind
Madison, but I barely heard him through the haze of complaints from the
others.  I had been focused on the big picture and the Teeth as a whole
since I inherited, trying to do some good with the powers I had been
‘gifted’ (as Quarrel put it).  Anything else had been acceptable
sacrifices or issues I could sort out later, but…

Madison had compared me to Emma, and I wasn’t totally sure they were wrong.

The difference was that when the Protectorate had come to take me away,
I had fought.  I had to fight every single day to keep the Butchers’
influence at bay, making sure that the Teeth weren’t too egregiously
awful… and Legend had still shown up.  I had to fight the Elite, sure,
but also apparently the PRT’s heavy-handed attempts to stop me from
keeping Winslow safe.

I mentally glanced at the clock via bugs sitting on the hands, realizing
that all of these thoughts would have to be addressed later.  I made a
mental note to talk to Lisa, Amelia, and Chrissie about everything and
headed to my first class.

 

------------------------------------------------------------------------

 

“Saved you a doughnut,” Chrissie said as I approached the computer
classroom.  “Even paid for ‘em, which reminds me that you still owe me a
date at Dunkin Do… you alright, Tay?”

I cursed Madison for dredging up one of my eternal fears surrounding my
relationship with Chrissie — did she like me or Butcher?  We had
discussed this, and she was perfectly upfront with her initial
attraction, nevermind the fact that I could hear the honest concern in
her voice.  So, I did my best to plaster on a tired smile and shook my
head.  “Not important right now.  Just… you know.”  I tapped the side of
my head.

/“Sure, blame us for all of your problems,” / Knockout complained.

Chrissie pulled me into a hug at that, murmuring in my ear.  “You’re
amazing Taylor, Butcher or no.  And the way you feed our enemies to your
swarm is kinda hot.”

The Butchers burst into laughter at that, and despite my mood I
chuckled.  “See?” my girlfriend said.  “Don’t believe the haters.”

I opened my mouth to object to that, which led to Chrissie obstructing
my retort with a doughnut.  She then gave me the rest of the bag and
darted off to her first class, leaving me to shuffle alone into Mrs.
Knott’s room.  The only teacher for which I maintained even a modicum of
respect frowned at my arrival, but didn’t say anything as I made my way
to my seat.  At least my hoodie was tied around my waist with the
numerals hidden — I had already disappointed her enough.

In an attempt to claw back a little of her opinion of me, I had started
helping the struggling students in the class.  Somewhat amusingly, in
the past two weeks I had single-handedly turned the class around.  I
hoped that the success was because I was actually helping them learn and
not because they were afraid of pissing off the Butcher by not listening
to her programming advice.  Regardless, I had found that I genuinely
enjoyed teaching them.

If I didn’t have a future as a supervillain I might have tried for a
teaching degree. 

/“You should go for it anyway,” / Reflex said.  /“It would honor your
mother’s legacy.”  /

/“I know Annette’s proud of you,” / Fester added.

Chisel hummed.  /“I can’t say I ever imagined going to college, but now…
it could be pretty damn funny.” /

/“Assuming Taylor’s still in charge,” / Sabertooth growled.  /“With all
of her bitching —” /

Several of the others piled onto that, and I pushed the whole lot of
them back into the recesses of my mind to focus on the person I was
helping; they flinched when I scowled.  “Not you,” I muttered.  “Now
copy this block…”

My pocket buzzed, revealing a text from Chrissie suggesting that we do
something nice tonight ‘to distract u ;)’.  A nuclear blush immediately
rolled up my neck and across my face, only for her to follow up with
‘how about nice dinner with ur dad’.

/“Japanese,” /   Quarrel nearly shouted.  “ /Do it.  You know you want
to.  Embrace the umami.” /

The others stopped their malcontented ramblings to blink at that,
metaphorically.  /“Quarrel… what?” / Knockout spluttered.

/“I put up with all of your shitty comfort food,” / she spat back,
sounding much more like her normal self.  /“If Taylor is going to go
home and mope, might as well do it over something actually good.” /

That sparked an even more heated discussion, which I supposed was an
improvement.  Quarrel pushed a few memories about how to actually cook a
few dishes from her childhood forwards, promising a shopping list; I was
typing away at my phone long enough that Mrs. Knott cleared her throat
quietly.  I pocketed the device and made sure that Jeremy didn’t have
any further questions, then stood up and walked to her desk.

“They’ve improved,” I said simply. 

“You have a gift,” Mrs Knott said softly.  “I thought most of this class
was a lost cause, but you turned them around.” 

I shrugged as we watched the class work.  “I simply motivated them,
nothing more.” 

“You’re too modest,” Mrs Knott said, looking down at the floor with a
sigh.  “I’m sorry that you had to seek solace with the Teeth of all
people to finally find your place.  I just hope you don’t get trapped
with them for life.” 

“Walking away isn’t an option,” I admitted.  “Though probably not for
the reason you may think.  Weaver lets anyone leave if they so choose,
but I don’t have that luxury… not that I would leave.  I turned down the
chance just yesterday.” 

Mrs Knott finally looked at me, a frown of concentration on her face. 
“Why would you do that?  Who would choose to stay with a gang?”

/“Aw hell, break it to her nicely,” / Alkaline muttered. 

I agreed with that sentiment, which meant I couldn’t pull my usual swarm
tricks.  “Think about it — who’s the only individual that /can’t / leave
the Teeth?” 

Mrs Knott’s face scrunched up in thought as she rubbed her chin.  She
didn’t speak for almost five minutes, drawing it out until the bell
rang.  Sighing, I moved to collect my bag when I felt her arm rest on my
shoulder. 

“Why can’t you just tell me?” 

I smiled, though there wasn’t much cheer in it and gave her a firm but
gentle hug.  “Because, when I tell people, they get frightened.  Believe
me when I say that is the last thing I want to do to the one person who
believed in me when no one else did.” 

As I turned back to the door, I heard her breath hitch, my bugs could
see a stray tear run down her face as her lip quivered.  Now that the
truth was known to her, I finally pulled my jacket on in full, the
numerals and my name on full display for her to see. 

“I didn’t lie when I said Weaver looks after her own.”  My voice was
just loud enough for her to hear.  “Thank you for everything, and I hope
you won’t mind me helping with class again tomorrow.” 

Not waiting for a reply, I stepped out and made my way to the next
class.  Today was turning out to be a long day and it only promised to
get longer. 

 

------------------------------------------------------------------------

 

Madison’s complaints continued to echo in my head as I followed Chrissie
into Gladly’s classroom.  The intervening classes had done little to
take my mind off of the problem, and as usual my predecessors had made
everything worse.

/“Untrue — we have, on balance, been more useful to you than not
recently,” / Damascian pointed out.

She wasn’t wrong, but I still had to push away a few of the more
annoying voices when they chipped in with further ideas.  The worst was
Marauder, who once again tried to vouch for going Carrie on the school
so that we never had to go back.  Even as I discarded that idea,
however, the others chipped in with ‘eat all of the wiring in the walls’
and ‘have bugs pull the fire alarms constantly,’ along with other less
destructive but no less chaotic ideas.

I refused to give any of the ideas any serious consideration.

And wasn’t that exactly the issue?  As Madison had so unnecessarily
pointed out, I had gone from ‘be a hero and ignore the Butchers’ to
‘goes to school without murdering everyone, probably.’  It stung what
little remained of my personal pride that I had somehow looped all the
way back around to where I was before going out in costume, except now
the Wards would be pouring containment foam on me instead of juice.

Sure, I could tell myself that the real reason I kept coming to Winslow
was to keep the Teeth safe, or to bolster my not-so-secret identity, or
even to improve the school like I had told Blackwell.  But Madison’s
comments had forced me to confront the real reason — it was the last
part of my personal, pre-Butcher life that I hadn’t sacrificed for the
Teeth.

Yet.

As such, I was going to do my literal damnedest to try to get the
education that my mom would have so badly wanted for me, and I was going
to try to enjoy it.  Thankfully I had Chrissie, who took my brooding
silence in stride and simply held my hand in support of the current
shitshow raging in my head.

/“And we’re not even saying that much,” / Sanguine said with a grin. /“I
mean, not really much to say when you get away with impaling Kaiser and
still get to sell Butcher plushies.” /  The original howled in annoyance
at that, much to Sanguine and the others’ amusement.

“Fuck you,” I muttered under my breath as I eased into my seat.

From next to me, Chrissie snorted.  “Here, in front of everyone, Tay? 
That’s bold, even for you.”

“What’s bold?” Madison asked as they walked past, sitting down behind
me.  They gave Chrissie a passable attempt at a stern glare.  “If she’s
smiling, I’m not sure I like it.”

“Smart move,” I retorted, earning an indignant squawk from my
girlfriend.  Then I grit my teeth and turned to face Madison.  “So, uh
earlier…”  Madison froze, their eyes going wide.  “Thank you.  I, um,
needed to hear that.”

The chorus complained loudly about my admission, of course, but as
unpleasant the morning had been, even I could recognize that I needed
the reality check.  Gladly started the lecture soon after, talking
uselessly for a few minutes before once again attempting to substitute
group work for teaching.

Chrissie leaned in conspiratorially as soon as the class split up.  “So,
what evil plan are you concocting this time, boss?”

“No plan,” I said, grimacing as I pulled out a sheet of paper and
started writing about the economic impact of the Teeth vis-à-vis plushie
sales.  “Maddie here just reminded me that I’ve been doing a shitass job
at /not / being the Butcher.”  A scowl rolled over Chrissie’s face, but
I waved her off with my other hand.  “Don’t give them a hard time.”

“As long as you aren’t planning on going easy on the Elite and whatever
is left of the Empire.”  Chrissie actually pouted at that.

/“Your mother would be so proud,” / Fester said.

I shook my head, keeping my voice down.  “Never.  But… Chrissie, barely
more than a month ago, I would be sitting here while Madison pelted me
with spitballs.  Now I get into drunken brawls with famous heroes and
just… show back up to school the next day.  I had lines I didn’t want to
cross, but they’re way behind me now.”

The other two capes stared at me.  “Tay, can we save the heavy shit for
after school?” Chrissie eventually murmured.  “Because that’s a hell of
a lot to unpack.”

“Sorry for bringing it up,” Madison added.

/“Even the Ward fuckin’ knows —” /  I cut off Ironsides before he could
complain further.

An awkward silence settled over the group for a moment, broken by
Madison reaching into their pocket and pulling out a cell phone.  “Um,
how about we look at cute puppy photos?”

I made a few additions to our nominal ‘group work’ while Madison and
Chrissie flicked through a few of the pictures, which turned out to be
Carly and her new puppy playing with teenagers who were almost certainly
Wards.  Madison’s brazenness of showing pictures of unmasked Wards to
the Butcher was completely offset by the fact that it was the Butcher
who enforced those Rules to begin with.

/“Cute dog,” / Sabertooth growled.  /“Can’t believe Rachel parted with a
puppy.” /

/“I am far more interested in Madison’s willingness to show us
incriminating photos of her colleagues,” / Damascian said. /  “Surely we
haven’t generated that much goodwill?” /

/“Hey, the whole paranoia about identities was one of the reasons I
joined the Teeth!” / Alkaline pointed out.

/“That and joining the Wards meant you couldn’t do mushrooms whenever
you wanted,” / Knockout retorted.

I pushed the banter to the back of my mind, along with the indignation
that Gladly was perfectly happy to let Madison goof off in class as long
as they could turn in my work once again.  It seemed that Ethan and
Carly had taken a few of the Wards to play with the puppy at a park near
the PRT headquarters downtown, and it made me feel ever so slightly
better that at least /something / I did recently was so wholesome.

My thoughts must have shown on my face.  “Legend and Chevalier were not
happy with me,” Madison murmured as they put the phone away despite
Chrissie’s protests.  “I had to sit through a talk about you being a bad
influence and wanting me to convince you to be a hero again.  They
didn’t like my answer.”

Chrissie actually laughed at that, which annoyed Madison but let me
finish the assignment in peace while they bickered about why there
weren’t more pictures of puppies.  The bell for lunch interrupted Gladly
from talking to one of the other ‘popular’ groups about their
assignment, which I took to mean that he forgot to call us up to present
our findings.

/“Is he really paying so little attention?” / Chisel mused.

Marauder grunted, eyeing one of my classmates.  /“Maybe he was was too
busy paying attention to her —” /

I slammed him down into the dark, but I had to bite my tongue on my
verbal retort when my bugs revealed a different annoyance approaching
me.  I fought down the urge to kick his ass, instead putting up a
suitably irritated façade before turning to him.  “Can I help you, Greg?”

Most of the class, including the so-called teacher, had left the room at
that point, leaving Greg alone with a handful of stragglers and three
Teeth capes who didn’t much like him.  “So, now you’re friends with her
but not me?” he blurted, gesturing at Madison.

I turned a flat glare upon the boy who thought that merely not
tormenting me meant that we were friends.  When he started squirming
under my gaze, I finally said, “Greg, Madison has apologized and taken
steps to make up for what they did to myself and others.  While they’re
not forgiven, I am doing my best to move beyond the past.  Maybe you
should do the same.”

Chrissie didn’t bother to hide her laugh at that, and Greg glared at
her.  “You’re just trying to get her entangled with the Teeth, just like
you were.”  I raised a single eyebrow and he stuttered.  “B-but you
don’t have to hang out with criminals, Taylor!”

/“Bit late for that!”  “Trying!?”  “Ooh, nice word.”  “What, is he
jealous?” /

“I happen to enjoy the company of the Teeth, thank you very much,” I
said, noting that a few of our classmates, having been somehow alerted
that Greg was about to do something extremely stupid, were shuffling
back into the classroom.  “But I don’t see how that is any of your
business.  They protect me, unlike anyone /else / here at Winslow.”

That last bit was partially aimed at the spectators, sending a few of
the more observant teens skittering back out the door.  I could never be
sure which of my classmates had actually put the clues together and
realized who I was, at least with the exception of Greg.  It boggled my
mind that he hadn’t figured it out.

/“Oh no, Taylor’s such a nice, sweet girl,” / Marauder said in a high-
pitched, mocking voice.  /“Surely she doesn’t chop Nazis into pieces
like sausage!” /

The other Butchers laughed at that, and Greg was mildly put off by my
own snickering.  “But, uh, Taylor… the Teeth capes.  Well, heroes can
protect you too, it’s, uh, in the name —”

“Who said anything about capes?” Madison snapped.  “Are you high, Greg? 
Sparky let you dip into his supply?”

“What?  No!” he retorted.  “I mean, it’s just, um…”  He visibly tried to
steady himself.  “You deserve better than villains, Taylor.  Trust me, I
know that capes are cool and all, I spend a lot of time reading about
capes and yeah, they’re really cool so I get that.  And sure, there’s a
bunch of powerful and interesting villains that people write, er, fun
stories about like that one Specific_Protagonist fic about Nilbog but
there’s so many more better heroes and I’m sure we can find you some —”

I tuned out Greg’s heartfelt but poorly planned rant to watch Madison
flinch at the reference.  They even blushed for a moment before
(presumably) getting themselves under control with their power.

“— and so I can really help you, just trust me here I can —”

“Greg, shut up for a second.”  I put every ounce of ‘done dealing with
Spree’s bullshit’ that I could cram into my voice.  “I am perfectly
happy where I am.  Who I am friends with is not subject to your approval.”

To the general astonishment of everyone, Greg didn’t back down. 
“Friends?” he asked darkly, taking a moment to psych himself up. 
“They’re not your friends.  You are only dating Chrissie because she’s V—”

Just as several voices roared for Greg’s head on a spike, I was
surprised by Madison of all people leaping up and clamping their hand
over Greg’s mouth.  Given how swift the motion had been, most would have
missed how their arm stretched to close the distance.  

“You really must be on drugs if you think that’s a good idea,” they hissed.

I ignored the faint, momentary shimmer near Greg’s neck.

“But —”

I cut in, holding up a paper cube.  “Choose your next words carefully,
Greg,” I said with deadly quiet.  “The Teeth have killed for less, and
their boss is always watching.”

“That’s a bluff and you know it,” he retorted, but his conviction was gone.

I shrugged, then crushed the cube dramatically.  Greg was likely one of
the few people in the school that hadn’t done the basic arithmetic to
figure out that Taylor plus XV hoodie equals Weaver.

Maybe it was time to correct his ignorance.

Bugs flowed from the ceiling tiles, from the cracks in the walls and a
hundred other dark recesses.  Greg screamed and several of the other
students bolted to the exit, but it spoke to my reputation that just as
many remained to watch the show.  Madison just pinched their nose and
furiously texted with their other hand, likely telling their own bosses
that everything was fine.

Chrissie had pulled out a snack. 

/“Girl has her priorities,” / Alkaline said with a nod. 

The bugs formed up into a vague humanoid shape, then I went a bit
extra.  Spiders formed into a braid-like pattern, mirroring my own. 
Fireflies settled into the eyes and cycled their lights so they were
always glowing.  I even replicated my hoodie to a degree and put the XV
onto the back of it, even if one had to squint to see it. 

/“Excellent detail work,” / Damascian noted.  /“Your skills are growing.” / 

/“Don’t be afraid to add some shaped stuff,” / Chisel said as she sent a
few ideas.  /“Could make the clones all the more convincing.”  /

I set their suggestions aside for later, focusing on the terrified boy
in front of me.  “Someone has quite the mouth on them,” my swarm spoke. 
Greg’s heart was racing through bloodsight; the clone chittered in
satisfaction.  “Tell me, Greg Veder, why do you antagonize my Teeth?  I
don’t take kindly to those looking to commit suicide by cape, but I have
been known to oblige them.” 

“You’re not real,” Greg said as he backed against the wall.  “I must
have hit my head or something.  There’s no way the Butcher is at
Winslow, there’s no way that monster would care about this school.  I’m
dreaming, or hallucinating, or… something.” 

/“Aww, the wittle baby is scared,” /Butcher sneered. 

“Dude, you’re embarrassing yourself,” another student, oh, Sparky
actually came to school today!  Shit, if he was high, well, higher than
usual, he might just ruin the surprise.  “Weaver’s pretty chill.  I
actually met her once, we got ramen.” 

/“Never thought Sparky of all people would speak up for us,” / Ironsides
said.

“That little stall does have damn good noodles,” my swarm said, then it
stepped forward and placed an arm on the wall beside Greg’s head.  “But
let’s not get distracted.  Greg, if I catch you speculating on things
that should best stay hidden ever again, you will meet the same fate as
Kaiser.  /Do you understand? /” 

/“Kaiser learned what happens when Mario misses the flagpole,” /
Alkaline snickered. 

Greg slid to the floor as a warm puddle began to form on the ground at
his feet.  I had to fight down a grimace of my own, given my own
heightened senses.  “Yes ma’am!” he squeaked out.

/“Quick, bets on if he notices this next one!” / Marauder said as a
flurry of activity followed in my head.

My swarm dispersed, collapsing into a mass of insects that vanished
almost into thin air.  Greg stared for a long moment at where the swarm
clone had been standing, only for his eyes to dart over and fix on the
hoodie hanging off the back of my chair.  It was angled just right to
put my name on full display.

That /finally / seemed to scare him out of the room, the overpowering
scent of urine following him as he beat a hasty retreat.  /“Exit left,
chased by swarm,” / Fester said in a terrible English accent.

/Huh? /

/“Did your mother never… Shakespeare, Taylor.  She loved the Bard,
enough to go on a date to see A Midsummer Night’s Dream.” /

Of course, Fester had to ruin it by sending a few memories of their
revelry /afterward / — how many people were… no, not thinking about that
— but I still laughed out loud at the mention of Mom.

I pushed away the chorus’s wolf-whistles and cheers too, pulling on my
jacket and nodding to Chrissie and Madison.  “Shall we?  It’s not like
we don’t get enough time for lunch as it is.”

/“What the hell is / she /doing here?” /

I had to agree with Sabertooth — I was not expecting my bugs to pick up
the rapid arrival of one of my least favorite people, phasing in and out
at impressive speed over the rooftops on a beeline for Winslow.  The
timing might have been suspicious if not for the fact that Sophia had
been a student here; I had been looking forward to a mostly peaceful lunch.

“Hey Mads, any reason Sophia might want to drop by for lunch?” I
murmured quietly enough that the Teeth following us to the lunch room
wouldn’t hear.

Madison stopped dead in the hallway, eliciting an oof of surprise from
Britney when the latter ran into them.  “No, definitely not,” they said,
rapidly shaking their head.

/“Wasn’t Stalker supposed to be transferred to Boston?” / Chisel asked. 

/“New York,” /Damascian corrected.

That lined up with the last I had heard.  Her unwilling relocation was
part of the reason why Sophia had been willing to hit that Elite base
with Madison, as further punishment really didn’t matter to her.  Even
still, I wondered what she was risking by coming here, to do… what?

/“The real punishment would be leaving her here,” / Sanguine pointed out.

/“Taylor, we need to go to New York,” / Knockout said suddenly,
enthusiasm outstripping his usual displeasure.  /“Good bars, great
girls, better fights… come on!” /  He remembered a number of those in my

/“Sophia is obviously here for you,” / Ironsides grumbled, pulling me
back to the issue at hand.  I nodded in annoyance as we walked into the
lunch room, picking a table near the door and waiving the rest of my

that door, but to my surprise she hesitated before barging in. 
Bloodsight revealed her racing heart, and I was solely tempted to pain
blast her for the hell of it.

A little bit.

Just like the secretary.

The Butchers, naturally, leapt onto the cruelty train and started
offering all of their own horrible suggestions, gleefully ignoring the
fact that Sophia was out of costume and still a Ward to boot.  They
continued even as I forced all of them into the dark, which gave Sophia

She encountered the table where I sat with Chrissie and Madison

“You seem to be doing so,” I retorted, drawing a snort of amusement from

/“You haven’t killed her yet, so I don’t know why they’re bothering,” /

Alkaline scoffed.  /“Madison is practically a member, so they’re

Something like fear flickered over Sophia’s face for a second before she

I was too busy boggling over the idea that Sophia was apologizing for /

Sophia flipped her off, much to Chrissie’s amusement.  “They realized

“I’m more surprised by how pissed they were about Vista,” I said,

“They tried to take her taser,” Madison said with a smirk.  “She ran the
battery out before throwing it at some poor schmuck’s head, yelling the

I couldn’t help but laugh at the mental images that inspired.  “Tell

/“Do that anyway,” /Knockout said with a snicker.

The conversation stuttered to a halt after that, but we were all saved

Turns out, eradicating the assholes meant that people were willing to be
themselves.  What an idea.

We wanted to eventually retrofit Winslow’s sad excuse for a cafeteria,

There were plenty of kids who wanted nothing to do with us, but a fair

/“Amusing that you pay someone just to bring food every day,” / Marauder

Sanguine huffed.  /“Would you eat the garbage they serve?”  /

/“I’d rather eat from a dumpster,” / Chisel said. 

The trio of junior Teeth immediately set about distributing the meals

/“Nerd.” / Pyro teased.

/“That is so fucking cool!” / Sabertooth exclaimed, followed by chants

“If anything, they’d get rid of them for being /too / effective,” Sophia

/“Well, no one said Stalker was stupid,” / Knockout said.  /“Can’t be,

/“Did none of the other Wards connect the monster to the self-

/“Of fucking course she does,” / Marauder snapped.  /“Cape like her?

/“I’m pretty sure Amelia will put us all to shame when she snaps,” /

“Taylor?”

Chrissie’s voice snapped me back to reality, and I found all three girls

The Ward in question didn’t bother to hide shock.  “What —”

I tapped my head.  “Several decades of cape experience.  The PRT is

Finally, Sophia fell back into more recognizable patterns — defiance

“They apologized.”

“I’m s—”

My hand slammed down on the table.  “No you’re not,” I hissed.  “And if

/“Oh come on!” / Marauder whined, and I punted him into the dark.

Chrissie rolled her eyes.  “At school, yeah.  You kinda set some of our

Sophia’s face went stony.  “That was her trigger.”

I pushed down the revulsion and pity I felt for Emma at that moment to

Sophia froze, and I took great satisfaction at how her heart rate

“Sophia, if Taylor was going to kill you, she would have done it

“Assholes,” Sophia grumbled, stabbing at the remains of her food.

The entire table chuckled at her misfortune, but I could see the gears

“What are you talking about Madison?” Sophia asked.  “I wouldn’t be

They wouldn’t dare touch me.”

/“This is,” / Reflex said, clearly conflicted. 

My temper flared at the obvious manipulation, and the slightest zap of

“Taylor…” Madison warned, ignoring Chrissie’s outright laughter. 

 I stalked around the table and hoisted Sophia under the shoulder.  “You

“Truth be told, I want nothing more than to strip the flesh from your
bones,” I growled as I stared her in the eyes.  Several bugs began to
crawl along the walls, chittering in time with my words.  She looked
away — the fear quite real, but so was the longing.  “Still, that’s
better than I view Animos and Spree.  I have three rules.  Rule one, if
you want my job, issue a formal challenge in the arena.  Rule two,
bodily autonomy is sacred, no rape, no prejudice against how someone is
born.  Rule three, the Teeth do what they want /unless I say
otherwise /.  Don’t like it, refer to rule one.  Fuck any of that up and
I kill you myself.  Understand?”

Sophia nodded once.  “Still better than being sent to New York,” she
grumbled. 

“Good.” I said, letting the bugs scatter as I relaxed, pinching the
bridge of my nose.  “Now I get to deal with the headache of you joining
us while not fucking over your civilian life.  You can fuck off now, or
go to classes like normal, I don’t really care which.  If you stay, I
think Charlotte keeps extra hoodies in our colors somewhere.  Talk to
Lisa whenever you decide to get to the arena, and tell her to call me /
when / she has questions.”

“Who?” she asked. 

“You’ll figure it out,” I said, leaving her where she stood.  I wasn’t a
fool though and tagged her with my bugs as I made my way back inside. 
The Butchers made various appreciative noises, but I didn’t share in
their enthusiasm.  “This is a mistake,” I murmured to myself.

/“She’ll fit right in!” / Knockout said enthusiastically.

/“She’s useful?” / Fester tried.  /“Saber?  You’ve been quiet.” /   He
just growl-snorted and ignored her.  /“Huh.” /

Back at the table, Madison and Chrissie wore conflicting expressions.  I
gave Madison a long-suffering look before going back to my own food. 
“Tell the PRT that if she causes too much trouble, I’ll just bundle her
back up for them.  But it’s this or letting her run around completely
unsupervised, so…”

“Yeah, alright,” Madison agreed.  “I’m not sure how Sophia slipped away,
but I guess we know where she is now.  Chrissie?”

My girlfriend shrugged.  “Dunno, it’s hella funny to convert heroes and
she’s right up our alley, but I think you might need to zap her a few
more times.”

The Butchers agreed loudly with that, and without a retort of my own, I
decided to focus back on my lunch.  Sophia’s confrontation had eaten up
most of the hour, so I had to finish my takeout without taking the time
to enjoy it.

I was scraping sauce onto the last bit of rice when my personal phone
buzzed.  I wasn’t expecting a call, but that didn’t mean the Elite might
not have pulled something, or the Protectorate for that matter.  Lisa
was one of the few not present that had my number the other was… 

I swiped to answer faster than I ever had before.  “Dad?  Everything
alright?”

“Hey little owl…” His voice was hesitant and nervous, immediately
setting me on edge; I began to shift my relay bugs to take me straight
to the docks. 

“Dad, if you need me, just stay casual, otherwise tell me exactly why
you sound like someone has a gun to your head.” 

“Nobody has a gun to my head,” he said quickly.  “I did have to call the
PRT however.” 

“Call the—” I paused and took a breath, waving at Chrissie to let her
know things were under control.  “Tell me everything.” 

“A cape from the Elite came by the union office, wanted to make a deal. 
I turned them down,” he explained.  “They didn’t like that, got
belligerent and began to make threats.  I asked them if they knew the
Rules, he started to say ‘screw the rules’ and I put double aught
buckshot center of mass.  Now I have a dead Elite spokesman and a major
headache.” 

/“Damn, go Danny,” /Fester said appreciatively. 

Dad heaved out a long sigh.  “I called the PRT, and when they heard my
name they transferred me to Armsmaster directly.” 

Which meant that Hebert was flagged in their database in some way. 
“Madison, when you get back to work, run a console request on mine and
Dad’s name, see what it tells you about us.” 

Madison perked up, their face darkening.  “What happened?” 

“Dad put down a cape, his name got the incident kicked up to Armsmaster
immediately.” 

“Consider it done,” Madison said.  “Is he alright?” 

“Yeah, and the Elite are down another cape,” I said, which prompted a
whooping cheer from Chrissie and half our boys in earshot, before
returning to the call.  “Dad, I have a direct line to the Union if you
need me, just message me if that is necessary.” 

“In or out of costume?” he asked hesitantly. 

“Either/or, you tell me,” I said.  “I’ll put the Teeth on alert and make
sure Lisa knows to watch out for other violations of the Rules they may
try to pull.  I doubt they expected a shotgun, but I also doubt they’ll
send someone squishy after, say,  Amelia.” 

“Alright Taylor, just don’t do anything too drastic,” he said. 

“Hey, none of that,” I said firmly.  “You defended yourself from someone
trying to use you to get to me.  I would have killed them myself if you
hadn’t.  Hell, take a trophy and show it off the next time you’re at the
arena.  If the Protectorate try anything, I’ll remind them why they
don’t fuck with a cape’s family.” 

“Alright kiddo,” he said softly.  “I just worry.” 

“I know you do, which is why we’re going to have a nice dinner at home
tonight and talk over a few things.  I expect you to be blunt, and I
will do my best to listen.  I just ask you to give me the same courtesy.” 

I could almost hear the smile in his reply.  “I think I can do that, do
you need me to pick anything up?” 

“Quarrel gave me the recipes, I’ll grab everything after school,” I
said.  “See you tonight.” 

Dad sighed.  “Stay safe, Taylor.” 

As soon as I hung up, my fingers were flying across the screen as I sent
Lisa a synopsis and request to look into things.  She immediately
replied that she was sending someone to keep an eye on Amelia in the
event the Elite tried something equally stupid. Satisfied that I had
done what I could, I set my phone aside and leaned against Chrissie. 

“I hate people sometimes,” I grumbled as I popped a dumpling into my
mouth.  “Lisa’s on things now, so hopefully we don’t have any further
idiots.”  

“You know we will,” Chrissie said as she hugged me.  “Let me know if
Danny needs help preparing his trophy.” 

I shrugged.  “Eh, I figure that would be more of a father daughter
bonding moment, but thanks for the offer.” 

 

------------------------------------------------------------------------

 

Sophia reappeared for afternoon classes, but apart from the widespread
shock and amusement of seeing her with a crimson hoodie tied around her
waist, nothing really came of the rest of the day.  Teachers watched me
with a wary eye and I helped those I could with any problems they might
have run into.  Chemistry especially allowed me to show off Alkaline’s
knowledge, and she knew ways to explain things in a way that even an
idiot that thought the class would teach them to cook their own meth
would figure out. 

As we worked, the collective had found a new way to torment me, and I
could do nothing but grit my teeth and resist the urge to join in. 
Worse, the bastards in my head actually sounded halfway decent and it
was a crime to mute Bohemian Rhapsody in any form. 

/I see a little silhouetto of a man, /

/Scaramouch, Scaramouch, will you do the Fandango! /

/Thunderbolts and lightning, very, very frightening me /

/Galileo, Galileo /

/Galileo, Galileo /

/Galileo, Figaro  /

/Magnificoo /

It was incredibly frustrating, and made worse because Sabertooth was
actually damn good at acapela instruments.  I worked in frustrated
silence, showing one of my Teeth why you don’t want to mix certain
chemicals unless you have a death wish, then subtly explained how to
delay the reaction until you could get clear. 

All of that was just a distraction, and looking at the clock, I knew I
would lose the race for the buzzer.  Maybe I would get lucky and
everyone would think I was plotting murder or something…

/Oh mama mia, mama mia, mama mia, let me go /

/Beelzebub has a devil put aside for me, for me, /

/For meee /

Then, in unison, all fourteen of my headmates began to headbang, and
damn them all, I had to join in.  Those with the Teeth likely understood
exactly what I was enduring, at least I hoped they did.  No doubt that
it would become a running joke back at the arena, at least when they
didn’t think I was listening. 

Unfortunately, I shared this class with Chrissie and Sophia, which
dashed all my hopes of it not getting around.  At least I could use the
excuse to sting Sophia if she tried to spread it.  I had enough of that
over the last two years, I didn’t need her falling back into old habits. 

When the final bell rang, I said my goodbyes to Chrissie for the moment
and began my cross town teleportation and shopping trip, grabbing
ingredients from half a dozen shops located within the former ABB
territory.  Once that was finished, I made my way home, thankful that my
backpack held everything and that I had invested in one that was flame
proof. 

/“Nearly a grand, just so it didn’t burn up when you teleport,” /Pyro said. 

/“You just wish you could have afforded one,” /Knockout said. 

Pyro didn’t deny that as I chuckled, appearing in my backyard with a
thunderous crack.  It was a common enough occurrence that the neighbors
had to know, as evidenced by the handful of nearby homes that had
suddenly gone on sale.  Lisa bought up each one just to ensure someone
didn’t move in just to spy on me or mine, not that I wouldn’t have
noticed with my swarm. 

Chrissie was already inside, lounging on the couch and watching
something on TV; the backdoor was unlocked.  I let myself in while a
small swarm announced my presence. 

“Holding down the fort?” I asked as I set my backpack on the kitchen
table and began to pull out all the ingredients and tools needed for the
meal. 

“You know it!” she called back.  “Watching America’s Funniest Cape
Bloopers, this one had Chevalier trip during a diplomatic meeting or
something.” 

/“Damn, we should watch that show more often,” /Fester said. 

/“Pity they avoid showing villains,” /Ironsides grumbled. 

Marauder laughed.  /“Would you want to risk the Slaughterhouse or heaven
forbid, us, showing up?”  /

/I don’t think we’re quite as feared as the Slaughterhouse.  /

/“You underestimate how much capes fear the Butcher’s inheritance,” /
the man himself said.  /“Remember how scared everyone was when you first
inherited?  And even later, Battery was seconds from pissing herself in
fear of you.”  /

/  / Had she been?  It didn’t feel like it at the time, but looking back
with the experience I had now, I could see the fear.  The heroes (and
villains) had been jumpy, just waiting for me to snap.  Of course, they
had been right to be cautious, but I hadn’t even noticed because I was
still adjusting to the /everything / that had been dumped on me.  I sure
as hell wasn’t the girl from that first night, not anymore.  I was
someone new — Butcher XV, different from all of my predecessors but
still so much the same.

That was the truth and I refused to hide from it.  Instead, I would rise
to meet it, and this dinner was a step towards that goal. 

Donning my apron, I set myself to the task at hand. 

The recipe was something Quarrel had made with her own family as a kid
before they’d been killed in a car accident.  That tragedy was one of
the few things she and I didn’t give each other grief over, and this
recipe had been one of her favorites.  It helped that the memories she
had of the meal were enticing as hell. 

/“Dice those a bit finer, it helps the flavor seep into the rest of the
mixture,” / Quarrel said, watching through my eyes. / “Lower the heat on
the rice a bit, you want to steam it, not boil it.”  /

I rolled my eyes, but did as instructed.  I worked methodically,
prepping everything through the help of memories not my own and
Quarrel’s guidance.  I doubt we would ever be on friendly terms given I
did kill her, but I didn’t want to be completely antagonistic with the
people that I would spend the rest of my life, and apparent afterlife with. 

Most of the others in my head were keeping to themselves, though I could
feel a few were watching intently, anticipating the meal to come.  This
was a bit of an experiment, letting each of my predecessors pick a meal
from their childhood they wouldn’t mind me learning to cook.  So far, it
was proving to be a hit. 

It was also extremely relaxing to do something as mundane as cooking for
a change.  It helped remind me that there was more to life than being
the larger than life figure that I had to present myself as all the time
in public.  Even in my civilian life I had to keep the persona up since
I liked to broadcast my identity.  It helped keep my dad safe, it kept
Winslow in order, it protected my friends. 

It left me tired more often than not. 

I had to wonder how much of the Butcher persona was just me now and what
remained an act.  The line was beyond blurred now, and I didn’t feel a
hint of remorse about killing anymore.  It was terrifying to feel myself
sliding further and further away from the girl I used to be, yet…  

Looking at Chrissie, at Lisa and Amelia…  Dinah, Rachel, Alice, Michael,
Damien…  Alec, Aisha, Charlotte and Todd, hell, even Elliot and
Madison…  I’d made differences for so many people, helped improve their
lives in a myriad of ways.  I’d helped Reflex reconnect with his niece,
I’d gotten letters back from several other Butcher’s families as well. 

I was changing things around me even as I changed.  Hopefully I would be
able to live with what I became and could be proud of the legacy I would
eventually leave in my wake.  Warm arms wrapped around my waist and I
found myself wrapped tight in an embrace by my girlfriend.  I leaned
into her warmth, savoring the moment. 

She pulled away after a disappointingly short time, but moved to help
get the table set while I put the finishing touches on the meal.  She
was just finishing up setting the table when Dad walked in, breathing
deeply. 

“Wow.  That smells amazing!” he called out. 

“Then get in here and help us eat it!” Chrissie yelled back as I pulled
a chair out for her.  

“Hurry up before it gets cold.” I added.

He chuckled and the bug I had tracking him moved towards the stairs. 
“Alright, just let me get out of this damn suit and I’ll be right down.” 

Sitting down, I felt my heart flutter at Chrissie’s smile.  It was easy
to forget in moments like these that I was sharing a bed with a hardened
killer.  That I was one myself, but moments like this?  Even as Dad
finally joined us, I smiled genuinely. 

“Dig in!” I called, savoring the flavor of the curry and rice.  /
Quarrel, this is fucking delicious. /

She practically preened under the praise as the rest of the collective
joined in, voicing their own enjoyment for the meal.  Chrissie and Dad
talked about simple topics but things I knew were important to both of
them.  Stories behind her tattoos, how she got a particular scar, that
time Dad clubbed a Nazi over the head and Mom got him away before the
cops arrived.

By unspoken agreement, we avoided any discussion of Dad’s earlier
aggressive self-defense.

It was casual and free, even if the talks to come were going to be
heavy.  I might not be a good person anymore, but I would do what I
could to protect those I loved.  I had a family again and I wasn’t going
to let anyone get in the way of that. 

Not even myself.
