Chapter Notes

    We're back, for real this time! (See post chapter notes for more)

See the end of the chapter for more notes <#endnotes42>

/Monday May 9th, 2011 /

Aisha tapped her foot impatiently, she was in civvies and standing out
front of the PRT HQ waiting for Missy to get off shift.  They were
supposed to have a study session back at Brian’s place, but something
came up that required her to stop by the base beforehand.  Dinah
couldn’t hide away from the crowds like she could, so she had elected to
wait in the cars.

Plural.

Because she refused to tell Aisha why they needed a second car.  Damn
Precogs and Thinkers playing their games, not like she wanted to be in
on the joke anyway.  It didn’t take Missy long to come out of the
building, but she hadn’t expected her to be following someone while
yelling. 

The domino mask each was wearing did next to nothing to hide either’s
identity if someone went poking, but all that would do is earn them the
Weaver special.  Nobody left in Brockton Bay would be that stupid. 
Well, the Elite seemed to lack common sense, but that was just a
temporary thing.  Either they got some and ran, or it wouldn’t matter. 

“I thought I told you to fuck off,” tall, dark and athletic snarled. 
“I’m done, I’m leaving, stop bothering me.” 

“Sophia, you can’t just quit!” Missy hissed, completely unaware that
Aisha was right next to them.  

“Just did, and I’ve already got a new job to roll right into,” Sophia
said as the two SUVs pulled up.  Aisha’s eyes narrowed as Dinah stepped
out of the back vehicle.  “See, my ride’s even here.” 

“Your ride?” Missy asked, her eyes narrowing.  “The Teeth. You’re
leaving the Wards for the Teeth.” 

“I guess she is,” Aisha said, gripping her power tight.  “Wish someone
had given me the heads up.  Nice to meet you Stalker, you can call me Imp.” 

Dinah grinned and shrugged before walking over.  “Stalker, you get the
front car, it will take you back to base.  Aisha, Missy, ready to study?” 

“Study?” Sophia asked, then glared at Missy.  “Oh this is rich, you’re
giving me shit for joining the Teeth, but you’re hanging out with them
too?” 

“It’s not the same!” Missy protested.  “I knew them before they joined
and it’s not like I’m going out on raids with them like you will be!” 

Sophia just scoffed.  “Still sounds a bit pottish to me there, kettle. 
Whatever, goodbye little hypocrite, see you around.” 

Aisha of course had let her power relax while Dinah talked to Missy in
hushed whispers.  She needed to have a moment with Stalker before they
officially became teammates.  Just as the girl reached the car, Aisha
grabbed her by the wrist and made herself known. 

“So, I hear you shot my brother,” she said cheerfully to the surprised
ex-Ward. 

“Gonna have to be a lot more specific than that,” Sophia said. 

Aisha just grinned wider.  “Really now?  Make a habit of shooting non-
Nazis and slavers too?  For shame.  I’ll make it easy, while you’re just
getting out of the hero game, he just got into it and is set to return
from Boston tonight.” 

Sophia stared for a moment, proving she wasn’t the quickest of wits, but
Aisha was used to people not measuring up to her own brilliance. 

“Your brother is Grue,” Sophia said. 

“Blackout now,” Aisha said.  “Such a downgrade too, Grue was cool and
mysterious, Blackout is just bland.  Anyway, I just wanted to let you
know that as a courtesy.” 

“What’s that supposed to mean?” Sophia said, reaching for something at
her hip. 

“It’s quite simple really.  Go after my brother again, and I’ll consider
that going after my family.  You know how Weaver handles that, and I
would be all too happy to drag you into the pit for an honor duel if you
forget the rules about family.” 

Before Sophia could respond, Aisha relaxed again, checking Sophia for
weapons, finding a single knife near where she had been reaching.  Aisha
relieved her of it and pressed it to her throat, drawing a thin line of
blood before she clamped back down on her power.  Sophia reeled back
immediately, dragging the knife just a bit deeper as she did. 

“Let that be a lesson to you,” Aisha said with none of her usual cheer. 
“Come after my brother again, and you won’t even know why you’re
bleeding out on the ground.” 

This time Aisha remained visible as she walked away, the knife she kept
as a souvenir.  Obviously Sophia didn’t need it, and if she wanted it
back, she could find the nerve to ask.  Aisha had made her point, and
she still had one more to make tonight, which was why they would be
studying at Brian’s tonight. 

Aisha threw her arms around her two friends, a grin on her face.  “Come
on, those essays won’t write themselves!” 

 

------------------------------------------------------------------------

 

Aisha glared down at her half written essay.  It wasn’t due until next
Monday but Missy and Dinah had insisted they meet up and work on it
together.  She wasn’t just some teen girl anymore, she was Imp!  A cape
that ran with the Teeth.  If anything, homework should have been beneath
her.  

For the most part, Taylor was a cool as shit boss.  She could smoke and
drink whatever the hell she wanted, when she wanted to, so long as it
didn’t interfere with her school work.  She’d heard that the Teeth at
Winslow would hang out up front and have a morning toke before classes. 
It made her excited to start high school, assuming she could talk Missy
into picking Winslow over Arcadia.  Sure, Arcadia had the better
teachers and shit, but it didn’t have Weaver.  It also didn’t have
nearly the same level of Teeth membership in attendance, and it let you
wear the colors completely in the open.  

Her school didn’t like people wearing Teeth colors, not that it stopped
Dinah most days.  She even took to wearing her Omen hoodie openly. 
Aisha’s own hoodie didn’t have a name on it, just a silhouette of a
horned head that had become her own symbol.  It didn’t feel right to put
her name on it, given her powers. 

It was a bit of a cosmic joke that a villain team would have the same
educational expectations as the white hats, but that was what set Weaver
apart.  She actually cared about her people, even if she did clearly
favor some over others.  Not that she could blame her badass boss.  She
was pretty sure that Chrissie and Taylor were scoping out Amelia and
Lisa to add them to more than just their frequent cuddle piles. 

Not that it was her business, but she was nosy and Weaver’s ability to
track her was complete bullshit so she couldn’t get the best dirt. 
Dinah wasn’t any help either, not wanting to discuss relationships due
to how her powers took the mystery out of things. 

“Missy, I’m telling you, that isn’t something you want to know,” Dinah
said with no small amount of exasperation.  “The future is ever
shifting.  Even my telling you about the future could shift it, I could
go as far as to manipulate you into dating myself, Aisha or both if I
wanted to and you would never know it.” 

“But I don’t even like girls,” Missy said with some confusion. 

Dinah just rolled her eyes.  “Sixty four point two seven three five
percent chance you date a girl before you turn eighteen.” 

“Oh really now,” Aisha said with a predatory grin.  “I think this
deserves our full attention, and some booze.” 

Missy looked downright scandalized, which just amused her further. 
“Aisha!  We’re too young to drink.”

“Villains, remember?” Aisha said with a shrug.  “Plus, I know where
Brian keeps his stash from when he was still Grue.” 

“Jack and coke for me,” Dinah said.  “Whatever you do, don’t get into
the vodka.  It doesn’t end well.” 

“Noted,” Aisha said and hurried off to the living room and the hutch
that held the liquor.  It was locked, but that never stopped her,
especially when Brian sucked at hiding the key.  Thirty seconds later
she had half a bottle of Jack, three cans of coke and the cups to go
with.  “Ask and ye shall receive!” 

Missy continued to glare as Aisha mixed the drinks up just like the guy
at the Teeth’s bar had shown her.  The capes had their own bar up in the
loft, but it was self-serve, which was why she hung out down in the
Alley.  Between the food stalls and how she got whatever she wanted on
her tab, it was like paradise. 

Sure, she had to put up with the fact that the Teeth dealt drugs, but
they weren’t anything like the Merchants about it.  She had singled out
Todd and had a long talk with their chief dealer, and while she didn’t
leave happy, she at least understood.  Weaver knew they couldn’t
eliminate the distribution of hard drugs, all that would do is invite
competition.  So, she did the next best thing and controlled it, made
sure that those taking it had access to rehab if they needed it, and
made sure it was done as safely as possible. 

Even her mom had shown improvement, not having to suck up to some scummy
dealer for her next hit, or worrying that she would get a bad batch from
an Empire dealer trying to kill off those they saw as sub-human.  It was
too bad that the Teeth had tracked them down before she joined, because
that kind of work was exactly what she wanted to do with the Teeth. 

Missy was handed a glass and she stared at the liquid like it would burn
her, which given how much Jack was in it, wasn’t far from the truth. 
Once she asked for a refill however, well, let it not be said that mix
master Aisha couldn’t be generous. 

Time passed as they drank and bounced ideas around for their essays, the
subject as dry as Missy’s apparent love life.  Of course, when Missy
tried to shift the focus to her, she faded into the background.  It
wasn’t like she didn’t have anything to say, she just didn’t kiss and
tell, no matter how good Alec was at it. 

“You have no idea how stressful this weekend was,” Missy grumbled, her
words ever so slightly slurred.  “Everyone panicked when the Teeth
showed up like that on Sunday.” 

“Couldn’t have been worse than the civvies meet and greet Lisa put
together on Saturday,” Aisha said.  “Alec and I had a lot of fun
pranking people all weekend, but I would have killed to be there for
Taylor’s little bug show.” 

“I wasn’t there either, but Jouster lost his shit,” Missy said.  “He’s
already back in New York after he talked to Chevalier and Legend. 
Flechette is here to stay though, especially now that Stalker defected.” 

“I doubt she will be the last,” Dinah said with a smirk. 

Missy groaned even as Aisha laughed.  Even if it wasn’t true, just the
idea of more heroes leaving would scare the shit out of the rest of the
heroes.  Aisha only wished she could sit in on those meetings as the
heroes pissed themselves and second guessed everyone.  Oh well, she
could at least attend the Teeth meetings where everyone had a laugh over
the heroes running around like idiots. 

“I’d ask for good Teeth gossip, but I think Sophia leaving like that is
as good as it gets,” Missy grumbled.  “I just can’t see anything topping
that anytime soon.” 

“And you jinxed us,” Aisha said as Dinah grimaced.  “Just watch, shit is
gonna hit the fan, or Weaver’s gonna go on an acid trip.” 

Dinah shook her head.  “Seven point zero five seven one percent chance
that Weaver tries anything psychoactive within the next two weeks.”

“That’s seven percent too high,” Missy said.  “Did you see the footage
from that?  Weaver fought the entire Protectorate at once.” 

“And she was playing around too,” Aisha said proudly.  “Boss lady is a
badass bitch after all.” 

“Generous too,” Dinah said.  “I think we’re all millionaires after Lisa
balanced the books for Taylor.” 

“Blood money,” Missy grumbled. 

“Hey, you should be sitting pretty by the time you turn eighteen,” Aisha
countered.  “Your merchandise is popular as fuck.  You have to be worth
millions by now.” 

“I might be if my parents didn’t squander everything they had access
to,” Missy said darkly. 

“That sounds illegal as shit,” Aisha said. 

“You would be the expert,” Missy countered, then slumped.  “They can’t
touch my college fund, but they can touch my merchandising revenue,
which is one of the highest among the Wards nationwide.”  

“Just say the word and we’ll set Lisa loose on them for you,” Dinah
said.  “She can get the Youth Guard involved and maybe throw it to Carol
to keep her off Amelia’s back.  There’s a small window where things can
go extremely wrong and we need to head that off.” 

Missy paused for a moment, staring at her drink.  Then, she downed the
rest of the cup, shivered and met Dinah’s eyes.  “Do it.  Fuck my parents.” 

“Kinky.” Aisha said without missing a beat.

“Someone’s been spending too much time around Alec and Michael.” Dinah
said with a smirk as she fired off a text.  “Done.  Detective Lisa is on
the case.” 

“And like that I’ve embraced villainy…” Missy muttered. 

“Eh, more villainy adjacent.” Aisha said.  “It’s not too different from
how Lisa sic’d Carol on the Canary case.  Villainy for a good cause and
all that.” 

“The only villainy involved there was by the PRT.” Dinah said heatedly. 
“Besides, the numbers are better with Canary free.” 

Missy swallowed, apparently not happy with the implications.  “Would you
have left her to her fate if they weren’t?” 

“No.” Dinah said, her teeth grinding.  “I saw glimpses of what Coil had
planned for me.  I refuse to force imprisonment on anyone for the
greater good, especially when they’re innocent.” 

“Nobody likes a Dumbledore type.” Aisha agreed.  “The greater good can
shove it.” 

Missy looked like she had sucked a lemon at that statement, but who
could argue with it?  That case being made for the greater good and
avoiding undue risks had allowed the Empire to flourish, or at least
that was what Taylor and Lisa had said in the meeting.  Sometimes the
status quo was shit and had to be torn down. 

Aisha refilled Missy’s cup, putting in a much more liberal portion of
Jack this time, her friend needed it after all.  The sound of the front
door rattling had Aisha smirking as she hurried to top off her own cup,
as well as Dinah’s.  The door swung open, and Brian walked in, grumbling
about something under his breath when he froze in place, staring at the
three girls and the very obvious, and rather empty, bottle of liquor. 

Sucked to be him, she would have shared if he arrived sooner, snooze you
lose and all that. 

“Aisha, who are—” his voice cut off as he seemed to recognize Dinah. 
Aisha had heard about Dinah’s explosive introduction as well as how her
big brother had witnessed it, then pussed out like a bitch. 

“What is she doing here?” he asked Aisha with an accusatory tone.  “Why
is there a member of the Teeth in my home?” 

“Damn dude, way to forget my friends,” she said with a shake of her head
and took another drink.  “Sometimes it feels like you forget you even
have a sister.” 

Just to prove her point, she relaxed and faded from awareness.  Brian
blinked as his brain struggled to figure out what he was doing before
she threw her arm over his shoulder and tightened back down on her
powers.  She gave him a noogie to drive the point home. 

“What the hell?” he hissed, pulling away as he regarded his sister in a
new light.  “You’re a Stranger.” 

“Harsh,” Dinah said in a mocking whisper.  “He isn’t even denying it.” 

Aisha grinned.  Dinah had always been in her corner and it felt great
when she got to return the favor.  “Well, it’s not his fault he isn’t a
Thinker.”

“Aisha, you’re a cape,” he said dumbly as he looked at Dinah.  “You
brought a member of the Teeth into my home.” 

“Oh spare me the indignation,” Aisha said, high-fiving her mental
Taylor.  Scrabble night was starting to pay off.  “Since we’re being
open about all this fun stuff, you ran with the Undersiders.  Alec says
‘Blackout is a lame as shit name’ by the way, he suggested Tenebrae.” 

His face twisted as though she had struck him, which was what Alec had
actually asked her to do, but she counted the noogie as good enough. 
Then he turned eyes on Missy and seemed confused, her power was just
great like that.  

“Vista,” she said, not making eye contact.  “You skipped the Wards,
probably for informational security reasons.  We’re a lot more open
about our identities than the Protectorate tends to be.” 

“And what would Armsmaster say if I told him you’ve been drinking?”
Brian demanded.  “Or that you’re fraternizing with the Teeth?” 

“He already knows,” Missy said.  “I called him as soon as I found out my
friend was with the Teeth.” 

“My girl here even had ramen with Weaver,” Aisha said, giving Missy a
side hug.  “She also tased the shit out of Bastard Son.  Certified
badass is what she is!” 

“Aisha, you’re drunk.” 

“I will only admit to that if you admit you left booze where
unsupervised minors could reach it,” Aisha countered.  “Besides, Weaver
lets us smoke and drink.” 

“Weaver wouldn’t be happy we’re drinking on a school night,” Dinah
interjected.  “She does take our educations seriously.” 

Aisha grinned.  “She does, which was why we were discussing whether we
would go to Arcadia or Winslow.” 

“Don’t the Teeth run Winslow?” Brian asked.  Aisha could tell he was
getting pissed. 

“Browbeat goes to Winslow, as does Stalker,” Missy said.  “Though
Stalker quit the Wards today, she’s with the Teeth now.” 

“Don’t worry,” Aisha quickly interjected.  “I already warned her to stop
fucking with you or I would kill her myself.” 

“Don’t make threats you can’t follow up on,” Dinah said, quoting the
baddest of asses, Big Robbie.

“Wouldn’t be my first,” Aisha said, doing her best to not remember the
Empire assholes that had come for her.  “I’d even use the knife to make
a point.” 

Dinah groaned.  “You’ve been spending too much time with Alec.” 

“You what?” Brian asked, his voice turning hard.

Shit, she’d said too much and now she had to get into a subject she
really didn’t want to with her brother.  Her friends were one thing, but
him?  Would he actually understand, or would he throw another tantrum
and give her shit for that too?  Oh well, at least he wasn’t being pissy
about the alcohol anymore. 

“You heard me Brian, I’ve killed people.  The fuckers that caused my
trigger for one, which Lisa says was a hit put out by your former boss
before Dinah here put him down.”  Her brother sucked in a breath, but
she wasn’t done.  “Weaver tries to keep me from having to kill, but she
made it quite clear that she wouldn’t berate me if it came down to it. 
My life is more important than some fucker that came around to cause
problems.” 

“Well spoken.” Dinah cheered, raising her glass then downing the rest. 
“Besides, the only real danger left in this city at the moment is the
Protectorate.  The numbers keep shifting, but they’re going to start
something in the next few hours, and if it goes bad a lot of people will
die.” 

“I’ve not heard of anything aside from another rotation heading to
Boston tomorrow morning.” Brian said, and there was no way Aisha wasn’t
taking that little nugget straight to Taylor first thing.  “We don’t
even have a local director, Rennick’s under the Chief Director’s orders
to be as unantagonistic to the Teeth as he possibly can.” 

“Someone new is coming, but I haven’t figured out who it is yet.” Dinah
said.  “Things get murky when I try to narrow it down, which means
someone is working to keep Thinkers in the dark.” 

“That’s ominous.” Aisha said.  “If we knew who it was we could just have
Weaver visit them in their sleep and give them the Ghosts of Butcher’s
Past experience.” 

Dinah waved her off.  “Just because Taylor can use her bugs to let the
previous Butchers communicate doesn’t mean she’s going to reenact
classic—  Oh no…  She /would / use them to reenact classic literature.” 

“Because she’s a big ‘ol nerd.” Aisha said with a grin.

Now she just had to find a way to be there when Taylor pulled it off,
preferably with a camera and some popcorn. 

Big bro muttered something as he pulled out his phone, then paused as he
stared at the screen.  Did he have a girlfriend or something sending him
tit pics?  She wasn’t exactly jealous of that, but it was a lot easier
to be open about her own bisexuality now that the Nazis were gone.

“The Teeth kidnapped Panacea,” Brian said, blinking before he began to
grab his things to head out the door. 

“The Empire tried that one already,” Dinah said, then muttered something
to herself.  “Oh, it would seem Amelia has joined the Teeth full time
now, rather than moonlighting.” 

Missy’s eyes widened in horror, then in a completely uncharacteristic
move, she looked at her cup and downed the entire glass.  Aisha watched
the girl drift from side to side, then drop to the floor, completely
wasted.  Whatever, her friend would be fine, but she needed to get back
to the arena and celebrate the new member.  The Teeth were no doubt
throwing a kickass party without her!

She moved to down her own cup, but Brian snatched it away and downed it
himself before she could even engage her awesomeness and snatch it back,
the cheat!  Oh well, she did just that, taking the empty cup and moving
to refill it while everyone was completely unaware of her.  Big bro was
too busy typing to pay attention anyway. 

She flopped down beside Dinah, then reigned in her ability once again. 

“This good or bad?” Aisha asked, being careful not to ask a question
that could be answered with numbered odds. 

“Both,” Dinah said.  “This change means we are going to have an eventful
week, but it also heads off several bad ends in the future.” 

“That’s good,” Aisha said.  “Any other insights you can offer, all
seeing Omen?” 

Dinah set her cup aside and took the bottle in hand.  She stared at it
for a moment, then downed a heavy swig.  “Enjoy yourself now, for we
won’t be able to do so in the coming days as the Teeth drown in sorrow.” 

Well shit, that was an omen worth drinking to.

/Tuesday May 10th, 2011 /

“That covers Little Japan…” Charlotte muttered, going over the paperwork
Lisa had supplied her the day before.    “What about the Archer’s Bridge
project?” 

“Still progressing.” Kevin answered, looking over his own paperwork.   
“The Merchants really fucked it up during their short tenure, it will
take a lot of canvassing to see who needs what help.” 

Doing all of this in the ass a.m hours wasn’t her idea of a good time,
but there were too many things that needed to be done before school
started and not enough hours in the day to see it done.  Given what
happened with Amelia just a few hours ago, it was best if the only Teeth
presence on the streets was that of their charity teams.

Charlotte sighed.    “Do what you can, I need to get in touch with Rachel.” 

“You’ve been spending a lot of time with Bitch.” Kevin commented slyly. 
  “Anything I need to kick up to Vex or Weaver for teasing points?” 

“No, just helping her with her shelter,” Charlotte replied hurriedly.   
“She’s great with the dogs, but she needs help managing the permits and
supply stuff.” 

“Mhmm, and why can’t you delegate that to an underling?” Another of her
minions asked. 

“Would you rather deal with Rachel?” She asked, tallying a few numbers
and hoping she got them right.    “The last minion I sent pissed her off
enough for her to sic the dogs on him.”

Minion number two winced.    “Oh right, Fred’s still fucked up from that.” 

“Exactly.  At least with me she hesitates before snapping,” Charlotte said. 

“Because she sees you as an authority figure,” Madison interjected,
dropping the massive crate they’d been hauling off the truck.  “You’re
friends with Taylor, and that means you’re above the others in her mind.” 

“Rache doesn’t really get people,” Charlotte said softly.  “She seems to
think more like a dog than a person.” 

“You took the time to learn how she views the world, you show her
respect,” Madison said with a shrug.  “It makes sense that she trusts you.” 

“Says the person that turned themself into a dog just to get belly
rubs,” Charlotte countered with a smirk, earning an indignant squawk
from the Changer. 

“That was one time!” Madison snarled. 

“And you were drunk,” Charlotte said with a smirk.  “Don’t get me wrong,
a power like yours?  I’d do stuff like that all the time.  It’s a shame
the Wards limit you to Browbeat.” 

“Tell me about it.  It can be so damn tempting to just let loose and go
full t-rex or something on the gangs.” 

Charlotte smirked.  “Or Xenomorph.” 

“You have no idea how fun that was,” Madison said with an inhumanly wide
grin.  “Too bad the PRT have a stick up their ass right now over
Taylor.  The only reason they’re tolerating my being here is because it
is genuine charity work and they’re counting it as time served on my
community service.”  

They tapped their ankle monitor for emphasis. 

“Hard to move against the Teeth when all they’re doing is helping the
city,” Charlotte agreed.  “Any word on if they’re going to transfer you?” 

Madison paused as they considered the question, then flopped back to sit
on one of the crates.  “Sophia tried fighting it, but they were going to
force it through, hence joining the Teeth.  They can’t say much about
the whole thing without potentially outing her and pissing off Weaver. 
Missy doesn’t want to go either and she’s managed to twist both parents
into fighting to keep her here.” 

“You didn’t mention yourself,” Charlotte said, eyeing Madison
carefully.  “Are they shipping you off as well?” 

“They want to, and my parents are entertaining it,” they admitted. 
“Assault’s trying to help but there’s only so much he can do without
outing me as Ripley.  They’d ship me off in an instant if that happened.” 

“Wouldn’t that just piss off Weaver?” One of the minions asked, getting
a glare from both girls.  He held up his hands in surrender and scurried
off. 

“You’ll figure something out,” Charlotte said softly.  “If not, you
could always defect and dare them to try something.” 

Madison laughed.  “Hell, I could just take a page out of Taylor’s
playbook and just flaunt that I’m Ripley and dare them to say
something.  Hell, it’s working for Sophia.” 

Charlotte hummed.  “Taylor has been complaining you aren’t wearing the
shirt.” 

“I think I have a hoodie waiting for me at Parian’s too.” Madison noted,
pulling out their phone.  “Fuck it.  I should be able to swing some time
on the boardwalk if I can talk Assault or Battery into covering for me.” 

Charlotte did a quick check of her own responsibilities and saw everyone
was ahead of schedule.  She could afford to hand things over to someone
and take a bit of time for herself.  She needed to get over to Rachel’s
shelter anyway and the Boardwalk wasn’t too far out of the way. 

“Fuck it, Kevin!” The man in question looked up.  “Executive privilege,
take over while I deal with some shit!” 

“Got it covered!” He yelled back. 

Charlotte grinned at Madison’s incredulous look.  “Sometimes you just
have to own the fact that you work for a supervillain and you’d be
amazed how many people just fall in line.” 

“Whatever you say,” Madison said, shaking their head with a wry grin. 
“I’ve got a ride on the way.” 

“Don’t want to call the Teeth chauffeur services?” 

Madison snorted.  “Do you want to explain to the PRT why a Ward is in a
black SUV with two Teeth members?” 

“Three, technically,” Charlotte added casually.  “Part time employment
is still employment.” 

Madison frowned as a car pulled up and the passenger window rolled down.
  A man who looked to be in his twenties was in the driver’s seat
wearing an obnoxious pair of sunglasses.  

“Maddy!  You called for a lift?” the man hollered. 

“Ethan, could you be any less subtle?” they asked, grabbing their bag
and gesturing for Charlotte to follow. 

Charlotte shook her head as she followed, looking the man in the eyes as
he frowned at her choice of outfit.  It wasn’t obvious, a red tank top
and pale jeans that looked gray enough in the sun.  It was still enough
to make him visibly nervous.

“Friend of yours?” he asked. 

“Classmate.  She’s the one coordinating the fundraising efforts today,”
Madison answered. 

“I heard rumors that the Teeth were behind things,” he said, glancing
back at Charlotte as he pulled away.  “Doesn’t seem like their kind of
thing.” 

“People keep saying that until they actually meet Weaver,” Charlotte
said casually.  “She tends to tear down people’s expectations of what a
Butcher can be.” 

“Until she strips a man to his bones,” Ethan mumbled before continuing a
bit louder.  “He was a Nazi, so I can’t say it wasn’t deserved, but it
still falls a bit close to the old Butcher ways.” 

“It’s a good reminder that the kinder, gentler Butcher can still be the
Butcher when needed,” Madison said, surprising both her and Ethan. 

“You’re getting too attached,” Ethan muttered.  “We might need to pull
you out.” 

Madison snorted.  “Good luck with that, you’d lose more than just me if
you tried.” 

“Stalker was on her way out regardless,” Ethan said. 

Charlotte kept quiet, not wanting to interrupt the rather fascinating
conversation by reminding them she was there. 

“Stalker is the least of your problems,” Madison said, smirking.  “Want
to roll those dice and see where they land?” 

“They do not pay me enough for this,” Ethan mumbled. 

“You could always come work for us,” Charlotte said casually.  “We pay
better and have great dental.” 

“You do know I bring home six figures, right?” Ethan said. 

“And I’ll probably bring home seven,” Charlotte countered.  “I am
literally the community manager for the entirety of the Teeth.  Weaver
comes to me when shit hits the fan and she needs to run damage control.” 

“Here I thought she’d have her Thinkers on this,” Ethan said.  “No
offense, but you don’t look very much like Tattletale to me.” 

“I’m not a cape at all, I just happen to have a skill most of the Teeth
lack,” Charlotte said confidently.  “I’m good with people.” 

Madison snorted, then barked out a laugh at something.  “Could you
imagine if she put Animos in your shoes?” 

Charlotte groaned.  “Thanks, now I’m going to have nightmares.  It’s
hard enough to spin his whole ‘I eat people’ thing as it is.” 

“She can never meet Glen,” Ethan said solemnly. 

Before Charlotte could wonder who that was, Madison cackled. 

“I can only imagine how many notes he wants to compare at this point. 
The Teeth have kinda rewrote the script on how villains can win over a
population.” 

Charlotte took some measure of pride in that statement.  It hadn’t been
all her of course, but she had tempered Taylor and Lisa’s suggestions
and turned them into something viable, working off of their Thinker
abilities and consulted with Dinah to ensure they wouldn’t backfire too
much if things went off script due to other Thinkers. 

A few had tried, and Lisa managed to confirm a suspicion she had about
Bagrat being part of the Protectorate Think Tank.  It didn’t change
things too much, and they managed to keep their topics on message for
the past few weeks while winning the ongoing PR war through their
charity drives while the Protectorate at large focused on their usual
games of patrols and PR events. 

Unfortunately for them, the smiling faces of heroes don’t put food in
the bellies of hungry people.  The Teeth did that instead.  They worked
with those displaced by the gang wars, those suddenly out of work or
just in a spot of bad luck.  Job drives had sprung up, with the DWU
taking in almost five hundred new workers as the contracts for
reconstruction efforts poured in. 

Lisa had leveraged Fortress Construction quite well in that regard,
working exclusively with the DWU for their projects and were even
drafting plans to clear out the boat graveyard.  They just needed the
Teeth and the Protectorate to have a few more high profile skirmishes in
the area first to kick start it all. 

Taylor had that handled, which meant that she just had to play damage
control when it kicked off.  An easy enough task when most people would
applaud the Teeth for limiting their fighting to the graveyard.  The
Teeth showed restraint under Taylor, and always worked to limit
collateral damage.  Even in all her takedowns of the ABB before she
joined, the damage was limited to her targets, even if she did have a
bit of an arson streak back then. 

The Empire and Coil however were surgical, even against hard targets
like that first Empire raid before the Teeth had been given proper
training.  She had even recorded some of their training and ‘leaked’ it
just to prove the point.  Lisa had loved the initiative and Taylor had
been embarrassed to see footage of her facing off against Robbie’s team
in the pits.  She approved of their paintball match footage though. 

“Are we there yet?” Madison muttered as Ethan sang along to some oldies
rock music. 

“Keep whining and I sing louder,” he answered with a grin. 

Charlotte huffed.  “Careful, Weaver plays guitar.  I can always get you
a private showing.” 

Ethan paled, and both teens took great pleasure in the sudden lack of
off key singing for the rest of their ride to the Boardwalk.  When they
reached the closest parking, the pair quickly divested themselves of
their escort, much to his irritation, but he didn’t protest too much,
and he phoned in that he would be keeping a distant watch on Madison
while they went shopping with a classmate. 

“Ethan seems pretty chill,” Charlotte said as they made their way
towards Parian’s soon to open shop. 

Madison sighed.  “I know you’re respecting the rules and all, but it
should be obvious that they wouldn’t assign a standard PRT agent to
watch me when I’m associating with the Teeth in my off hours.” 

“I haven’t a clue,” Charlotte said with a cheeky grin.  “I’m thinking I
might pick up a custom jacket myself.” 

“Pretty sure she’s already making you one,” Madison answered.  “Talked
to her a bit on my last patrol and she mentioned a few ideas she had.” 

Charlotte took note of how Madison was blushing a bit and grinned.  “Any
ideas of your own make it in there?” 

“Maybe,” they answered and picked up their pace ever so slightly. 

They arrived at the storefront shortly after, a large ‘coming soon’ sign
hung from the window where several fancy dresses were already on
display.  Charlotte took a moment to admire the outfits before knocking
on the door. 

“We’re not open,” a familiar voice came. 

“Not even for investors?” she answered back. 

There were sounds of panicked rustling before the door was suddenly
open, revealing a ruffled Sabah in civilian attire.  She looked at the
two of them then the crowds in the distance before she sighed, then she
raised her voice comically loud. 

“Sorry, Parian’s not in right now, can I help you?” 

Madison snorted.  “Here for a hoodie, think you could help?” 

Sabah eyed them carefully for a moment, then stepped aside, gesturing
for the pair to come in.  The door shut behind them and Charlotte was
more than a little surprised to find that Sabah hadn’t been alone.  A
rather cute Asian girl was leaning against the counter, trying far too
hard to appear innocent.  

Madison broke down into laughter and walked right up to the girl and
raised an open hand.  The girl, in her confusion, lifted her own and
Madison high fived her.  “Nice going Lils, knew ya had it in ya!” 

She groaned.  “I knew it…  Just how much did you win?” 

“About a hundred since I have to split it with Carlos,” they answered. 

“There was a betting pool?” Sabah asked with mounting horror. 

“Don’t look at me,” Charlotte said quickly.  “It wasn’t us.  Taylor and
Chrissie would have loved to get in on this, though there would have
been thousands on the line in that case.”

“Of course they would,” Sabah said with a sigh.  “Yes, Lily and I are
dating, happy now?” 

Both Madison and Charlotte let out various ‘awws’ in reply as Sabah
rolled her eyes.  “So, what brought you two out to my humble little shop
today?” 

Charlotte glanced at one of the glass displays holding an elaborate
scarlet dress made of spider silk with a six figure price tag and a
‘sold’ sign attached.  “Humble, right.” 

“Hey, exotic materials means exotic prices,” Sabah said with a shrug. 
“Still, that’s cheap compared to the prices I charge the Protectorate
for a simple body suit.” 

“Um…  They know?” Lily asked softly, looking Charlotte’s choice of
outfit over. 

“Yes, they know.  Charlotte was a big help in getting my shop set up,
and Madison pays regular visits when on patrol to make sure people are
respecting Brockton’s rules about independents.” 

“Madison?” Lily asked carefully. 

“They all know I’m Browbeat,” they said with a weary sigh.  “Never mind
that Jouster basically outed all of us to the Teeth when he decided
flirting with Weaver in civvies was a good idea.” 

‘Dumbass’ Charlotte coughed, getting a few laughs from everyone in the
room. 

“Right, so, you wanted a custom hoodie?” Sabah asked, changing the
subject.  “What were you looking for, exactly?” 

Charlotte could see that Sabah was eying Lily carefully, which was fair,
but Madison didn’t seem to care.  “I’m thinking audacious, so red and
gray with a Xenomorph print on the back, with Clements embroidered over
it.” 

Lily sucked in a breath as Sabah nodded.  “Had a feeling you might ask
for one eventually.  Didn’t know it was you though, so it doesn’t have a
last name on it yet.” 

“You’re Ripley?” Lily hissed.  “What the fuck, Mads!” 

“I’m surprised you hadn’t figured any of it out yet,” Madison said with
a shrug as Sabah slipped away.  “I was one of the bitches that caused
Weaver’s trigger.  She didn’t kill me, and when I saved her girlfriend
from being arrested in the Empire’s little trap, she let me help put
them down.” 

“If the Protectorate finds out—

Madison laughed.  “Assault, Battery and Armsmaster are all aware.  Hell,
those attacks may as well have been sanctioned with how I reported
directly to Assault for both of them.  How do you think the PRT managed
to ferry Rune and Othalla away in the chaos?” 

“We thought the Teeth abducted them,” Lily said with a haunted tone. 
“What else are the PRT doing behind the scenes if they’re condoning
black ops like this…” 

“Offering captured villains a plea deal for joining up is fairly
common,” Charlotte said, looking over a catalog Sabah was putting
together.  “Besides Shadow Stalker, they’ve taken in Rune, Othalla and
Purity recently, and I can say you’ve met at least one other villain
that flipped sides.” 

“And more than one hero,” Madison added as Sabah returned.  “Don’t
forget that Weaver started as a hero until the Protectorate fucked her
over.” 

“How’s this?” Sabah asked, holding up a Teeth standard hoodie much like
Taylor’s.

The design was exactly as Madison had requested, with the Alien’s visage
taking up most of the hoodie’s back.  Room had been left for a name, and
Madison grinned. 

“Perfect!  How long until you can get my last name added?” 

“Clements, right?” Sabah asked.  “Give me about ten minutes, I have the
embroidery stuff on hand.” 

Threads sprung into motion all around Sabah as letters were plucked from
a drawer and she deftly sewed them on with her powers.  Her casual
display reminded Charlotte a bit of Taylor with her swarm, and the way
she directed all of it without even paying it any obvious mental focus.  

Lily was off to the side, deep in thought and barely paying any
attention to it all.  That was understandable given she’d just had
another pillar of her worldview rattled, much as she no doubt had when
she met Taylor in civvies.  Charlotte’s own views had been suitably
rattled when Taylor swooped in, outed herself as Weaver, then put the
Teeth bullies in their place. 

She appreciated the irony that the two that had bullied her that day now
reported to her directly when she all but took over managing the Teeth
at Winslow.  Her responsibilities had only grown since, but she was
enjoying the challenge and that she was genuinely helping people.  That
brought her mind back to an argument she had with her parents… 

 

------------------------------------------------------------------------

 

“It’s not that bad,” Charlotte insisted, ignoring the glare from her
parents.    “The Teeth don’t pressure me to do anything.” 

“But you still do things for them,” her mother stated.    “You joined a
gang!    I know we raised you better than this!” 

“You caught me coordinating charity work!” Charlotte shot back.    “I
don’t run drugs, I don’t collect protection money.    I help the poor
and needy, I just do it with the Teeth’s approval.” 

“You were doing more than that,” Her father interjected.    “The Teeth
looked up to you, there were adults in Teeth colors following your
orders.    We aren’t blind Char, you aren’t someone unimportant.” 

Charlotte steeled herself, knowing revealing this would spark
something.    “I go to school with Weaver…    She saved me from some
bullies back in April.” 

“Weav— the Butcher,” her mother gasped but her father pressed on.   
“That madwoman who killed that Anders guy?” 

“Kaiser.    She killed Kaiser,” Charlotte grit out.    

Why was it that so many people focused on her killing a man rather than
call him the monster that he was?    Her parents were Jewish and they
still didn’t see him as a Nazi first.    It was infuriating. 

“Nazi or not, she killed him in a horrific way and turned it into a
spectacle,” her mother said softly.    “How can you feel safe around her?” 

“Because, the people that tormented her at school are still alive,”
Charlotte whispered.    “She hates bullies because she was bullied
herself, both before and after she got her powers, even after she became
Butcher fifteen.    She won’t tolerate it and she acts as a shield for
everyone indiscriminately.” 

“The Butcher is insane,” Her father declared.    “She’s dangerous.” 

“Dangerous is an understatement.  Anyone with powers is,” Charlotte
answered.    “But she isn’t insane.    She’s articulate and most of the
school speaks well of her.    She would rather cuddle with her
girlfriend than hurt others, she just isn’t afraid to do so when needed.” 

“The students know she’s the Butcher?” her mother asked. 

“She doesn’t hide her identity,” Charlotte said confidently.    “She
puts herself on display, makes sure everyone knows because it means that
if anyone does anything to her friends or family there are no excuses.” 

“Like with Hookwolf,” Her father said. 

“Yes, that was a direct attack on someone’s family.    She took
exception to that.” Charlotte sighed.  “She’s not a bad person, she just
ended up in a shitty situation and tried to make the most of it.” 

“We just worry about you,” her mom said softly. 

“You could always meet Weaver yourself,” Charlotte said just as softly.  

“I—  We’ll think about it, okay?” Her dad said, surprising her.  “So
long as you stay out of the dangerous stuff, stick to helping people
like you have been…” 

 

------------------------------------------------------------------------

 

“What about you Charlotte?” Sabah asked, snapping her out of the
memory.  “Were you wanting anything while I’ve got all the stuff out?” 

“Uh…  Sure?” She muttered, caught a bit off guard by the casual offer. 

Sabah chuckled at her, prompting a pout that only made everyone else
join her in their mirth.  “So, given your name and how your boss loves
her spiders, I thought a play on Charlotte’s Web might suit you.” 

She then pulled one of the spare hoodies from behind the counter, a
spider’s web stitched into the shoulders but no other branding was
present.  It was fitting in a way for the girl that managed things in
the background for the Capes.  She accepted it with a smile and tried it
on, finding it was a near perfect fit, just ever so slightly loose to
allow her to keep growing a bit more. 

“It’s perfect,” Charlotte said. 

An irritated huff snapped her out of the moment, turning a harsh glare
upon Lily whose stride was heavy as she approached and shoved a finger
at Sabah. 

“How can you be so casual with the Teeth?”  She then spun on Madison. 
“And you, how the fuck can you work for them like that!?” 

Madison sighed.  “You’ve met Weaver, so tell me.  Did Taylor strike you
as someone likely to burn the city down?”

“Well, no but—”

“She’s making the best of the hand that was dealt to her,” Madison said
softly.  “She had every reason to become a horrific villain, yet her
responses have been measured.  Even when Militia put a bullet in Panacea
right in front of her, she didn’t strip the flesh from her bones, even
though she would have been justified in doing so.  What does that say
about Taylor to you?” 

“That she isn’t a fool,” Charlotte cut in.  “She would have been
justified in killing Militia, but given the state of the city and the
PRT, she would have just started yet another battle with escalating
stakes.  She chose to step back and deescalate instead.” 

“Which gave them the excuse to fire Piggot and move heroes in to regain
control of the situation,” Lily finished, her voice trailing off.  “They
brought the Wards in as a cover for stationing more heroes here, to keep
the Boston contingent on rotation and to have more people on hand if
things with the Teeth did escalate.” 

“Any truth to the rumors that Piggot started shit in Washington and we
might be getting a real piece of work as the new director?” Charlotte
asked.  “Tattletale’s been having issues getting solid information out
of Washington thanks to anti-Thinker measures being used, but she’s
confirmed that a man named Tagg is being considered.” 

“I’ve only heard a few whispers,” Madison said cautiously.  “A few
people are worried about it, because the man is a soldier, not a
negotiator.” 

“This is the same man that shot a nine year old villain who was holding
a Ward hostage,” Lily said softly.  “He’d happily shoot Weaver if given
the chance, consequences be damned.” 

“Which would light the spark that set the city ablaze,” Charlotte said
with a frown.  “She’s trying to get the city back on its feet, but if
she has to deal with him instead…” 

“She’ll kill him at the first excuse,” Madison said softly.  “He’d die a
martyr, galvanizing those in Washington that want to crack down on
villains.” 

“What a mess we’ve found ourselves in,” Charlotte muttered.  “So, how
much do I owe you for the hoodie?” 

“Tab’s covered,” Sabah said offhandedly.  “Taylor paid in advance for
any member of the Teeth to get custom clothes.” 

“How much in advance?” Lily asked curiously. 

“Quarter mil.” Sabah said, going back over to work on an intricate silk
dress in grays and red, one with a suspiciously conspicuous XV being
stitched into it.  “Taylor wants to make sure my shop succeeds and that
nobody can pressure me into anything I don’t want to do.” 

Charlotte nodded.  “Taylor is very much against forced recruitment for
her own forces.  She finds the PRT’s practices distasteful.” 

Lily seemed to consider those words and lost herself in thought. 
Charlotte took the opportunity to hook her arm through Madison’s and
made for the door. 

“Feel free to swing by anytime,” Sabah called back.  “I do novelty
shirts too if you’re interested.” 

“I’ll keep that in mind.  Thanks again!” Madison answered back, trying
to ignore Lily’s eyes still being glued to their retreating figure. 

“Well, that was awkward,” Charlotte muttered once they were outside. 

“Lily’s been a member of the club longer than Missy,” Madison said,
looking back at the shop as they walked towards Ethan’s car.  “It’s no
surprise this is confusing for her.” 

“How aware is the PRT of the division in the ranks around Weaver?”
Charlotte asked, her own curiosity getting the better of her. 

“Legend is quite aware, and he’s shuffled people around to keep the
detractors away as best he can.  Dauntless and Velocity are in Boston
for the next few weeks and may be transferred permanently.” 

“It truly is the calm before the storm,” Charlotte muttered.  “All we
can do is keep showing everyone that the Teeth aren’t the murder hobos
they used to be and hope it’s enough.” 

“A tall order,” Ethan said loud enough to startle both of them. 
“Weaver’s doing a good job of it for all the locals, but they aren’t the
real problem.” 

“I know…” Charlotte said.  “But they’re the ones that matter most, the
ones we can actually help.” 

Ethan nodded, opening the back door for them.  “Well spoken, I couldn’t
agree more.”  Madison slid in first, scooting over to the far window
before Charlotte slipped in beside her.  Ethan quickly shut the door and
came back around to the driver’s side.  “So, where to next, ladies?”

“The shelter on fifth and Clarkson, Rachel’s expecting us.”

“Sure, I can—” A trilling sound cut the man off as he pulled a phone out
and frowned down at it.  “The fuck?  Sorry, but I need to get Madison
back to err…  You know.  I’ve got to be somewhere apparently.” 

“Wait, are they sending you to Boston?” Madison asked, sounding
alarmed.  “I thought they were trying to keep the friendlies close at
hand.” 

“No idea,” Ethan said, glaring at the Changer.  Oh right, Madison was
just admitting that Ethan was a cape right in front of a Teeth member. 
Then again, Weaver had met with most of the important Protectorate capes
in civvies just days earlier, so why did it matter?  “But something
tells me it won’t end well.” 

“I’ll need to pass that along to Weaver,” Madison said.  “The last thing
we need is a pissed off Butcher all because one of the people that
tolerated her was pulled from the city.” 

“True,” Ethan said begrudgingly.  “I’m fairly certain Armsmaster is
being ordered to go as well, and Puppy just messaged me that she got the
same notice, which means we’ll need a dog sitter.” 

“I can check in on Furdinand if you aren’t back by this evening,”
Madison confirmed.

Charlotte failed to keep a straight face at the poor dog’s name.  Rachel
could never hear it, because she would no doubt have more than a few
words to say about the subject. 

“Thanks,” he said with a weak smile.  “I’ve got a really bad feeling
about all this, so be sure to take care of yourself.” 

“As best I can,” Madison said.  “Think you can release my ankle
monitor?  Just in case I need to act in my off the books role.” 

“Promise to behave?” he asked, all levity gone. 

Madison nodded.  “I’ll act in my capacity as ordered, and provide a full
report following your return.” 

“All I can ask,” he said.  “Now hop out so I can get to work.” 

“Yes sir,” Madison snapped with a crisp salute. 

Charlotte kept out of that conversation, but her fingers were flying
across her phone’s keyboard.  If all of this was going down before
school even started, it spoke to plans that would likely conclude before
the day was done.  She might not be a cape, but that wouldn’t stop
Charlotte from supporting her friends.

Chapter End Notes

    Chapter 44: Consequence 4.5

Chapter by Pendragoon <https://archiveofourown.org/users/Pendragoon/
pseuds/Pendragoon>

Chapter Notes

See the end of the chapter for notes <#endnotes44>

/Tuesday May 10th, 2011 /

Amelia snored lightly, finally asleep after her harrowing evening.  That
Carol /fucking / Dallon would attempt to sell her children to the
Protectorate was enough to make my blood boil, but I had to take solace
in the fact that she was safe for the moment.  Lisa was stroking her
hair, smiling softly down at her from where she laid on Lisa’s lap. 

/“That shit is too damn sweet,” / Fester said. 

Chisel however was focused on something else.  /“We’re skinning that
bitch first chance we get.”  /

There was a round of agreement from the collective, and I wasn’t about
to deny them.  In fact, I wanted it just as much as they did, perhaps
moreso.  Seeing Amelia finally at peace warmed my heart in a way that
was difficult to ignore.  Knowing that she was my line in the sand, that
I was willing to kill heroes for her if needed?  The only other person
that made me feel that way was Chrissie, and I wasn’t sure I was ready
to dig into what that meant. 

/“Oh come on, you know / exactly /what —”  /

I shoved Sanguine down, mostly because he was right, I just wasn’t ready
to unpack that mess and it wouldn’t be fair to Amelia to try to after
the… /everything /she just endured.  My hand reached across the couch,
finding Chrissie’s and squeezing gently.  We had taken up flanking
positions around Amelia and Lisa, to make sure she knew that the people
that cared about her were close at hand. 

That still left Victoria, who was currently sitting on another loveseat
and talking in low tones with Ashley.  I hadn’t expected Victoria to
join the fight, let alone the absolute screaming match she got into with
her mother. 

/“The soccer kick into the Bay was pretty damn great though,” / Knockout
said with a grin. 

The memory of the absolutely primal rage that Victoria unleashed,
followed by Brandish’s annoying ball form being launched out towards the
Bay, would probably remain with the Butchers for the rest of time — and
easily rank up there with some of the best moments in Teeth history. 

/“Now we just need her to become XVI so we can claim it as our own!” /
Sabertooth said. 

I rolled my eyes.  /You just want her so we can finally fly. / 

/“Do you blame us?” / Quarrel asked. / “Admit it, you want to fly too.” / 

Well, they weren’t wrong — I just wasn’t ready to become a voice in
someone else’s head.  I wanted at least a few years in the driver’s seat
before that happened.  Besides, that would just dump more stress on
Amelia, which I wanted to avoid at all costs. 

The collective chittered in laughter, but wisely kept their comments to
themselves.  Outside the sun had begun to rise, and I knew the coming
day would only lead to new headaches for the Teeth.  Amelia had made one
hell of a public declaration of her loyalty.  Hell, I could hear some of
the partying minions /singing songs /in celebration!  

/“You mean / hella /badass,” / Butcher cooed.  /“That girl is Teeth to
the core and you know it!” /

I rolled my eyes as I let my senses sweep through my swarm, taking stock
of my territory.  That was a bit of a misnomer these days given all of
Brockton counted towards that.  Amelia’s relay bugs allowed me to
perceive all of it, including the conversation currently underway in the
Wards area of the PRT building.  They had some anti-bug measures in
place, but there was never a truly bug free environment, especially when
someone wanted those bugs in place.

Madison was standing alongside Lily and Missy, arms crossed and glaring
at a cape that I didn’t recognize through my bugs’ limited senses.  I
hadn’t been paying it much attention at first, but the standoff had
drawn my metaphorical eye to the escalating altercation.  I couldn’t
make out what was being said either, but I did recognize that Madison
had their cube in hand and ready to be crushed. 

Each of my people carried one no matter where they went in the city, the
fly within were modified by Amelia to stand out to my senses and it
would send out a signal upon death to all nearby relay bugs, drawing my
attention to it even when sleeping.  With the city on the verge of
boiling over, I didn’t want to leave anything to chance after my father
needed to shoot a cape in his own office. 

/“It is strange that nothing has come of that,” / Stratego muttered. 

His power was less than helpful in determining what strategic advantage
the PRT wanted by just treating the event as self-defense, and we were
missing too many details.  Obviously they were planning something, since
they knew that we were related.  I didn’t have a secret identity, and
thus it was officially known that Danny Hebert was the Butcher’s
father.  Was that enough for them to overlook his actions?  It certainly
didn’t feel like it, especially with a faction working to replace the
Teeth with the Elite. 

I knew it would come back to bite us, I just wasn’t sure how. 

/“At least he claimed the trophy,” / Fester said.  /“Few unpowered ever
managed that, and it earned him a lot of respect around here.”  /

I still wasn’t sure how I felt about my father coming back to
headquarters with me, but he had indeed followed through on the
tradition of claiming a trophy, even if it wasn’t a body part.  A piece
of the man’s mask, still stained with his blood from the killing blow,
was more than fitting.  That it meant we were at the arena when Amelia
arrived was an added bonus and I couldn’t help but suspect Omen might
have pushed things a bit in that direction. 

Lily had stepped forward, and seemed to be dictating terms to the person
addressing them.  The bugs on Madison were picking up a subtle shaking
that I recognized as laughter.  Whatever was going on, I would no doubt
be hearing about it next time they came by the arena. 

/“They’re hardly the first hero the Teeth have corrupted, but I think
they might be my favorite,” / Sabertooth said. 

I couldn’t help but smirk.  /Is that some shapeshifter solidarity? /

/“Damn right it is.”  /

I wanted to laugh but it would disturb Amelia and that would be the
greatest sin in the world at the moment.  So, I just squeezed Chrissie’s
hand again and snuggled closer to Lisa, letting myself relax as best I
could.  It was hard not to listen in on others, especially with my ever
expanding domain.  I didn’t want to pressure Amelia, but there were good
odds that she could come up with bugs that I could hear or see through
just as well as I could with my own senses. 

Of course, now that the Protectorate knew Amelia was a biotinker, they
would be coming for her.  Pandemic’s debut removed any and all doubt,
and the PRT could hardly ignore the danger.  I needed to be ready for
whatever bullshit was coming, and I knew it meant I might need to kill
to keep her safe. 

/“Bring it,” / Butcher said. 

I didn’t dispute his words, and simply let myself drift off, content to
be with the people most important in my rather complicated life. 

 

------------------------------------------------------------------------

 

“Five more minutes.” 

A grunt escaped me at the sound of a familiar voice, all I wanted was to
curl up with the source of warmth and so that was what I did.  It
squirmed a bit, then I felt a gentle softness press to my lips.  I
leaned into the contact, returning the kiss with a smile.  My eyes
flicked open, but rather than deep red locks, I was instead greeted by a
frizzy mess of brown. 

The collective howled their approval even as my eyes shot wide open and
I pulled away.  Amelia was still in a half daze, and reached for me as I
jumped off the couch in a panic.  Shit, did she kiss me in her sleep
thinking that I was Lisa?  I slammed the entire collective into the
darkness to get a moment to think, and even then I could still sense
their amusement at my predicament. 

I knew that I had feelings for Amelia beyond friendship, but I’d always
chalked it up to being part of the Butcher experience.  She had Lisa,
however, and I didn’t want to do anything that might ruin that for
them.  The rest of my senses began to catch up with me, and it was with
a very deliberate slowness that I turned my head towards the kitchen
where Chrissie and Lisa were standing at the island. 

Lisa had her signature smile firmly fixed on her face, but Chrissie’s
expression was far more complicated than anything I had seen on her in
weeks.  The last time she looked at me like that, it had been when we
were fighting.  I almost reached for the furthest bug I could sense,
Pyro’s teleportation itching to pull me from the (social) danger, but I
quashed the urge. 

Amelia sat up, rubbing at her eyes as she did. 

“Too early,” Amelia muttered. 

Lisa shook her head, walking over with a steaming cup.  “Here, drink
this.  I think we all need to be awake and alert before we have this
conversation.” 

Amelia winced as she accepted the cup.  “How bad is it?” 

Lisa paused.  “Right, we have two conversations to get through.  Well,
easy one first then.  Someone posted a video of your little debut to

Sabertooth. 

/“Oh not this shit again!” / Sabertooth roared.  /“You gotta stop
blaming me for your shitty allergy!”  /

She wouldn’t, I knew that, just like Quarrel would never truly forgive
me for being the one to deal the killing blow and inheriting the mantle
of the Butcher.  When it finally came my turn to become a part of the
collective, I imagined I would hold a similar grudge against whoever
ripped me away from those I loved. 

/“You should get Stalker a pair of ice picks,” / Stratego said
suddenly.  /“Or hammers.  Anything that she could phase into someone
then rip out in the most brutal way possible.” /

/“That’s hardcore as fuck,” / Butcher said, almost in awe.  /“Where the
hell did that come from?”  /

Stratego sent a wave of smugness at the praise from our namesake and
basked in the cumulative preening of the collective.  Personally, I
filed the idea away for later once I was more assured that she wouldn’t
turn those weapons on me when my back was turned. 

“Come on,” I whispered.  “We should get dressed if we’re going to go
through with this plan and throw further wrenches into the hero’s PR
plans.” 

“But comfy,” Amelia said as she looked up, her eyes full of fire and
defiance, as well as something that I still wasn’t ready to quantify. 

I didn’t even need to turn to know Lisa had her smugest of grins
plastered on her face from her place in the cuddle pile.  Still, the day
was slipping away and there was only so much I wanted to just stay in, a
statement needed to be made. 

/“The PHO thread this spawns will be entertainment for days,” /Alkaline
said with a giggle. 

Sanguine chuckled.  /“Could you imagine social media in the bad old
days?  It would be a true trainwreck, and not that pretender that Robbie
ganked.”  /

That was an understatement if I ever heard one.  Hell, I hadn’t even
dared look at the current threads, let alone imagine them.  If anything
would get me banned from the forum, it would be sticking up for Amelia
in the face of whatever the mindless masses were spewing about her, or
the neverending propaganda being spread by all the PRT plants that
operate on the forum.

/“Sophia, Madison!” / I said through my swarm.  /“Wrap it up, we’re
going to school today to show the flag and make a statement.”  /

Madison didn’t need to be told twice, their form already shifting back
to the cutesy teen girl that nobody would ever suspect of being a five
hundred pound shapeshifting beast of flesh and acidic blood.

“Come on,” I said with my own lips this time.  “We can chill some more
once classes are over.” 

“That a promise?” Lisa asked.  “I’m going to be busy at Medhall today,
but I can certainly cut things short if you need me for any discussions
of a polyamorous nature.’ 

“Foot off the gas,” Chrissie said, stepping between Lisa and I.  “Just
because I’m pretty sure we are both more open to this than either of us
realized,” she spared a glance back at me and I nodded in agreement,
“doesn’t mean you need to overplay it.  Just, let us work through this
on our own, we’ll let you know when we’re ready to expand the discussion.” 

“Just keep me in the loop,” Lisa said with a wink. 

I didn’t need bloodsight to know that Amelia was positively glowing from
embarrassment.  Hell, my face wasn’t much better and Sabertooth’s
shifting wasn’t nearly as good at hiding that as Madison’s. 

“Deal,” Lisa said.  “Alright, I’m off to make some Nazi supporters cry
as I render them broke and destitute, I’ll send you the recording.” 

/“Oh, that girl knows exactly what to say to moisten m—”  /

I shoved Fester down before she could finish the statement.  She pouted
at being cut off, but got the point.  The woman was like an aunt to me
and it was really fucking difficult to stay in the mood when she was
making sexual comments that often involved my own mother. 

It didn’t take long for us to split off and find something to wear, the
hoodies that Parian made for us were the dress code for the day,
everything else was just window dressing from there.  I made sure to
grab a half box of cold pizza from the fridge for us to nibble on for
the ride which Chrissie pulled from my hands with greedy glee, then
passed it over to Amelia who was a bit more skeptical about the contents. 

It was fun, having all of us getting ready together, even if Sophia was
the odd one out, I was already coming to accept her as part of our
circle.  She’d chosen the Teeth, and despite any worries I had about her
one day seeking the mantle, she was one of us and I’d treat her as such
right up until she stood across from me in the Arena under an official
challenge. 

Just as we were about to head out the door I stopped to turn the TV off
when I froze in place and every bug in the city began to frantically
scurry about.  A press conference was being shown live from a location
that I couldn’t locate anywhere inside of my range, but the news made it
clear that it was about Brockton Bay. 

There was Miss Militia standing alongside a cape called Luminescence
which was easily the most half assed rebranding Purity could possibly
have received, as well as a Ward by the name of Scribe who I already
knew to be a rebranded Rune thanks to Myrddin. 

They were coming back to Brockton Bay, despite my promise to kill any of
them if they did have the gall to return. 

/“Well, this will be good,” /Butcher said, rubbing his hands together.

Marauder grinned.  /“Looks like Nazi is back on the menu.”  /

/“Along with a side of bootlicker,” /Fester said. 

Marauder was positively ecstatic.  /“The question is, which are we
capping first?” /

Chapter End Notes
