Amelia still held Crowbar in her grip, and I could practically feel the
conflict coming off of her.  I took a tentative step forward, trying to
speak but choking on the words.  I had no room to talk as she seemed to
debate killing the minion, but the least I could do was be there for her
as I came up beside her and dropped to my knees before wrapping her in a
tight hug.

“They wanted to turn me into one of these,” Amelia whispered, still
holding the man by the wrist.  “I can tell there’s still a person in
there, but he’s been twisted.” 

“I know,” I said softly.  “You know my stance on killing.  If you’re
going to do it, make sure it’s for you and not because you think it’s
expected.” 

“Bastard,” Amelia whispered.  “I wanted to kill him, but our powers
conflicted.  We both needed skin contact, which he wasn’t willing to
risk.  He was going to bring in Canary.” 

I nodded, holding Amelia tighter.  Up above, my swarm at the waystation
spoke that we had Amelia, but I only then noticed that Lisa was absent,
as was Robbie’s entire team.  I almost panicked when the comms lit up. 

“We got Bastard,” Lisa said coldly.  “Weaver, bring our girl, she
deserves to see this.” 

/“Oh fuck,” / Pyro whispered.  /“I’ve never heard her like that before.”  /

/“Someone tried to Master her girlfriend,” / Fester said.  /“If there
was ever going to be a moment for her to step up, this is it.”  /

Right, because Lisa and Amelia weren’t killers, and the Teeth considered
that an important distinction no matter what I said or they
contributed.  Murder and trophies were status with my cabal of monsters,
so of course they would expect it after all this.  Well, Amelia had
already stepped up, and that fire extinguisher would be hers if I had
anything to say about it.  

I wrapped my arms around Amelia, neither of us were all that concerned
with getting blood on each other, we were both fairly coated as it was. 
I relished the moment even as I directed Chrissie through the carnage
towards me as well as a few minions to collect the trophies from the battle.

One of Amelia’s tendrils snaked up, lifting my mask and the next thing I
knew she was kissing me with a burning intensity that I didn’t know she
possessed.  At that same moment, my knees nearly buckled when every
pleasurable nerve in my body seemed to fire at once and I made more than
a few sounds that would have even my predecessors blushing.

“Well damn, deal me in for some of that,” Chrissie said with a wolf
whistle. 

Amelia made to pull away, but I managed to keep a firm enough grip on
her to prevent her from falling back and potentially hurting herself. 
She could have gotten away if she truly wanted, my grip remained loose
for that very reason.

“Oh good, you can carry Amelia back to the yards then,” I said, winking
at the flustered biokinetic.  “We don’t want Amelia to be late for her
appointment.” 

Chrissie opened her mouth to argue, but quickly shut it as she seemed to
realize the implications that might arise from carrying Amelia and moved
to sweep her off her feet with a bright grin. 

/“I can’t wait to see what we do to this prick,” / Alkaline
said.  /“Hopefully Amelia gets creative.”  /

/We won’t pressure her into anything, but after everything she just
endured, something tells me we won’t need to. /

/“Damn straight,” / Pyro exclaimed.

/“We really need to retire that phrase among the current Teeth,” /
Reflex said, shaking his head.

There was a beat of silence in my head, only for it to be broken a
moment later. 

/“Did Reflex just tell a joke?” / Fester demanded. 

/“I think he did,” / Quarrel answered, sounding dumbfounded. 

Damascian chuckled.  /“Well, I’ll be damned.” / 

Several gasps rang out in my mind, not because Damascian had cursed, but
because she had dropped the posh accent completely.  She didn’t do that
very often, which made the whole thing extra special. 

I hoisted the groaning form of Crowbar over my shoulder as Amelia
settled into Chrissie’s arms.  That didn’t stop her from watching the
man that she had disabled while biting her lip.  When I raised an
eyebrow she just shrugged. 

“I knocked him out, but I figure if his power isn’t too deadly he might
make for good arena fodder.  I’m still pissed at how they kidnapped me
and might want to take it out on him later.” 

“Fair,” I said, jostling the prick to little avail.  “This lump is all
yours after the speech, though I wouldn’t mind getting a few answers out
of him first.” 

“Pity Alec can’t manage that,” Chrissie said. 

“There’s other ways to make a man talk,” Amelia said.  “Be gentle with
him because I’ll want my trophies and I’ve got a few ideas.” 

/“Pan Pan gonna bring the pain pain,” / Sabertooth exclaimed. 

More groaning filled my mind, but that was okay.  I’d gotten my people
back, and with minimal injuries to show for it.  Bitch’s dogs were
roughed up from all the gunfire, but she didn’t seem too concerned with
the damage done to them.  If it was something serious she would have
told me.  Madison was with her, helping pull Brutus from his meat shell,
and the dog appeared fine to my senses.  Madison’s self-biokinesis meant
their injuries were healed as they took them, which was a very handy trick. 

/“They have my vote for XVI still,” / Marauder said.

/Alexandria or bust, I countered.  /

/“Ah, we can only dream,” / Knockout said with a wistful sigh.

Hauling the catatonic Mastered minion out of the lower levels of the old
penitentiary took longer than it should have, but that mostly came down
to my constantly misjudging corners, hitting something of his on each
and every one.  It was a damn shame that I seemed so rattled from all
the fighting and killing. 

/“Yes, truly a shame,” / Fester said when his head bounced off another
corner. 

“Could you please not break his brain?” Amelia asked from her princess-
carry in Chrissie’s arms.  “Just because I /can / fix his brain doesn’t
mean I’ll be able to get any memories lost back.” 

I had the decency to wince and made a point of judging the corners
properly going forward.  The battle had mostly died down, and my swarm
was now devoted to rooting out those last remaining defensive holdouts
hiding in bathrooms or closets.  Few had surrendered, but those who had
were currently covered in stinging and biting insects just waiting for
an excuse.  They would all be delivered to Lisa and interrogated for any
information we could use against the Elite.  Just because we had
repelled this group didn’t mean they would give up, only that their
disposable units weren’t good enough.

“Do I need to patch anyone up?” Amelia asked after a few minutes of
silence.  

I shrugged, getting another groan from the jostled minion.  “There’s a
few that are stable but will die without surgery we can’t provide.  My
blood manipulation as well as Hemorrhagia’s is surprisingly effective at
battlefield triage.  Speaking of, Alice will need a bullet wound
patched.  Her power has it covered for now, but it won’t hold forever.” 

“Good, because I want to deal with what comes next /before / I have to
be careful with our guys,” Amelia grumbled.  “I don’t exactly trust
myself right now and don’t want to risk it.” 

“That’s fair,” Chrissie said.  “I don’t exactly trust myself with them
either.” 

A flicker of light and I barely caught sight of the translucent
forcefield slicing the minion’s ear.  Petty, but I wasn’t about to call
her on it unless she took it a step too far.  As far as I was concerned
he was a dead man walking just like his boss.

We stepped into the light of the sun to the resounding cheers of the
Teeth, weapons raised in victory and celebration of our victory.  It was
a pity I couldn’t indulge them in the moment, what with my cargo, or
with Lisa currently hopping out of a jeep and running over to us. 
Chrissie saw the coming disaster and was quick to set Amelia back on her
feet before the blonde missile could crash into them. 

Amelia caught her and seemed to squeeze for dear life.  Lisa may as well
be a Brute, yet Amelia didn’t seem to mind the hug she was enduring. 
Victoria had dropped close, but was clearly willing to wait for the two
to finish their moment before she tried to have her own.

“You did it,” Victoria said softly, floating closer as she did.  “I… 
Thank you.” 

“Amelia is Teeth,” I said.  “We look after our own, no matter what
stands in our way.” 

Victoria snorted.  “Whatever you have to tell yourself to keep up
appearances, softy.” 

“I will eat you,” I said with a laugh. 

“I think there’s a few girls that might get upset about that,” Victoria
said, gesturing towards the three girls that were technically all dating
me?  At least that was the impression I had gotten from the conversation
with Lisa earlier in the morning.  “I’m content with my own handful,
thank you.” 

Rolling my eyes, I gave Victoria a gentle nudge.  “You’re all right
Dallon.  If you ever need anything, just ask.  We’ll be there just as
you were there for us.” 

“Please don’t,” Victoria said with a slight grimace.  “I don’t know if I
could handle your brand of justice on a regular basis.” 

I rubbed the back of my head, grimacing at how my braid had come undone
in the chaos of battle.  “Well, if you ever figure out what brand of
justice you’re interested in, run it by us, I’ll get Lisa on it, if
nothing else.” 

/“Delegation is one of the most important parts of leadership,” / Chisel
said with an approving nod.  /“But not the only mark.”  /

/“Knowing when to delegate and when to get your own hands dirty is an
art unto itself,” / Ironsides confirmed.

Victoria perked up when Lisa pulled away from the group hug, as did
Chrissie.  “I’ll keep that in mind.” 

I didn’t comment on the tears trailing down Lisa’s cheeks as Victoria
drifted over, Amelia wasting little time pulling her sister into another
crushing hug filled with tears.  Whatever circumstances might have
brought the two together, they were still sisters despite everything. 

I tried to ignore the pang in my chest and how I had lost something oh
so similar.  I hadn’t kept up with Emma’s situation, only knowing that
she was in a facility a few miles outside of Boston proper.  I knew Lisa
was keeping tabs on her and would let me know if something concerning
cropped up.

Robbie hopped off the jeep, pulling a bound and gagged Bastard Son to
the dirt with him.  Animos stood nearby, ready to blunt his power if
needed, but the man wasn’t even conscious.  I pointedly did not react as
I was joined by the living legend who let the meat drop to the ground
beside us.  “Today was a victory worthy of the Butcher.” 

“It was a victory worthy of the Teeth,” I answered, finally turning to
face him.  “How many casualties?” 

“Eleven dead,” he said.  “Dumbasses one and all that ignored your orders.” 

I’d seen each of them die through my swarm, one caught by a stray bullet
through the eye, the other had a wall collapse on him from a stray shot
that went wide while Animos tried to herd an Elite Blaster back to where
Vex could bring him down.  Others still ran into capes or just stray
bullets. 

“We’ll honor them as we always do,” I said softly.

Grunting, Robbie continued to watch the Teeth celebrate the victory as
well as those that were performing their after action duties as we
prepared to withdraw.  “You know what has to happen next.”

“That will be up to Amelia,” I said, and tossed the minion to the ground
to join his bound boss.  “She gets first rights to his head for what he
orchestrated.” 

Having turned to where the man had fallen to the ground, Amelia let out
a heavy sigh and squared her shoulders.  She glowered down at Bastard
Son for a moment as a hush fell over the assembled Teeth.  After a
moment, Amelia reached down and touched exposed skin much to my alarm. 

“Relax, I just severed the connection to his power,” she said. 

The man jerked awake, though he quickly fell still once more, though his
eyes were open and darting around with bloodshot desperation.  This was
the man that had organized the Elite against my people, and I had just
one question for him before I allowed Amelia to have her way with him. 

“I only have one question,” I said, kneeling beside the paralyzed man. 
“Was the decision to target my father yours, or the Elite at large?” 

The man’s jaw remained locked even as his eyes flicked between
everything but me. 

“It was his call,” Lisa said, her eyes tight as she watched him
intently.  “How much support he had…  More than he wants to admit, but
not enough to get more boots on the ground ahead of the battle.” 

Given he had over thirty capes, that was saying something.

“Not true,” Longsword said.  “All we were told was to—” 

A gunshot rang out, and I blinked in surprise that it came from Lisa. 
She’d shot the other survivor of Amelia’s escape square in the head,
splattering brain matter across the grounds. 

“I am in no mood to suffer the ramblings of fools that don’t know
anything of value,” Lisa said with a sigh as she sighted the gun upon
Bastard Son.  “Now, answer the nice Butcher’s question before we stop
asking politely.” 

“I ain’t saying shit to some half-rate Thinke—” 

Another retort of gunfire, and Bastard Son cried out, unable to clutch
at the new hole she had introduced to the man’s intestinal tract.  I
knew there would need to be some conversations about this, especially
with it being her first act of murder and torture for the Teeth, but
that could happen behind closed doors.  

Lisa made a show of checking the bullets still in her revolver, then
locked it back in and grinned viciously.  “I can keep this up all day,
though it isn’t hard to see why some of the Teeth enjoy this sort of
thing.  It is rather cathartic, I must admit.  Though, I am surprised
that you actually /wanted / to inherit.” 

That revelation was like a bucket of ice poured down the back of my
costume. 

“Why in the ever loving fuck would you even think about inheriting?” I
demanded, stomping forward.  “Do you have any idea what it’s like?” 

“Lots of cool powers,” the idiot said. 

“And hundreds of years worth of memories,” I snarled, then hit the
little shit with a pain blast that he now lacked any protection
against.  “You don’t keep yourself through that, no matter how hard you
might struggle.” 

I’d figured that out the hard way, that no matter how much I tried, I
wasn’t the same Taylor Hebert anymore.  There were several points where
the girl I once was had died, but none were so poignant as that pivotal
moment.  She died alongside my mom, she died when Emma pushed me away,
she died when I triggered, she died when I inherited.  And she died when
the heroes tried to shove me in the Birdcage. 

“All that is left of me,” I continued, “is the Butcher.  That is my life
now, and I can promise you.  If you had managed to kill me, I’d make it
my eternal mission to drive you insane just long enough for one of mine
to slaughter you.” 

/“Hypocrite,” / Quarrel muttered. 

There was no promise that my power would allow the next in line to
control us like I could control the collective.  However, something we
had all learned since I took over was the power of cooperation.  A
Butcher that worked together was far more effective than the incoherent
screaming that had been a staple of my predecessors lives.

“You won’t get me to talk,” Bastard Son spat,  blood flecking his saliva
as he wheezed heavily from the gut wound.  “You may as well just kill me
and get it done.  That’s what you Teeth do, kill and destroy, but never
build and create, so rip out my skull, drink my blood, and get this shit
done already!”

“How shortsighted of you,” Lisa said, her voice cold as she lowered her
gun.  “You see, I may just be a lowly Thinker, but I’m not the one
that’s going to make you talk.” 

Before the man could react, a finger touched his forehead.

“I am,” Amelia said.

    Chapter 49: Interlude: 4.Chrissie

Chapter by Pendragoon <https://archiveofourown.org/users/Pendragoon/
pseuds/Pendragoon>

Chapter Notes

See the end of the chapter for notes <#endnotes49>

/Tuesday May 10th, 2011 /

Watching Amelia twist Bastard Son into her willing stooge was more than
a little uncomfortable, and just a little hot, Chrissie had to admit. 
Sure, she wouldn’t be asking for that sort of subversion anytime soon,
she might have liked Amelia more than a little, but the level of trust
wasn’t there yet.  Even as a shiver ran down her spine, Chrissie was
forced to acknowledge that there was some appeal there.  Then again, it
had been a /long / fucking day and she wanted nothing more than to crash
for at least the next twelve hours. 

That would have to wait until after the show, because there was no way
in hell she was going to miss Pandemic showing everyone just what she
could do to a person when she wasn’t following her prissy little rules. 
Lisa was already a good example of how she could turn a desk jockey
Thinker into a bad ass mother fucker in the ring.  Now she could show
off how she could turn the human body into a funhouse mirror.

This event was proving to be every bit as much of Pandemic’s reveal as
her little Eldritch Girl transformation from the night before.  Cthulhu
could suck it for how horrifying it was watching Taylor’s swarm melt
into that sleek costume.  Chrissie still got shivers from thinking about
it.  She hadn’t admitted it to anyone outside of the privacy of the
bedroom, but there were more than a few fun things that could be done
with bugs. 

A sharp elbow pulled her out of those fantasies and she was now glaring
at Lisa, whose eyes hadn’t once left Amelia or their prey. 

“Stop perving over power play,” Lisa said, her voice barely a whisper. 
“This is important, and it’s bad enough trying to read things without
picking up your bedroom habits on top of it.” 

Smirking, Chrissie gave her best sultry tone to the attractive blonde. 
“What, a girl can’t appreciate an artist at work?”

Lisa rolled her eyes, then frowned as Amelia finally took a deep breath,
her hand never once leaving Bastard Son’s forehead.  “Alright, time to
see if that worked.  Bastard Son, what’s your real name?” 

Rather than the struggle she expected, Bastard Son’s face remained
completely blank.  “Marvin Milstrud.” 

Chrissie snorted, and had to cover her mouth to hide the infectious
giggles now spilling out of her mouth.  Horrifying implications aside,
it was no wonder the man had picked something as edgy as /Bastard Son /
if that was his actual fucking name. 

Amelia glared at Chrissie and she fought back her mirth, schooling her
expression rather poorly if the slip of Taylor’s stoic mask was any
indication.

“Explain to me,” Taylor began, her voice set in that deathly calm that
always sent chills down Chrissie’s spine.  It was that same tone she’d
leveled upon her when Chrissie had attempted death by Butcher during her
debut with the Teeth.  “In what world did it seem like a good idea to
kidnap Amelia.  Who had the bright idea to grab a member of the Teeth
like that?” 

This time there was some resistance, but Amelia just squinted, and it
fell away a moment later.  

“The board determined that Brockton Bay would be a profitable venture,
but none were willing to risk the inheritance.  I volunteered, thinking
the Teeth’s reputation to be inflated.” 

Taylor snorted, her lips twitching in that characteristic way that
indicated the Butcher was conversing with their headmates.  It was a
habit Taylor fell into in short order after owning her identity as the
Butcher, one that both Quarrel and Damascian shared.  While it made them
appear manic, Chrissie couldn’t help but think that Taylor somehow made
it look cute.

“After the first exchange, I knew better,” /Marvin / continued.  “I
worked with others to evaluate my options, and it became clear that
certain objectives were moving out of reach.” 

Chrissie bristled at how his eyes turned to look vacantly at Amelia when
he said that, and apparently Amelia was having none of it either.  His
flesh bristled and bubbled, bones cracked, and his form began to almost
melt into a puddle.  It was Teeth as fuck and Chrissie couldn’t help but
watch with rapt attention as Amelia unmade the man.

It was with a snarl that Amelia grabbed hold of the mass of flesh
Bastard Son had been reduced to.  “Was I one of these /objectives /?” 

“You were.”  The voice burbling up out of the flesh puddle was barely
recognizable.  “Agnes wanted you brought on, and the rest of the board
signed off on any and all methods just this morning.  I arranged for
Canary to be brought to Nashville so that she could adjust your
loyalties to favor the Elite without muting your own mind as my own
ability would.” 

“Is it bad I want to send Imp to shank them?” Taylor asked, her voice flat. 

Right, the little Stranger could evade Master effects while her own was
active.  Aisha was the perfect assassin, but the twerp was /barely /
fourteen and only just joined the Teeth.  Maybe after a few more months
with Big Robbie in the pits learning to scrap, and a few more kills
under her belt that nobody ever manages to link to her. 

Pity the Empire was dead and done, they would have made good practice. 

Well, there were two former Empire members in the city, but one was
twelve and the other was fucking Purity with a new coat of paint. 
Neither were worth the risk, be it publicity or the ability to level a
city block in minutes.  Besides, Tay had dibs on Kaiser’s old glow in
the dark fleshlight and it was about to be open season.

“Does the Elite often resort to mind control?” Lisa asked, fury in her
eyes.  Chrissie stopped listening as the interrogation turned to names
and dates, letting the blonde to the Thinking while her girlfriend
literally made Bastard Son more pliable.  Even if Amelia hadn’t turned
the man’s brain into literal mush, Chrissie was certain that few could
hold out while the flesh sculptor went to work on their body.

It was… distracting.  And fascinating.

Meanwhile, the rest of the Teeth were wrapping up, and most had claimed
their trophies.  Hell, Tay had seen fit to grab all of their kills and
directed some of the troops to bring the remains to them.  Taking the
bodies would be too much of a risk, but Chrissie was already eyeing her
own cape kills and wondering how best to add them to her costume. 

“Think there’s any decent Nazi tats in this mess?” 

“Probably,” Taylor said.  “A lot of their grunts seemed to be sourced
from some of the Empire supporters scattered across the midwest and
south.  Reaver called in a Herren clan patch on one of the paramilitary
groups he steamrolled.” 

“Fingers crossed then,” Chrissie said.  

She’d been wanting to try her hand at some proper leatherworking, and a
Nazi pelt would make for some fun pieces.  It wasn’t like she didn’t
already have a few of those framed.  Hell, she’d been careful to carve
off one of Stormtiger’s even as she reduced the bulk of his fleshy form
into paste. 

“Wrap it up, the Protectorate is starting to get curious,” Taylor
suddenly called out. 

Following her eyes, she could just barely pick up the glowing form set
against the clouding sky.  It was always fun when the targets served
themselves up, but the idea of the glowstick of doom floating that close
to their entire group didn’t sit well. 

“Victoria,” Taylor said, eyes still locked on the distant figure. 
“Think you can run interference?” 

“Against a rebranded Nazi?” Victoria asked, her sour expression slowly
softening.  “Yeah, I think I can manage that, but I’m not going to fight
her, even if she’s just faking being a hero to avoid becoming bug food.” 

Taylor nodded.  “I know.  You’re here for Amelia, and nothing more, but
I still appreciate the assistance you provided.” 

The blonde bruiser waved the Butcher off casually.  “Yeah, yeah.  Lets
see if Purity learned to fake being a hero enough to avoid getting
punched like she so richly deserves.” 

Not wanting to leave /that / comment alone, Chrissie had to have the
last word.  “With an attitude like that, you’d fit right in with us.” 

Victoria turned, and her aura washed over everyone present.  More than a
few of their grunts made some space, a scarce few even brought their
weapons up, but Chrissie was made of sterner stuff, and just grinned,
gritting her teeth to hide how she was starting to tremble from the
pressure of fear coming from Alexandria junior. 

“Not bad, Dawson,” Victoria said, “but if you ever offer me a place in
the Teeth again, I’ll earn it by taking you into the pits.” 

Not waiting for a retort, Victoria shot off towards the looming Blaster
and Chrissie’s legs would have given out on her if not for Taylor’s
extended arm. 

“Please don’t antagonize my sister,” Amelia said, biting her lip.  “I
really wouldn’t want to put the both of you back together if it did come
to blows.” 

Chrissie grimaced at the idea of what the two might look like if they
did manage to land blows with one another and agreed with Amelia’s
assessment.  There was a reason she was ready to suggest miss collateral
damage be named Splat if she ever actually joined the Teeth.  Those
stories about thrown dumpsters were legendary among those who made the
streets their home. 

“Alright, I think I have enough,” Lisa said with a grimace.  “Can you
put him back how he was?”  Amelia stood stock still for a moment, then
Lisa laid a gentle hand on her shoulder.  “He doesn’t need to be
physically normal, but I would like his mind intact for the next part. 
I want him to feel the dread of knowing what you did to him and what is
to come.” 

Amelia grunted, her brow furrowing in concentration as she worked and
soon enough focus returned to Bastard Son’s eyes.  He blinked, then
squirmed and his pupils dilated almost comically when he realized his
new shape was anything but human.

“The hell did you do?” he asked with a tremor to his voice. 

A broken man — that was all that remained, and he seemed to have
realized that there was nothing that would save him now.  There was
resignation and acceptance in his tone, as well as a question that
Chrissie knew all too well from the people she had put in similar
positions.  

How much would he suffer before meeting his end?

It was always intoxicating to inflict that upon a monster, and watching
Bastard Son break was going down as one of her better memories already. 
She couldn’t wait to get Amelia back to the Arena for the coming party,
or the inevitable after party.  Just thinking about what the tentacles
of her costume could do… 

A shiver raced through her spine as the man screamed, his form trembling
as Amelia inflicted her power upon him.  The last surviving minion
seemed to finally stir at the sound of his Master’s suffering, but
without whatever weapon he happened to specialize in, he would be useless. 

Chrissie had killed two such minions during the fighting, she had the
yoyo and boat paddle to prove it.

“How can you do this to such a great man?” the minion demanded,
thrashing against his bonds.  “Can’t you all see how wrong this is?” 

“Of course” Lisa said, then pulled a gun and fired once, splattering his
brains across the ground.  “This way nobody else will ever suffer at his
hands again.” 

Amelia jerked slightly at that, but continued with her own work on the
bastard that threatened to rob her of her free will.  Ever so slowly,
Amelia pulled Marvin’s skull from his flesh, leaving the brain behind as
she did.  How the hell she managed to preserve it was something that
Chrissie didn’t want to look too deeply into.

“Vicious,” Chrissie muttered in approval.  

Taylor nodded beside her.  “The collective is singing their praises
right now.” 

No shit they were, because Lisa and Amelia had stepped up in a big way
and Chrissie couldn’t wait to give them a proper Teeth welcome now that
they were both blooded.

There would be one hell of a party tonight, and Chrissie was fully aware
that none of them would make it to school tomorrow.  Taylor /might / be
able to make it, but without all her friends, she would probably blow it
off with them and just chill.  Amelia would need cuddles, not to mention
distractions, given everything that happened.

A day of hedonism and debauchery would be exactly what the grumpy medic
ordered.

Well, that and a bunch of shitposting online, because that was oddly
cathartic.  Seriously, PHO was such a weird site for allowing villains
to post openly, and it had strict guidelines for getting verified. 
Other sites had tried to do what they did, but struggled with
maintaining verification of cape status, or in one case, was implicated
in a Gesellschaft kidnapping through IP tracking. 

Naturally Chrissie had taken note of all that shit, because like hell
she would post to a site that helped the Nazis.  Dragon herself backed
PHO with a promise of Truce-like terms for those who adhered to the
rules of the site and it exploded from there.  Hence Hookwolf having the
handle of Murderblender, a name that she was /still / trying to get them
to release to her. 

Maybe she should take up Alice on developing Vex brand salsa after all. 
Get your salsa from New York City?  Try getting it from Brockton Bay!  

/*Some Nazi chunks may not be fully processed.   /

Chrissie laughed at her own joke, and when Taylor raised an eyebrow she

Lisa snorted and Chrissie could only beam at the fact the Thinker got

Granted, most were about murder or eating people, and that was an

Taylor’s head turned skyward and Chrissie couldn’t help but follow her

“Should we do something about that?” Taylor asked, gesturing skyward.

The human leather shifted in color until it finally settled into a

Plus, it was sweet and thoughtful of Amelia to do that for Lisa.  Hell,

Regardless of that, Victoria floated down, flanked by the two Pelham

“New Wave,” Amelia said.  Her costume was on full display, complete with

Amelia.” 

Huh, kudos to her for getting Amelia’s name right, but that was still
the bare minimum.  

Amelia seemed to agree if her answering huff was anything to go off of. 
“Just get to the point, I’ve had a fucking /day / already and just want

“Our Alaskan King,” Lisa cut in with forced cheer.  “You know, us

The flat glare from Demolition Dallon was something to behold, though it

Give it another month and she might be the next Ripley.  The Changer

Pity Chrissie swore to kill her if she ever came near Tay ever again. 
The decision hadn’t been immediate, but the more Tay opened up about

Speaking of not taking things well, Laserdream was biting her lip as if

Now to throw a bit of fuel onto that fire. 

“Dallon, keep that up and we’ll need to get you a matching bed,”

Victoria yelped as her family turned to regard her, and Ashley

“As interesting as that is,” Laserdream started.

Shit, Chrissie really needed to learn their actual names.  She’d never

that more often than the fun nicknames.

Laserdream fixed Amelia with a heavy look.  “We were worried about you.” 

While she wasn’t sure how to handle genuine familial concern, the

expected. 

“Oh, you were concerned?” Amelia snapped.  “Where was that concern when
you were shooting lasers at my sister and I as we fled from an Elite

And critical damage!  Both of the laser bitches recoiled at that one,

“Oh, you /fucking / assholes,” Lisa snarled, stalking forward.  “You /
knew /!?” 

Laserdream started to raise her hands, but quickly turned them away when

only just found out!  You see, Carol said—” 

“She made a deal with the PRT,” Lisa said, her eyes suddenly wide. 
“She’s the reason Bastard Son came after Amelia today…” 

Silence fell over the ruined courtyard of the penitentiary, the

stage a kidnapping?  Oh god, Danny was used as a distraction for that
ill advised plan… 

Sure enough, Taylor vanished in a puff of smoke. 

“Is Carol still in the city?” Amelia asked.  Laserdream’s eyes widened

Victoria moved her mouth as if she were going to speak, but Amelia took

“Yeah, Carol’s dead,” Lisa said with a sigh.  “The Elite killed Weaver’s
father earlier today as a distraction for the kidnapping.  Given how she
handled Hookwolf—”  Taylor reappeared in a flash of fire, only now she

“CAROL!” Photon Mom yelled.  Chrissie didn’t hesitate to throw an entire
field of force fields between the New Wave capes and her girlfriends.

despondent form of Taylor, who hadn’t even reacted to the mass of

“You’re not wrong,” Taylor said, her voice flat.  She then tossed the
head towards Amelia, who caught it with an indignant squawk, somehow
maintaining her hold over Victoria as she did.  Above them the sky
darkened as her swarm gathered, casting the entire penitentiary in

wanted was to live my life in peace, and every action I have taken was

live, and even count one of them among my friends now.” 

The form of Ripley actually shivered at the admission. 

“Yet, people cannot seem to understand that, and continue to push the
limits.  This latest attack was beyond the pale, and my father lies

Carol admitted her involvement, and so I did what was necessary.  Do not

“This isn’t over,” Photon Mom snarled. 

Amelia growled, releasing Victoria’s hand only for her sister to drop to

Carol fucked up left, right, and center, all the way back to when she
decided to attack my father and I in our own home.  She stole me, then
treated me like a villain waiting to happen.  Great self-fulfilling
prophecy right there!  Now, she’s partially responsible for another
attack on a villain’s family.  A villain that /also / tried to be a hero

before creating more villains out of the heroes around you.” 

“Mom,” Victoria whimpered, coming to her senses. 

Amelia paused, nearly jerking in place.  She gave Lady Photon one last
glare then returned to her sister’s side, sharing hushed whispers even

Yeah, that was going to be a problem in the very near future.  Hopefully
they wouldn’t need to fight Victoria over killing her mother, but it
would be hard for anyone to deny that she’d invited Weaver’s wrath by
working with such monsters.  Given Taylor had just taken Victoria’s

difference, people rarely reacted rationally to loss.

Taylor took a deep breath, looking away from the distraught Alexandria

Chrissie reached out—slow enough that Taylor had the option to pull back
—and was thankful that her girlfriend let her take her hand with a

and she /really / needed a chance to decompress and process what had
happened and what they had done. 

A cuddle pile in their room was an absolute must.  That, and a big fat
blunt to take the edge off.

/Wednesday May 11th, 2011 /

The Teeth didn’t need an excuse to party, not that the celebrations had
slowed following their crushing victory over the Elite the afternoon
before.  Even now that it was technically her birthday, Chrissie knew
the party raging on wasn’t really for her.  Taylor no doubt remembered,
and there was no way that Lisa didn’t know, but the mood among her…

Shit, did she call it a polycule, or was it too soon for that?

Anyway, Amelia wasn’t taking things well and had retreated to one of her
rooms with Lisa.  While Taylor was putting on a good show for the rest
of the Teeth, Chrissie could recognize how her girlfriend was projecting
herself into the swarm.  It reminded her of that first day when Taylor
came to the Teeth after the heroes tried to send her to the Cage.

Somehow, despite Taylor ending up as the most terrifying Butcher since
Marauder, had also led to her befriending half the heroes in the city. 
Hell, one of those heroes now shared a bed with them.  Granted, Amelia
was a bit of a special case, but Taylor had lured her over to the side
of Nazi skull splitting with promises of friendship, and it fucking worked. 

Even Miss Collateral Damage had been cordial with them… which was
probably going to change after Taylor all but threw Brandish’s severed
head at her aunt’s feet.  Hell, Amelia had stripped Vicky of her bodily
control just to keep her from doing anything rash.  Chrissie did not
envy the talks those two would need to have over that mess.

Chrissie’s attempt to take her mind off of things with a fight had also
only been partially successful.  Sophia was a hell of a fighter, and she
fought just as dirty as the most scarred Teeth veteran.  Beyond that,
the PRT was at least doing one thing right by teaching their Wards CQC,
so Chrissie was only mildly upset when Sophia managed to throw her
across the pit.

Under any other circumstances, she would have had a blast, even losing
handily.  Sophia practically lived in the pits, and had a pointed line
about being black in Brockton and fighting Empire hopefuls since grade
school.  Learning meant fighting better opponents, and that would keep
her alive in the shitstorm that the raid had kicked up.

They would need to fight again, when Chrissie could appreciate the effort.

“Yo, Vex!” 

Chrissie turned, plastering a grin on her face as Michael joined her,
beer in hand.  “Sup dude?  Get any good trophies?” 

“You fucking know it!” he said, returning the smile.  “Got this sick
back tattoo off of one of their melee capes, but that’s not ready for
display yet.”  Chrissie nodded along, knowing just how arduous the
process of preserving a tattoo could be.  “I also scored this kick ass
blade off another slippery bastard.” 

He then whipped out this absolutely bitchin’ serrated blade that looked
so edgy it hurt.  Like, actually hurt. 

“The fuck is that?” Chrissie asked with a wince.  “It’s like just
looking at the damn thing is making it try to cut me.” 

Michael shrugged, returning the blade to his belt.  “Fuck if I know, but
there was no way I wasn’t keeping that.” 

Yeah, Chrissie could absolutely agree with the sentiment.  “Too true,
man.  I got a new Nazi tat, as well as a pair of scissors and a mop
bucket.” 

Michael froze at her random items, then his eyes widened in
comprehension.  “Right, Bastard Son’s minions…  Really, a mop bucket?” 

Chrissie chuckled.  “Yeah, Not as good as the fire extinguisher that
Amelia nabbed, but still up there in the ‘weird’ department if you ask me.” 

“That girl,” Michael said, shaking his head with a grin.  “I wish to
fucking hell I had been sober enough to see her little pronouncement. 
The video was badass as all hell.” 

That it was.  “Eh, you got to see her turn Bastard Son into silly putty,
so that counts for something.” 

“Too bad nobody recorded /that / one.” 

A snort was her answer.  There was a damn good reason Taylor made sure
nobody recorded even a hint at what Amelia could do to a person with a
touch.  If it got out, it would put all their fears about the girl
firmly onto the reality side of things. 

And they couldn’t be having that.  

Thankfully Lisa was on top of the Teeth social media accounts, and
everyone knew that if a single word was spoken of that day outside of
their gang, that person would get some one on one time with the Butcher
and her assortment of powers in the pit. 

People still had vivid memories of Quarrel randomly rotting people’s
faces off for the lulz.  Shit like that stuck around.

“Bitchin’ knife,” Damien said, having wandered over.  “Wanna test it on
a clone?” 

Chrissie cackled as Michael didn’t even hesitate to draw the knife
again, Damien splitting off a clone right on the spot which was promptly
gutted right in front of everyone.  Half the room cheered, even as a
swarm immediately descended upon the eviscerated corpse and began to
strip it clean.  Sure, Taylor knew it would be reduced to mush within
fifteen minutes and practically evaporated within an hour, but that was
beside the point.  It was always metal as fuck when Taylor made a body
disappear. 

Speaking of Taylor, she’d stepped out for a minute, leaving a bug clone
behind to watch over things.  Chrissie wasn’t sure what that was about,
but she didn’t worry too much, Tay would fill her in if it was anything
of importance.  Instead, she joined in with the cheering crowd as a few
others stepped forward to try out their newly pilfered weapons on a few
of Damien’s clones. 

He only did this party trick when drunk, and people knew to take
advantage while they could.  That Damien got a kick out of watching
people die in interesting ways kinda made sense, what with his power
letting him test that infinitely. 

Naturally she joined in, even getting a shot at him with Michaels new
blade of mindfuckery.  It was fun and helped her ignore how Lisa and
Amelia had disappeared soon after getting back to the Arena.  When she
tried to go after, Taylor had simply put a hand on her shoulder and
shook her head. 

The blade bit viciously into Damien’s latest clone, even as the man
laughed at his doppleganger’s death.  The fun part about the blade was
how it almost seemed to eat at the injury, or absorb it?  Eh, Chrissie
wasn’t too hung up on all that, language was more Tay’s thing. 

Speaking of, she still wasn’t around and that was more than a little
concerning.

Hell, even Madison was front and center in the celebrations, even if
they weren’t as enthusiastic as Sophia.  Both had kills and trophies,
which was all the excuse needed to cheer for them and offer up a toast. 
Chrissie was right there with them, grabbing the nearest sealed bottle
and popping it with one of her razor fields.  They were handy for shit
like that. 

Alice was laughing with Robbie over something, now fully healed from the
hit she took.  With the Teeth of old, she would have died, but Taylor
took care of her people, and Amelia made sure everyone was patched up
before vanishing with Lisa.  Probably to their own room.  Amelia had
some stuff to work through given she’d been kidnapped, and Chrissie
could only hope that she would join them later for a proper cuddle. 

After the bucket of water that was Carol’s actions and death, Chrissie
just wasn’t in the mood for anything more.  Downing the rest of her
bottle of whatever, she tossed it over the edge of the lounge and began
the long trek back toward her shared room with Taylor, who was still
sticking to bug clones for her appearances.  Usually the Butcher would
be in the thick of things after such a major battle and victory, yet she
was hidden away. 

Chrissie stumbled into Taylor’s room, more than a little inebriated as
she hit the light.  There were many things she expected, from the sight
of trophies half prepared, to a cuddle pile already in progress.  What
she hadn’t expected to see was Taylor still in her costume, mask
discarded to the side and sitting against the headboard of their new
Alaskan King with a dozen empty bottles of Reserve scattered around her
being quickly pulled away by a swarm of insects.  

Worse were the tears streaking down her face.

Chrissie moved in a blink, nearly stumbling as she did, but Taylor
didn’t shift.  She just stared listlessly into the distance as Chrissie
half fell over her legs.  Okay, being drunk really isn’t the best thing
for attempting to console one’s girlfriend, but Chrissie could only work
with what she had.

So, she held Tay tightly, and that seemed to break the dam and set her
girlfriend to sobbing uncontrollably as she almost crushed Chrissie in
the returned embrace.  Yeah, those were bones cracking, which was going
to be a problem in the morning.  She would need to talk to Amelia about
some enhancements sooner than later if she was going to be subjected to
Brute hugs. 

Actually, given Lisa’s enhancements, that was two of four of their new
little arrangement that could crush the life out of someone.  Well, that
was a project for the future, once everyone had the time they needed to
bounce back from the past twelve hours and the hell they brought with them. 

“He’s gone,” Taylor whispered. 

Chrissie wasn’t sure what she was supposed to do in this situation,
because if someone told her that she’d just lost her parents, she would
probably celebrate by buying their killer a big bottle of the good stuff
before slapping them for depriving her of the kill. 

Unlike her, Taylor actually had a decent relationship with her father,
even if it was strained by the whole distance thing they had before she
inherited and started working to mend that bridge.  Chrissie wouldn’t
pretend to understand what she must be feeling right now, but she would
be there, which she was pretty sure counted for something if those
youtube vids on relationships were worth a damn.

Lisa probably knew she watched them, but she’d done her best to keep it
from Tay.  Her bugs were good, but they struggled with screens and
headphones made it harder to listen in on things.  The same things she
complained about with the Elite’s opsec were how she managed to get
something over her girlfriend. 

It still meant that gift shopping was going to be a bitch when it came
time for her birthday next month, but she would work with Lisa and
probably order online.  

Her bugs were good, but sealed packages were something she struggled with. 

And Chrissie just made herself sad.  If she’d been better about it,
Danny might not be trapped inside a bubble of stopped time.  Chrissie
knew that Lisa was already reaching out to Missy and Lily about making
an attempt to get him out, something about their power synergy, but
Chrissie didn’t need to be a Thinker to know how much of a longshot that
would be.

A gentle knock at the door caused Chrissie to jump slightly, but based
on the slight smirk on Taylor’s face, she’d let her girlfriend’s bit of
levity slide.  She could only assume that Tay had done something to
signal those on the other side, because they let themselves in a moment
later. 

“Hey Amelia,” Chrissie said, turning as she addressed them both, “Lisa.” 

“Sorry about that,” Amelia said quickly, looking more exhausted than
Chrissie could ever remember her being.  That included the stints she
did in the hospitals following some of the Teeth raids over the last
month.  “I needed to make sure Carol’s head didn’t rot away before I
could tend to it further.” 

Oh right, Amelia had kept her adoptive mother’s severed head.  That was
something that Chrissie wasn’t even going to begin to unpack, especially
considering how Amelia somehow had a worse homelife than Chrissie’s
own.  Sure, her parents had been invested during her early years, and
she was a model daughter. 

Then her dad walked in when she was kissing her best friend.  It was her
first kiss, and at the time she still wasn’t sure she was gay.  It was
enough for the man to pack her off to a Haven run conversion camp.  It
didn’t take a Thinker to figure out that it also got donations from
Medhall right up until Chrissie forced it closed with her rather
explosive trigger. 

That was almost three years ago, and she was now one of the most feared
villains on the coast.  She took a great deal of pride in herself for
that title, even if it was only down to a PHO poll where she placed
third behind two of her girlfriends. 

And Amelia had gotten that rating /before / she joined the Teeth.  Let
it be said that her bedside manner was truly to be feared.  

“I’m sure she’ll feel right at home on your bookshelf,” Lisa said,
barely able to repress her snickers.

“You put her in a jar?” Taylor asked. 

Amelia shrugged.  “Seemed the best thing to do with her head.  It’s not
like I can just magic up the rest of her body considering what you did
to it.” 

Taylor winced.  “Not my best moment, but I refuse to apologize.” 

“Nah, she deserved it,” Lisa said.  “Maybe this time the lesson will
stick.” 

“Doubtful,” Amelia muttered darkly. 

Not like she’d get a chance to demonstrate, what with being a severed
head and all.  Which brought to mind a terrible joke that Chrissie just
couldn’t keep herself from giving voice.  She was sure the Collective
would approve, which should give Taylor a laugh if nothing else, and she
might just share some of the better ones with the rest of them. 

“Well, at least she can quit while she’s a head.” 

Amelia groaned almost immediately even as Lisa barked out a laugh. 
Taylor had cracked a smile even as her focus drifted in that telltale
way that told her the collective was all jumping in on something and she
was actually invested in the conversations.  Tay had once compared their
conversations to organized chaos.  Fourteen voices all going at once
would overwhelm most people, but Taylor was the exception.  She could
handle all of it and more, because what was fourteen voices in the face
of a billion insects? 

“Pay up!” Amelia demanded. 

Lisa promptly pulled a twenty out of her pocket and handed it to the
biostriker.

“You bet on who would make the joke first, didn’t you?” Taylor asked
with a smirk. 

Lisa didn’t even seem the slightest bit upset at having lost.  “Sure
did.  I had my money on the collective throwing it out there first.” 

“Technically they did,” Taylor said.  “Marauder got it in before her
body even hit the floor.” 

“I’m not paying you back,” Amelia retorted immediately. 

Lisa slumped.  “Damn, that’s what I get for making the bet without
tapping my power.  I’m sort of running on fumes and Amelia-grade
painkillers right now.” 

“All I did was dull the pain centers around your corona,” Amelia said
with a shrug.  “Technically it’s messing with brains, but I didn’t
actually change anything and the effects will wear off in a few hours.” 

Amelia looked more than a little smug about that, which was proof that
Lisa was a horrible influence on the girl.  The fact that she wasn’t
currently a complete mess after being kidnapped by a group of monsters
intending to Master her on the other hand…  

Maybe Lisa was actually an amazing influence on the poor girl. 

Or Amelia was just as broken as the rest of them. 

Eh, tomato tomahto.

That Lisa only curled closer to the Teeth’s newest terror was further
proof that she deserved to be there.  That wasn’t even mentioning the
cold-blooded execution of that Elite minion.  Sure, she was doing the
guy a favor given how deeply Bastard Son had Mastered him, but it still
took someone with a measure of resolve to just put a cap in a skull. 

There wouldn’t be any further whispers about if either of the two belong
with the Teeth after this, that much was certain.  Lisa and Amelia were
both blooded now, which would silence even their staunchest detractors. 

“Any luck?” Taylor whispered. 

It took Chrissie a moment to realize she had asked Lisa. 

“I sent messages to Lily and Missy to see if they could do anything, and
have a few feelers out there.  Armsmaster and Legend haven’t gotten back
with me, but I did hear from Accord that he would look into some things
that we couldn’t.” 

“Accord?  No shit?” Chrissie asked. 

Lisa shrugged from her place in the cuddle pile.  “Turns out he doesn’t
want a return to the old way of things with the Teeth and recognizes
that helping keep the Butcher’s father from being a permanent fixture on
the waterfront helps him as well.” 

“I’m surprised he didn’t get swept up in the Boston mess,” Taylor said,
stepping around the obvious.  “Then again, he was always a slippery
bastard.” 

“He actually helped the heroes in the end,” Lisa said.  “His plans
managed to contain Bakuda and the Travelers and it looks like they’re
all in PRT custody.” 

Taylor certainly didn’t seem happy about that.  “Let me guess, they’re
going to let Accord go back to being the criminal they know.” 

“Of course they will,” Chrissie said.  “It’s not like Accord kills more
heroes than we do or anything.” 

“No, we just recruit them,” Amelia said with a smirk while fishing out a
blunt.  She lit it up and took a deep hit, letting the smoke trail out
with a contented sigh.  “Fuck that’s the good stuff.” 

Lisa snatched it from her fingers and took her own hit before passing it
over to Taylor.  Let it be known that the Butcher has some fucking
impressive lung capacity.  By the time Chrissie got it, there was maybe
a single puff left on the damn thing.

Not that she was going to complain, that was still more than enough to
get her stoned as hell.  Amelia’s stuff was just that damn good.  The
four lounged on the oversized bed long enough that Chrissie began to
doze off.  It was what they all needed.

So when near silent sobbing broke out, it was rather hard to miss.  The
entire pile shifted to cuddle the source, Taylor stopped trying to hold
it in and finally let it all out with gut wrenching sobs that had
Chrissie ready to find a zombie cape to revive the Elite just so Taylor

“He’s really gone.” 

Chrissie could only hold her tighter, which wasn’t saying much given she
still lacked any of Amelia’s upgrades.  Still, she needed to say

to be there for her girlfriend. 

“Don’t worry, Tay.  You’ll see your dad again soon enough.” 

“That’s the thing Chrissie, I can still see him,” Taylor said, her voice
choking.  “Right now I have an entire swarm dedicated to surveillance. 
If the effect breaks, I want to be there the instant it happens.” 

It was said with a quiet desperation, and Chrissie knew it was a vain
hope, but it was the only thing currently holding her girlfriend
together.  Chrissie wouldn’t take that away from her, not for anything. 
So, she held her tighter, letting the moment drag itself out as Taylor
vented everything she had been holding back since the first shots of the
day were fired.

“Hey, if it helps, I lost my father today too,” Lisa said softly. 

Taylor snorted, sending snot shooting all over her lap.  “Lise, I shot
your father, at /your /direction.  That is hardly the same.” 

“True, but it got a laugh out of you, which is more than his life was
worth,” Lisa said, grinning almost genuinely.

“She also decapitated my adopted mom,” Amelia added.  “Still not sure
how I feel about that, but I’m sure I’ll process it all over the next
few days.” 

Well, let it not be said that the Teeth were healthy, but damn was it
nice to be among others that /got / it.  “Well, as the only one with
shitty parents that are both alive and reachable, I’m feeling left out
here.” 

This time, Taylor choked out a laughing sob, pulling Chrissie into a
hug.  “I’ll think of something.”

/Wednesday May 11th, 2011 /

 

Chrissie stirred, was cocooned in a pleasant warmth in the dark room. 
From what she could feel, a leg was draped over her own, and strong arms
held tight, yet it was clear they weren’t from the same person. 
Blinking, Chrissie’s eyes adjusted to the darkness and the minimal light
coming from a small plug light near the door. 

It wasn’t hard to recognize the arms as Taylor’s, but the legs were a
fair bit softer than her own, and draped in a way that suggested the
person wasn’t just curled up with the rest of them.  Attempting to
shift, a soft groan followed and those strong arms pulled her back down. 

“Shh, let her sleep,” Taylor whispered.

Right, Amelia and Lisa were in bed with them, in a /much / larger bed
than the one that she had shared with Taylor the night before.  Well,
until they relocated to the couch in the lounge following Amelia’s debut
with the Teeth.  The tangle of limbs was nice enough, but it was
becoming increasingly clear that Amelia had opted to drape herself over
the trio like a fluffy teddy bear blanket or some shit. 

Not that she was complaining, but Chrissie did wish she had her—and
there it was—dangling from a mass of spider silk and being carried by a
small swarm of the flying horrors that Amelia had made for Taylor that
day at her home, before Taylor’s identity was blown wide open to the
Protectorate at large. 

Accepting her phone, Chrissie kissed the closest bit of skin she could
reach and unlocked her device.  She considered playing a game for a bit,
but curiosity won out.  The PHO app was opened and she quickly made her
way to the Brockton boards looking for any news relevant to the Teeth.

Huh, so that was why all their closest supporters among the heroes were
out of the city and the PRT managed to sneak a bunch of Nazis into the
city.  Lisa had said something about that, but the memory was hella
fuzzy after all the booze and weed.  The people that might have spoken
up against it were kicking ass over in Boston and showing their locals
how it was fucking done.  On the plus side, it gave them that much more
volume when they warned of the danger of trying to remove the Teeth from
Brockton. 

If the people that ended the second Boston Games in a day said that
removing the Teeth was too much of a risk, then only an absolute dumbass
would argue with them.  On the other hand, that fancy little party the
rich fucks were planning to throw sounded like just the thing that could
benefit from the Teeth’s brand of a fun time.  Chrissie knew better than
to not run it past Taylor, so she sent a text with a link to the thread
to her girlfriend even though she was laying right next to her.  There
was no point in risking waking Amelia after all.

There was another thing that Chrissie could bring up, but after
everything they went through yesterday, it felt a bit selfish to remind
people that it was her birthday.  Sure, her parents stopped caring after
she came out as gay, and the Teeth never gave any shits one way or
another either.  It was just an excuse to get drunk, and someone ripping
a half decent fart often qualified for such a dubious honor. 

No, Chrissie could let it slide this year.  It wasn’t like turning
seventeen was anything special.  She was still technically bound to her
sperm and egg donors for another year legally, so she would just keep to
their usual arrangement and continue attending Winslow.  At least Taylor
had managed to make that a less miserable prospect, and Amelia would be
joining them for the next year as well; even if she was ahead of them in
her studies. 

Finally, Amelia began to stir.  Taylor reached over, pulling her close
and Chrissie joined in the hug, making sure Taylor was as much a part of
it as Amelia.  It was a bit surreal that she was the only one in the new
polycule that hadn’t lost a parent in the last twenty-four hours, a fact
that Lisa hadn’t really elaborated on. 

Maybe Medhall meetings weren’t so boring after all. 

They had to be better than missing out on the revelry from ending the
Elite.  It was no surprise that Taylor hadn’t been in the mood to join
the celebrations; though Lisa did talk her into making a half-hearted
show of bringing them all out for fresh drinks then dragging all of them
back to bed.  That got a round of cheers and kept the rank and file
happy enough.  Of course, nothing happened, all they ended up doing was
smoking some more weed and vegging out all night in a warm pile of snuggles.

“Mornin,” Amelia muttered, rubbing at her eyes.

It was so damn adorable.

Unfortunately Taylor beat Chrissie to the kiss to the forehead, not that
she let it stop her from feathering a second.  Lisa muttered something
incoherently as she extracted herself from Amelia’s grip, only to let
herself flop onto the terror’s lap. 

“Too early,” Lisa whined. 

“It’s after ten,” Taylor said as her swarm airlifted Amelia and Lisa
their phones.  “Take your time getting up, I’ll go grab something for
brunch.” 

“Lots of bacon,” Chrissie said.  “Maintain the illusion of breakfast.” 

“Easy enough,” Taylor said with a dry chuckle.  “I’ll get right on that,
then we can figure out how badly yesterday fucked the dog.” 

Chrissie winced.  “If PHO is any indication, it’s pretty spectacular.” 

“I figured as much.  I’ve been up all night keeping watch on the city. 
The heroes haven’t tried anything and New Wave left my range shortly
after nightfall.  Victoria is at Ashley’s and is currently still
asleep.  I’m fairly certain Ashley slipped her something to help with
that.  She was pretty shaken from what little I spied.” 

“Well, she did watch her mother commit suicide via Butcher,” Lisa said,
but she still squeezed Amelia tightly.  “That’s going to take some time
to process.” 

“Hopefully she doesn’t hold it against me too badly,” Taylor said,
hanging her head.  “I /like / Victoria, and the last thing I wanted to
do was hurt her, especially after she helped us save our sweet little
Amelia.” 

“I am right here,” Amelia grumbled, tucking her face against Lisa’s
shoulder. 

Chrissie laughed, then feeling a bit spontaneous, leaned forward and
kissed her on her frizzy mess of bedhead.  “That you are, and we intend
to keep it that way.” 

As Chrissie and Lisa hugged Amelia, Taylor smiled brightly.  “I’ll be
back with food in about twenty.  Try not to burn down the Arena while
I’m out.” 

“No promises,” Chrissie said cheerfully as Taylor vanished in a puff. 
Sitting there, she silently wondered how long it would take Tay to
notice that she was still wearing her night clothes wherever she ended
up going for food.  It would all come down to if they realized she was
the Butcher and how much of a spine they had as to if they would point
out that Tay wasn’t wearing pants.

Chrissie herself took her time getting out of bed, but she did make sure
that she slipped into some jeans and threw on a sleeveless shirt,
because guns like hers shouldn’t be hidden.  A part of her wanted to get
tattoos representing the capes she killed yesterday, but she also had
several new scars from the fighting that Amelia had healed up for her
just the way she preferred. 

Seriously, who would want healing that didn’t preserve the reminder of
the awesome moment that earned those markings?  Her scars all had a
story, they were badges of fucking honor, and all the Teeth knew she
earned them! 

Just as she was fastening her belt flames burst from behind the steel
screen Taylor kept setup for her teleportation.  The most awesome
Butcher ever stepped out with two overstuffed take-out bags.  Funny
enough, she still wasn’t wearing pants. 

“Nobody gave you any problems?” Amelia asked with a smirk. 

Taylor shrugged, her tank top flexing against her muscles.  “Not
really.  Some might have tried, but I felt like showing off my new
tattoo and that seemed to get the message across.” 

Chrissie grinned as Taylor turned, showing off the rather blatant design
that Amelia had worked into her flesh, all bright crimson and light
gray.  It was beautiful, and made sure everyone knew exactly who stood
before them.  The only problem was that it was only truly visible with a
backless design, of which Tay had worn to bed last night so Amelia could
do her work.  That it helped distract her from everything that happened
was just a convenient bonus and certainly not a nefarious plot organized
by one of the strongest Thinkers on the coast. 

Lisa however giggled and glanced down.  “Nobody gave you any grief over
the lack of pants?” 

Taylor’s head tilted for a moment, then her eyes widened and she looked
down sharply.  “Oh you fucking /assholes /!  That was what you were
snickering about the entire time I was waiting!?” 

“Pity you can’t pain blast the collective,” Chrissie said.  “I’d say

Chrissie certainly didn’t miss getting blasted, though it happened more
under Quarrel than Damascian, and only once under Tay when they were
experimenting with varying the levels in place of other fun implements. 
That hadn’t worked out, sadly.  It was no secret that she enjoyed the
pain, but even the weakest pain blast felt like all of her nerves were
dipped in acid which was more than Taylor was comfortable with when it
came to fun play. 

The bags were tossed on the bed and Taylor hurried over to the dresser

It covered up the tattoo completely, which was part of the point of
putting it somewhere easily concealed.  As much as Taylor was open about

Once dressed, Tay joined them back on the bed where the food had been

“Really going for the gold there,” Chrissie said with a grin. 

Amelia picked up one of the bacon slices and eyed it warily.  “I am
going to have to flush all of our arteries after this…” 

“Can you flush your own?” Taylor asked, having grabbed some toast to

Amelia hung her head for a moment, then shoved the bacon in her mouth

Yikes, that sounded terrifying.  No wonder she was reluctant to really

girlfriend.” 

“Careful now, flattery might get you something unexpected,” Amelia

“I hope it’s hidden venom sacks,” Chrissie said with a manic grin.

Worser—Chrissie really needed to keep skimming that thesaurus—Taylor

“It’s open,” came over the intercom before she could even knock. 

Letting out an irritated huff, Chrissie opened the door and stomped in,
letting her confidence as Vex carry her through the familiar mountain
cabin.  There were a lot of memories here, few of them pleasant.  She
could still remember getting starved for two days after kicking some
board member in the dick when he hit on her, or the time she returned
after breaking out of camp and delivered her ultimatum. 

Stepping into the living room brought those memories rushing back,
though last time her parents had been surprised by her sudden return. 
This time they were sitting there waiting for her, though she caught the
moment that they truly took in her appearance.  It had changed since the
start of the school year when she’d last stopped by.  

The side cut was new, though the color wasn’t.  Red suited her far more
than blonde and thanks to Amelia, it was her natural color.  Last time,
she only had one tattoo, and hid it under long sleeves.  This time, she
was wearing a shirt with the sleeves torn off, leaving all her scars and
tattoos on full display, including the one in honor of her kickass
girlfriend. 

A girlfriend that she got the distinct impression they were aware of if
their blanket terror was any indication.  Internally shrugging, Chrissie
decided to roll with it and stepped over to the open chair and flopped
down, throwing a leg over the armrest and turning her steely gaze upon
them. 

“Why the fuck am I here?” 

No point trying for sophistication or elegance, much as they tried to
instill all of that into her, she just didn’t give two shits about
proper society and ladylike behavior.  The only highlight to those
parties was getting to sneak off and make out with Katherine, and that
ended when they were both caught.  She’d been sent off to that Haven
camp after that, then came the torture, then— 

“You’re seventeen now,” her mother said, a slight hitch to her voice as
she spoke.

“Your point?” Chrissie snarled.  “You didn’t give a shit about my last
birthday, why do you suddenly give a shit about this one?” 

No car, no nothing, just a party for rich assholes and a quick trip to a
fucked up Haven camp for kissing a cute girl.  Goddamn did she want to
just blend them and get it all over with.  That part of her life was
behind her, but just seeing them again was enough to poke her right in
the Trigger Trauma.

“I’ll cut straight to it then,” her father said, getting her to open a
single eye and glare at him.  He then picked up a folder and tossed it
onto the table.  “Read it.” 

Chrissie scoffed, but reached over and collected the document.  Her face
morphing from anger to confusion as she read on.  After a moment, she
looked up, fighting back every emotion fighting to spill forth. 

“What is this?” 

“That, is a legal emancipation,” he said sternly.  “Sign that document,
and you are effectively disowned.  We would have zero legal rights to
you, and you would have no legal rights to any inheritance we might
leave behind.” 

Chrissie stared blankly at them before returning her attention to the
documentation.  It all looked to be exactly as he had described.  A
clean break with no strings attached, the exact thing she had demanded
almost a year ago just after joining the Teeth but was summarily denied
due to how it would look among their circle.

A circle that the Teeth had effectively gutted.   

“Why now?” Chrissie found herself whispering, her attention almost fully
engrossed by the legalese on the papers.

“To be blunt, the only reason we agreed to your little farce was to save
face.  Your girlfriend’s stunt with Anders ended any point in continuing
the act.” 

Chrissie looked up, a creeping suspicion clawing at the back of her
mind.  “Weaver contacted you.” 

“More like burst into existence in our living room,” her mother said
sheepishly.  “She gave us a choice and this is the one that we elected
to take.” 

“What was the other option?” Chrissie asked, though she had a feeling
she already knew. 

“Nothing,” her father said sharply.  “This is the deal.  I suggest you
take it, otherwise you’ll be moving with us to Chicago.” 

Funny, that’s where all the Protectorate peeps kept moving the Nazis
to.  Lisa was going to have a field day with that nugget and it might
just mean a road trip was in order for the Teeth. 

“I know my girlfriend,” Chrissie said, dropping the folder with a huff. 
She let some of her force fields catch the light and looked her mother
dead in the eyes.  “Try again.”

Her mother had always only offered a token resistance to her father. 
She was completely beaten down, with no initiative of her own.  A
perfectly demure wife, just as she had been raised to be.  Pity Chrissie
learned at an early age not to put up with the pathetic excuse that boys
were just being boys and broke Kevin’s jaw when they were seven. 

After several moments of uncomfortable eye contact, her mother’s resolve
either hardened, or broke, Chrissie couldn’t say which. 

“She said one way or another, you wouldn’t have parents by the time you
turned seventeen.” Her mother whispered.

“Bianca!” Father shouted, as he rose to his feet.  He tired to take a
step closer but she had razor blades at his throat before he could move
on her.  He brought his hands up slowly, but Chrissie was done playing. 
“Now Christina…” 

A single nick, drawing the faintest trickle of blood, was all it took to
break the man.  His entire facade crumbled as an aborted and choked sob
broke through his mask.  Chrissie couldn’t help it, she laughed.  Holy
hell did she want to kiss Taylor for setting this all up, and she only
wished she could have seen it all unfold.  

An evil little thought came to mind and she had to fight down further
snickers. 

“So, what I’m understanding is that if I refuse to sign, my girlfriend
will come in here and murder you both?”  Her mother simply closed her
eyes in resignation, but her father was now begging incoherently for
mercy.  She grabbed him by the collar of his designer shirt and pulled
him close with a snarl on her lips and vengeance in her heart.  “Or
maybe I should just do it myself and finally pay you back for shipping
me off to that hell hole.” 

Chrissie took no small measure of delight at the fear she could
practically feel radiating off of him as the color drained as though she
had already slit his throat.  It would be all too easy to run them
through the blender like she had with Stormtiger.  She wanted to do it,
to finally be rid of the fuckers that caused her trigger. 

The only thing that stilled her hand was the thought of Taylor.  She had
set this all up, given them the option to walk away cleanly, and they
accepted.  It was all she ever wanted, but more than that, Taylor had
given Chrissie the choice as well.  They were far enough from the city
that no help would be coming if she did attack them and she could scrub
the scene long before any forensics team arrived.  Taylor had delivered
them into her hands to do as she wished, and positioned herself to be
far enough away that she wouldn’t be watching over Chrissie’s shoulder. 

Taylor trusted her.  

Trusted that whatever choice she made would be the correct one, and she
knew that Taylor wouldn’t question her no matter the outcome.  Chrissie
could feel the tears prickling at the corners of her eyes as she looked
at the signatures of her parents, a singular blank space left for her own. 

The choice was literally in her own hands, along with the pen she had
picked at some point as she stared at the document, wondering which
choice she would end up making.  Her father hadn’t stopped groveling,
and just that alone was such catharsis that she could only let out a
shuddering breath. 

In the end, did it even matter which choice she made?  

She was free.

 

------------------------------------------------------------------------

 

Chrissie would never admit it, but she always felt a bit warmer when she
returned to the arena, it was home after all.  The guards gave her a
curt nod as she stepped through the doors and those meandering near the
entrance all took notice of her arrival. 

Respect was such a simple word, but one didn’t understand what it truly
meant until it was earned from others.  She had earned it, and it felt
amazing to see so many people smile at her arrival, the nods of
approval.  Hell, even some of the kids ran up and shouted her name with
wide grins. 

Because the refuge had become a community.

Taylor had changed what the Teeth were at their core, and the people
loved them.  It was a new feeling, one she relished and never wanted to
give up.  She didn’t have to change how she fought either, nobody cared
that she blended Stormtiger, some even cheered her on for it.

The heroes could suck it, because all of that?  It made everything worth
it. 

She made her way back up towards the lounge and was surprised to find
the door locked.  Damien had to be high as shit if he actually locked
the door behind him for once.  That or Aisha was playing a joke on her,
which would require retribution if that was the case.  

It wasn’t like anyone locked the door when they were fucking.  The
number of times she walked in on Damien or Michael fucking a groupie… 
Just blech.  She should not be aware of what most of her coworkers’
dicks looked like.

The temptation to shred the lock was there, but Taylor might get upset
with her for it, so she took the time to fish her key off her belt and
unlocked the door.  A singular roach scurried over the door frame and
paused.

Chrissie couldn’t help but smile.  “Someone’s getting smacked for this
Tay, just warning you now.” 

The roach fluttered its wings before scurrying off.  

Chrissie chuckled as she swung the door open and blinked at the darkened
space.  Even the arena floor was blanketed in shadow, which was
unusual.  Had they lost power or something?  Maybe Michael and Alec’s
ever growing entertainment center managed to short out the fuses or
something. 

She’d barely made it two steps inside when every light kicked on at
once.  Her force fields sprung up around her out of reflex as she
readied herself for any attack. 

“*SURPRISE!*” 

Chrissie’s panic quickly faded as she saw all of her family assembled,
with Taylor at the front as her swarm held a banner over their heads
that read ‘Happy Birthday!’  Taylor surged forward and wrapped her in a
hug, spinning her around and pressed Chrissie into her collar as she did. 

Chrissie wasn’t crying, and anyone who suggested otherwise was lying
their asses off.

“Happy birthday,” Taylor said softly.  “Did you like my present?” 

She smiled, laughing as she gripped her girlfriend tighter.  “I loved
it, Tay.  Thank you.” 

“Don’t mention it,” Taylor said, pulling back and grinning her wide
smile.  “Remind me to show you the video later, it’s fucking hilarious!” 

“You recorded it?” Chrissie asked. 

“My conversation with them at least,” Taylor said, rubbing the back of
her neck.  “I made sure your visit was private however.” 

“You’re the best,” Chrissie said, hugging her again. 

“Alright, that’s enough mushy shit,” Aisha said, suddenly hanging from
their shoulders.  “Is this a party, or is this a fucking party?” 

“You heard the brat!” Damien shouted.  “Let’s show this city how the
Teeth throw a goddamn party!” 

“Fuck yeah!” Elliot cheered, hauling out a keg from behind the kitchen
counter. 

Chrissie smiled as her family claimed their refreshments or vices of
choice.  The rest of the arena came to life as people swarmed out and
joined in on the continued revelry.  It wasn’t as though the party had
truly stopped since they got back from the battle with the Elite, more
that it ebbed and flowed. 

Down below, two of the Teeth were laughing as they faced off with one
another in a friendly match, well, friendly by Teeth standards.  That
Amelia was whooping and cheering over the side that she would patch up
the winner was decidedly cruel of her and Chrissie found herself
approving of the girl’s steady descent into villainy.  

Michael was giving Alec a Warhammer primer along with Madison and
Charlotte, which was amusing as hell.  Alec apparently didn’t see the
point if the game didn’t play itself like his consoles did.  Michael’s
groan of frustration had her chuckling as Madison took over explaining
something else while Charlotte just shook her head.  

That Rachel was watching both girls fondly did not escape her notice. 

Off to the side Dinah and Aisha were playing some card game together,
laughing and smiling while Big Robbie watched over their little Omen’s
shoulder.  She’d never seen the man so animated as he was dealing with
the little runt.  He’d never had a family and it was rare that people so
young joined the Teeth.  He’d looked over her when she first joined as
well, but never quite like he was with Dinah.  Then again, she was a
fair bit older than Dinah when she turned Skidmark into salsa. 

“Everything alright?” Taylor whispered into her ear as she handed her a
beer. 

“Yeah,” Chrissie said with a smile.  “Everything’s great.” 

“Almost everything,” Taylor said. 

Following her eyes, Chrissie observed a morose Alice working on her
famed Chili.  The last time she’d been working on a batch, Danny had
been there with her.  She’d overheard the comment Alice made about Danny
being good for some fun, but hadn’t considered that it might actually be
a legitimate thing going on between them.

“Did she actually…  You know?” 

Taylor shrugged.  “No idea.  I never got a chance to ask and didn’t want
to know at the time.  Given how sullen she’s acting?” 

Ouch.  Knowing that someone several of her past lives had fucked
senseless had also jumped her dad’s bones had to be a real kick in the
teeth.  Ha!  Too bad she had enough self preservation to keep /that /
zinger to herself, but there was still another that she could drop instead.

“Could be worse,” Chrissie teased.  “Alice could end up as number sixteen.” 

“Do. Not. Jinx. Me,” Taylor said pointedly.  “I already have memories of
what my mom was like in bed and so help me if I end up in the head of
someone who has slept with my father…” 

“Not gonna happen, Tay.” Chrissie whispered.  “I won’t let it happen.” 

“Please don’t make promises like that,” Taylor said softly.  “I don’t
want to end up in your head either.” 

Now that was an opening she couldn’t resist.  Chrissie leaned forward,
her lips ghosting a feather touch against Taylor’s ear as she whispered,
“oh Taylor.  If I wanted you inside me, I’d ask Amelia for a favor.” 

Taylor immediately coughed, pulling away as she choked on nothing.  A
wide grin broke out across Chrissie’s face as the whole thing with Danny
and Alice no longer seemed as important as the idea Chrissie had suggested. 

“Maybe someday,” Taylor said after a long moment, then she looked away
all bashful like.  “I got you something else, though you won’t be able
to wear it until tomorrow.” 

Curiosity won out as Chrissie watched a small swarm shepherd a cardboard
box over to her.  When Chrissie opened it, she couldn’t help but gasp at
the elaborate dress made of spider silk expertly patterned after her Vex
costume.  It was with trembling fingers that she held it up and admired
the complexity of the design.  Clearly she owed Parian a compliment
because it was just perfect. 

“What’s the occasion?” Chrissie asked. 

Taylor’s smile turned vicious.  “Remember that little fundraiser that
the PRT is hosting in Boston?  I figured it might make for a fun date
night if we got all dressed up and crashed it.” 

Chrissie couldn’t help but bark out a laugh.  “Oh Tay, you take me to
the best places.” 

“There’s no place I’d rather be,” Taylor said, snuggling up close. 
“Right by your side.” 

Oh. 

Oh hell. 

She remembered.

Taylor was definitely getting something special tonight.
